content_it:
Il centro allargato di Surcin, alla periferia di Belgrado, è destinato a una profonda trasformazione urbana. È prevista la realizzazione di oltre 500.000 metri quadrati di nuove costruzioni su un’area di circa 63 ettari, portando la superficie lorda complessiva a 659.780 m². Il progetto, attualmente in fase di consultazione pubblica anticipata fino al 2 febbraio, prevede la costruzione di 2.705 appartamenti per circa 7.300 residenti, con un aumento significativo rispetto agli attuali 881 alloggi e 2.378 abitanti.  

Sono inoltre programmati nuovi servizi pubblici: un asilo nido per 270 bambini, un ampliamento della scuola elementare “22. oktobar” con 8 nuove aule (per un totale di 720 alunni), una scuola secondaria di primo grado per 480 studenti e un centro sanitario di circa 1.250 m². Il numero di posti di lavoro previsti salirà da meno di 200 a oltre 4.600.

Il piano, elaborato dall’Istituto Urbanistico di Belgrado per conto dell’Ufficio del Capo Urbanista della Città, punta a innalzare il livello di urbanità della zona, sostituendo le attuali abitazioni unifamiliari con edifici plurifamiliari, regolamentando il traffico, risolvendo la cronica carenza di parcheggi e migliorando l’infrastruttura. Particolare attenzione è riservata allo sviluppo di centri urbani misti, soprattutto lungo via Vojvodjanska e piazza Zoran Djindjic, dove i piani terra degli edifici dovranno ospitare attività commerciali e di servizio. La superficie lorda destinata a tali funzioni passerà da 11.000 a oltre 58.000 m².

Come riportato da ekapija.com, si tratta di un’importante opportunità per le imprese italiane attive nel settore delle costruzioni, delle infrastrutture urbane e dei servizi pubblici, che potrebbero partecipare alle gare per la realizzazione di alloggi, edifici scolastici, strutture sanitarie e centri commerciali.

title_en: Jerinic: Construction work on EXPO facilities to be completed by year-end
title_it: Completamento lavori EXPO entro fine anno
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Siniša Mali/ Instagram) Construction work on facilities intended for the specialized international exhibition EXPO will be completed in the last quarter of this year, said the director of the EXPO 2027 company Danilo Jerinic, adding that the handover of the premises to the participants would begin immediately after that and that they would then begin equipping their premises. Jerinic told TV Prva that all planned deadlines for the works during 2025 had been met, and that the next major international technical meeting with representatives of the participating countries would be held in March 2026, similar to the one from the previous year, which had been attended by 400 delegates from around 150 countries. – At that meeting, we also discussed the procedures necessary to begin work on their pavilions... These countries will largely hire domestic companies or hire domestic labor - from lawyers and accountants to construction companies - to participate in the EXPO – said Jerinic. He also believes that EXPO 2027 will be “the largest global event, at least when it comes to Europe,” and that the organizers must establish a single information portal this year to inform all future participating countries. Expo 2027 doo Beograd EXPO 2027 Danilo Jerinić construction of EXPO facilities Your comment Send
content_it: I lavori di costruzione delle strutture destinate all’Esposizione internazionale specializzata EXPO 2027 saranno ultimati entro l’ultimo trimestre di quest’anno, ha dichiarato Danilo Jerinic, direttore della società EXPO 2027. Subito dopo, inizierà la consegna degli spazi ai Paesi partecipanti, che procederanno quindi all’allestimento dei propri padiglioni. Jerinic ha confermato a TV Prva che tutte le scadenze previste per il 2025 sono state rispettate e ha annunciato che nel marzo 2026 si terrà un nuovo importante incontro tecnico internazionale con i rappresentanti dei Paesi partecipanti, simile a quello dell’anno precedente, cui avevano preso parte 400 delegati da circa 150 nazioni. Durante tali incontri, vengono definiti gli iter necessari per avviare la costruzione dei padiglioni. Secondo Jerinic, molti Paesi si avvarranno di imprese locali, ricorrendo a professionisti e manodopera serba, da legali e commercialisti a imprese edili. L’evento, ha sottolineato, sarà “il più grande appuntamento globale, almeno per quanto riguarda l’Europa”, e quest’anno verrà realizzato un portale informativo unico per supportare i futuri partecipanti. Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’opportunità di fornire servizi e materiali per la costruzione e la gestione di padiglioni nazionali potrà rappresentare un’interessante prospettiva per imprese italiane specializzate in infrastrutture, allestimenti fieristici e servizi professionali.

title_en: How would ADNOC help MOL when it comes to the purchase of NIS and how much does another five percent of ownership mean for Serbia?
title_it: ADNOC, MOL e la quota NIS per la Serbia
content_en: (Photo: Print screen / Google maps) Energy expert Zeljko Markovic, speaking about the “Emirates fund” in the context of negotiations between MOL and Gazpromneft on the purchase of Naftna industrija Srbije, points out that it is possible that the Arab ADNOC will provide some support to the Hungarian oil company. He also explained what it would mean if Serbia had a 34% stake in NIS and how it would affect fuel prices. In the context of negotiations between the Hungarian MOL and NIS, the Arab oil company ADNOC was also mentioned as a potential buyer, but also - a fund from the Emirates. – It is still an enigma (what exactly is the aforementioned fund). We have heard that MOL is talking to ADNOC about support. It could be financial support or a joint agreement. ADNOC is also a minority owner of OMV. There could be other contracts and cooperation – explained the energy expert. Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto said that they had “made fairly rapid progress in negotiations on the sale of the Russian stake.” – We are a little more certain that MOL is seriously negotiating with Gazprom. An agreement has still not been reached, we also heard that from the president, that a document is expected to be issued that defines the main terms and conditions of the future contract that would complete the acquisition. This should be presented to OFAC and then we will move on – he explained to N1. Serbia currently has a 29% ownership in NIS, and Vucic said that we could buy another five percent. This would make Serbia have a 34% stake in NIS. Markovic explains what this would mean. – According to our Companies Act, for some decisions you need a majority in the Parliament. If by buying five percent you would have 34% of the shares, you would have more than one third. If the majority owner decides to sell parts of the company, to change the legal name, to change from a JSC to an LLC, they cannot do so unless they have a two-thirds majority - that is, Serbia’s consent for the decisions – he pointed out. NIS a.d. Novi Sad MOL Gazpromneft NIS ADNOC OFAC Željko Marković Peter Szijjarto purchase of NIS Serbia Hungary oil pipeline construction of Serbia Hungary oil pipeline Janaf Your comment Send
content_it:
L’esperto energetico Željko Marković, intervistato in merito al possibile coinvolgimento del fondo emiratino nelle trattative tra MOL e Gazpromneft per l’acquisto della Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS), ha evidenziato che la compagnia petrolifera araba ADNOC potrebbe fornire sostegno alla società ungherese, sia in forma di supporto finanziario che tramite accordi di cooperazione. ADNOC è già azionista di minoranza di OMV e potrebbe estendere collaborazioni analoghe anche con MOL.

Il ministro degli Esteri ungherese Peter Szijjarto ha dichiarato di aver compiuto “progressi piuttosto rapidi” nei negoziati per la cessione della quota russa in NIS, sebbene l’accordo non sia ancora concluso. È atteso un documento con i termini principali da sottoporre all’ufficio americano OFAC per l’approvazione.

Attualmente, la Serbia detiene il 29% di NIS. Il presidente Vučić ha annunciato l’intenzione di acquistare un’ulteriore quota del 5%, portando la partecipazione nazionale al 34%. Secondo Marković, ciò garantirebbe alla Serbia un diritto di veto su decisioni strategiche, come la vendita di asset, il cambio di denominazione o la trasformazione giuridica della società, in quanto richiederebbero una maggioranza qualificata dei due terzi.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, tale modifica rafforzerebbe significativamente il potere di influenza del governo serbo nella gestione di NIS.

Per le imprese italiane, un maggior controllo statale serbo su NIS potrebbe influenzare le condizioni di accesso al mercato energetico dei Balcani, con potenziali ripercussioni su progetti infrastrutturali e forniture legate al settore oil & gas.

title_en: First four Chinese trains for new city railway arriving this year, remaining ones by end of February next year - In 2026, purchase of 12 sleeping cars and tenders for renovation of regional depots too
title_it: Nuovi treni cinesi per la ferrovia serba
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Dejan Aleksić) The fleet of the railway company Srbijavoz should be significantly modernized and rejuvenated by 2028, because in addition to new passenger trains, the renewal of locomotives and sleeping cars is also planned. One of the first "rejuvenations" should follow this year, during which the delivery of the first four electric trains from China for speeds of up to 120 kilometers per hour is planned for the railway currently being built from Zemun Polje to the National Stadium. The remaining five should be delivered by the end of February next year , Ljubiša Pejicic, acting director of Srbijavoz, pointed out for the latest edition of the magazine Pruga. The commercial contract for nine trains, as he reminded, was concluded in November 2024. - The introduction of these trains into service is expected immediately after the completion of the necessary tests on the tracks, and no later than the start of the EXPO 2027 Specialized Exhibition - he said. The trains will operate on the Belgrade railway network, which starts from the Classification Yard and passes through the stations Rakovica, Belgrade Center, New Belgrade, Zemun Polje, Nikola Tesla Airport and ends at the National Stadium . As Pejicic pointed out, these trains were developed on the "reliable, proven and safe platform of Chinese regional and suburban EMVs, as well as in accordance with the characteristics of the Belgrade city railway". - These are three-part electric motor sets 63.2 m long, with a battery autonomy of 5 km and with 380 seats, of which 90 are for sitting and 290 for standing - said Pejicic. In addition, the procurement of Srbijavoz is also underway, related to the purchase of six multi-system locomotives from a EUROFIMA loan worth EUR 40 million. As Pejicic said, six new locomotives should be delivered and put into service in 2028 . In addition, the news is that Srbijavoz plans to announce a public procurement for 12 sleeping cars this year . The loan agreement and guarantee agreement for financing this procurement were concluded with the EBRD on October 31 last year. The delivery of the new sleeping cars is also planned for 2028 , i.e. by the end of that year. When it comes to the reconstruction of Srbijavoz's regional depots, as Pejicic announced, projects for their modernization are in the final phase, and the announcement of the tender for the execution of works at the depots is scheduled for April and May this year . Srbijavoz a.d. Beograd Srbijavoz ad Beograd Ljubiša Pejičić new trains for Srbijavoz new train engines for Srbijavoz railway from Zemun polje to National Stadium modernization of Srbijavoz depot sleeping cars Your comment Send
content_it: La flotta di Srbijavoz, la società ferroviaria serba, sarà significativamente ammodernata entro il 2028. Già quest’anno arriveranno i primi quattro treni elettrici provenienti dalla Cina, destinati alla nuova linea ferroviaria in costruzione da Zemun Polje allo Stadio Nazionale, con velocità massima di 120 km/h. Gli altri cinque arriveranno entro febbraio 2026, ha dichiarato Ljubiša Pejičić, direttore ad interim di Srbijavoz, secondo quanto riportato da ekapija.com. Il contratto commerciale per i nove treni è stato firmato nel novembre 2024 e il loro esercizio inizierà non appena completati i test, al più tardi all’avvio dell’EXPO 2027. I treni, composti da tre carrozze per una lunghezza di 63,2 metri, offrono 380 posti (90 seduti e 290 in piedi) e dispongono di autonomia a batteria per 5 km. Opereranno sulla rete ferroviaria di Belgrado, che collega lo Scalo di Smistamento, Rakovica, Belgrado Centro, Novi Beograd, Zemun Polje, l’Aeroporto Nikola Tesla e lo Stadio Nazionale. Parallelamente, è in corso l’acquisto di sei locomotive multisistema, finanziate con un prestito EUROFIMA da 40 milioni di euro, che saranno consegnate nel 2028. Sempre nel 2028 è prevista la consegna di 12 nuove carrozze letto, i cui finanziamenti sono assicurati da un accordo con la BERD firmato il 31 ottobre 2024. Inoltre, entro aprile-maggio 2025 sarà indetta la gara per la ristrutturazione dei depositi regionali di Srbijavoz, i cui progetti di ammodernamento sono in fase conclusiva. Questo ampio programma di rinnovamento del trasporto ferroviario serbo potrebbe offrire opportunità alle imprese italiane specializzate in infrastrutture ferroviarie, componentistica e servizi di manutenzione.
sector: Infrastrutture e sovrastrutture per strade ferrate

title_en: Nis Airport breaks cargo traffic record from 2017

This is the highest turnover in Nis so far, considering that the previous best result was 2,537 tons - in 2017. Si tratta del volume più elevato mai raggiunto nella sua storia, superando il precedente record di 2.537 tonnellate stabilito nel 2017, come riportato da ekapija.com. Questa crescita evidenzia un incremento dell’attività logistica e del trasporto aereo nella regione meridionale della Serbia, offrendo potenziali opportunità per operatori italiani nel settore dei trasporti e della logistica interessati a espandere le proprie operazioni nei Balcani.

title_en: From June, Air Serbia to establish direct flights to Alicante
title_it: Air Serbia lancerà voli diretti per Alicante
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Shutterstock/Gansstock) Air Serbia announces the launch of its eighth destination in Spain – Alicante, starting from 1 June 2026. Flights to one of the most popular summer resorts on the Costa Blanca Riviera will be available twice a week, every Monday and Friday, by Airbus A320 family, with the possibility of season extension, the national airline announced. Airfares for this destination will be on sale from today. – This strategic move builds on Air Serbia’s previous success in connecting Belgrade with crucial tourist and business hotspots in Spain – Malaga, Seville, Valencia, Madrid, Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca, and the island of Tenerife. The speed of adapting to the market, proactive response to demand, and continuous improvement of services remain the main advantages that distinguish Air Serbia compared to other airline models in the region – the press release says. The new direct Belgrade-Alicante service is a result of a detailed analysis of the market and performance of comparable routes. – This confirms that Air Serbia remains committed to sustainable growth, increasing the market share, and providing a better choice of destinations to its passengers. We are immensely pleased by the fact that we will be able to offer even easier access to Spanish summer resorts to passengers from Serbia and the region this summer. With this strategic move, the national carrier further boosts its presence on one of the fastest-growing markets in Europe – said Bosko Rupic, GM Commercial and Strategy, Air Serbia. By the way, competing company Wizz Air flies from Belgrade to Alicante three times a week. Air Serbia ad Beograd Air Serbia Boško Rupić Belgrade Alicante air route Your comment Send
content_it:
Air Serbia ha annunciato il lancio del suo ottavo collegamento con la Spagna: da Belgrado ad Alicante, a partire dal 1° giugno 2026. I voli verso una delle località estive più rinomate della Costa Blanca saranno operati due volte a settimana, il lunedì e il venerdì, con aeromobili della famiglia Airbus A320, con possibilità di prolungamento stagionale. Le tariffe saranno disponibili già da oggi.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa nuova tratta si inserisce nella strategia di Air Serbia di collegare Belgrado con importanti destinazioni turistiche e commerciali spagnole, tra cui Malaga, Siviglia, Valencia, Madrid, Barcellona, Palma di Maiorca e Tenerife. L’adattamento rapido al mercato, la risposta proattiva alla domanda e il miglioramento continuo dei servizi rappresentano i principali vantaggi competitivi della compagnia aerea rispetto ad altri modelli nella regione.

Secondo Boško Rupić, General Manager Commercial and Strategy di Air Serbia, il nuovo collegamento è frutto di un’attenta analisi del mercato e delle performance di tratte simili, confermando così l’impegno della compagnia verso una crescita sostenibile, l’espansione della propria quota di mercato e un’offerta sempre più ampia per i passeggeri. Attualmente, la compagnia concorrente Wizz Air opera tre voli settimanali da Belgrado ad Alicante.

Questa espansione offre opportunità alle imprese italiane nei settori del turismo, dei trasporti e dei servizi aeroportuali, in un mercato europeo in rapida crescita.

title_en: Freight traffic on Budapest-Belgrade railway to begin on February 27, passenger traffic a week or two later
title_it: Ferrovia Budapest-Belgrado: traffico merci dal 27 febbraio
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Dejan Aleksić) Freight traffic on the Budapest-Belgrade railway will be established on February 27, RTV Panon reports. As indicated, Hungarian Minister of Construction and Transport Janos Lazar pointed out that most of the freight capacity had already been sold. He emphasized that they wanted to open the aforementioned section to passenger traffic between February 27 and March 15. Hungary guarantees three pairs of departures, and Belgrade the same number. Trains will depart from Budapest every two hours. The Hungarian side will strive to ensure that passport control does not last longer than 30 minutes, it is stated. Let us remind that, as eKapija wrote in the past few days, Hungarian media reported in the first days of January that the works in Hungary had been slowed down by challenges such as the installation and integration of modern security equipment, which is necessary for high-speed trains . In addition, as a member of the EU, the country had to comply with stricter regulations for public procurement and other procedures, which turned out to be more time-consuming than the regulations that apply on the Serbian side, but the opening of the railway to traffic is certainly expected in February. Janos Lazar high speed railway Belgrade Budapest Your comment Send
content_it: Il traffico merci sulla ferrovia Budapest-Belgrado prenderà il via il 27 febbraio, come riportato da RTV Panon. Il ministro ungherese delle Costruzioni e dei Trasporti, János Lázár, ha precisato che la maggior parte della capacità di trasporto merci è già stata venduta. L’apertura al traffico passeggeri è prevista tra il 27 febbraio e il 15 marzo, con tre coppie di treni garantite sia dall’Ungheria che da Belgrado. I treni partiranno da Budapest ogni due ore. Le autorità ungheresi si impegneranno affinché il controllo dei passaporti non superi i 30 minuti. Come riportato da ekapija.com, i lavori in Ungheria avevano subito ritardi a causa dell’installazione di sistemi di sicurezza moderni, necessari per i treni ad alta velocità, e per l’obbligo di rispettare le più rigorose normative UE sugli appalti pubblici. Nonostante ciò, l’entrata in esercizio della linea era comunque attesa per febbraio. L’implementazione di questa importante infrastruttura ferroviaria potrebbe offrire opportunità alle imprese italiane attive nel settore dei trasporti e della logistica, oltre che nella fornitura di tecnologie per la sicurezza ferroviaria.
sector: Infrastrutture e sovrastrutture per strade ferrate

title_en: Wizz Air to launch direct routes from Belgrade to Sardinia and Sicily in March
title_it: Wizz Air lancia voli diretti da Belgrado a Sardegna e Sicilia
content_en: (Photo: Pexels/Joe Ambrogio) Wizz Air announced today that it will launch direct routes from Belgrade to Alghero in Sardinia and Palermo in Sicily in March this year. - We remain committed to expanding our offer of destinations from Belgrade and strengthening Serbia's connections with key tourist destinations in Europe - said Wizz Air Corporate Communications Manager Olivia Harangozo. Wizz Air currently offers 32 routes from Serbia, connecting it to more than 10 countries across Europe. It was highlighted that, from January to December 2025, the airline operated more than 1,000 flights and transported nearly two million passengers with a flight performance rate of 99.8 percent, which is among the highest in the sector. content_it: Wizz Air ha annunciato oggi il lancio di collegamenti diretti da Belgrado ad Alghero, in Sardegna, e a Palermo, in Sicilia, a partire dal mese di marzo. “Restiamo impegnati ad ampliare l’offerta di destinazioni da Belgrado e a rafforzare i collegamenti della Serbia con importanti mete turistiche europee”, ha dichiarato Olivia Harangozo, responsabile della comunicazione aziendale di Wizz Air. Attualmente, la compagnia aerea opera 32 rotte dalla Serbia, con collegamenti verso oltre 10 Paesi europei. Secondo quanto riportato da ekapija.com, tra gennaio e dicembre 2025 Wizz Air ha effettuato più di 1.000 voli, trasportando quasi due milioni di passeggeri, con un tasso di regolarità del 99,8%, tra i più elevati del settore. Questa espansione potrebbe offrire nuove opportunità per le imprese turistiche italiane operanti in Sardegna e Sicilia, grazie a un accesso facilitato dal mercato serbo.

title_en: Air Serbia carries nearly 50,000 passengers in first year of direct flights between Belgrade and Shanghai
title_it: Air Serbia: 50.000 passeggeri su Belgrado-Shanghai
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Shutterstock/Abdul N Quraishi - Abs) The national airline Air Serbia has announced that it has carried nearly 50,000 passengers on the route in one year of direct flights between Belgrade and Shanghai. The company’s CEO, Jiri Marek, assessed that the result “further confirms the strategic importance of the Belgrade-Shanghai route.” – The introduction of direct flights between Belgrade and Shanghai was aimed at connecting Serbia more strongly and efficiently with this important global hub. During the first year of operations on this intercontinental route, we carried almost 50,000 passengers, which clearly shows that we have successfully responded to market needs and justified passenger expectations – Marek said in a statement on the occasion of the first anniversary of the establishment of the airline. He added that direct flights between Belgrade and Shanghai “enable faster exchange of experiences, development of business cooperation, as well as more intensive cultural and tourist contacts between Serbia and China.” Air Serbia operated its first direct flight from Belgrade to Shanghai on January 11 last year, and in addition to that Chinese city, it has also established a direct flight to Guangzhou. Air Serbia ad Beograd Air Serbia Jiri Marek Belgrade Shanghai air route Your comment Send
content_it: La compagnia aerea nazionale serba Air Serbia ha trasportato quasi 50.000 passeggeri in un anno sulla rotta diretta tra Belgrado e Shanghai. Il CEO dell’azienda, Jiri Marek, ha dichiarato che questo risultato “conferma ulteriormente l’importanza strategica della rotta Belgrado-Shanghai”, introdotta per collegare la Serbia in modo più efficiente a questo importante hub globale. “Nei primi dodici mesi di operatività su questa rotta intercontinentale, abbiamo trasportato quasi 50.000 passeggeri, dimostrando di aver risposto con successo alle esigenze del mercato e alle aspettative dei viaggiatori”, ha affermato Marek in occasione del primo anniversario del lancio del collegamento. Il manager ha inoltre evidenziato che i voli diretti favoriscono “uno scambio più rapido di esperienze, lo sviluppo della cooperazione commerciale e contatti culturali e turistici più intensi tra Serbia e Cina”. Air Serbia ha effettuato il primo volo diretto da Belgrado a Shanghai l’11 gennaio dello scorso anno e, oltre a Shanghai, ha attivato anche un collegamento diretto con Guangzhou. Come riportato da ekapija.com, questo potenziamento dei collegamenti aerei con la Cina rappresenta un’opportunità per le imprese italiane interessate a operare nei Balcani e in Asia, grazie a una migliore accessibilità della regione.

title_en: Belgrade Airport completing terminal review to increase efficiency
title_it: Aeroporto di Belgrado ottimizza terminal
content_en: (Photo: Aleksandar Parezanović) Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport has completed a review of its security and terminal operations in a bid to enhance efficiency and prepare for future growth. The airport contracted the UK-based EBEA Consulting, which specialises in airport planning and operations, to conduct a comprehensive operational review of its departing passenger processes throughout 2024 and 2025. The airport required a detailed assessment of the centralised passenger security area following recent terminal expansion, alongside its associated passenger flow management. Furthermore, the airport required strategic recommendations to enhance operational efficiency, improve the passenger experience and prepare for future growth within its development timeline. EBEA developed a comprehensive operational review methodology encompassing passenger security screening, check-in processes and terminal management functions. The approach included detailed site visits, operational shadowing, stakeholder interviews with security management teams, operations personnel and terminal management staff. Extensive data collection and analysis was conducted covering queue time performance, equipment capacity assessment, staffing deployment models, forecast accuracy and system capabilities. Throughout the project, EBEA worked closely with airport operational teams, examining over twenty key operational areas from security lane performance to terminal flow management. Detailed security process optimisation recommendations were made for Belgrade Airport , covering queue management, staffing efficiency, data utilisation and technology enhancement focused on maximising throughput of existing facilities. A strategic recommendations portfolio with initiatives covering infrastructure optimisation, process improvements, staff development and technology integration was also produced. Iain Cochrane, Senior Manager for Optimisation at operator VINCI Airports, noted that EBEA had conducted a very professional, thorough and detailed assessment of the existing landside security and check-in processors, identifying multiple areas for significant operational and service improvement. content_it:
L’Aeroporto di Belgrado Nikola Tesla ha completato una revisione delle operazioni di sicurezza e dei processi del terminal per migliorare l’efficienza e prepararsi alla futura crescita. L’aeroporto ha incaricato la società britannica EBEA Consulting, specializzata in pianificazione e gestione aeroportuale, di condurre una valutazione approfondita dei flussi dei passeggeri in partenza nel biennio 2024-2025. L’analisi si è concentrata in particolare sull’area centralizzata di sicurezza passeggeri, ampliata di recente, e sulla gestione dei flussi associati.  

EBEA ha sviluppato una metodologia completa che ha incluso sopralluoghi, osservazione diretta delle operazioni, colloqui con i responsabili della sicurezza, del personale operativo e della gestione del terminal, nonché un’analisi dettagliata di tempi di attesa, capacità degli impianti, modelli di impiego del personale, accuratezza delle previsioni e prestazioni dei sistemi.  

Sono state formulate raccomandazioni strategiche per ottimizzare la gestione delle code, migliorare l’efficienza del personale, utilizzare meglio i dati e potenziare la tecnologia, al fine di massimizzare la capacità degli impianti esistenti. È stato inoltre elaborato un piano di iniziative riguardanti l’ottimizzazione infrastrutturale, il miglioramento dei processi, lo sviluppo del personale e l’integrazione tecnologica.  

Iain Cochrane, Senior Manager per l’Ottimizzazione di VINCI Airports, ha sottolineato che la valutazione condotta da EBEA è stata “molto professionale, accurata e dettagliata”, individuando numerose opportunità di miglioramento operativo e del servizio.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’iniziativa rientra nel più ampio piano di sviluppo dell’aeroporto. L’ottimizzazione delle infrastrutture e dei processi aeroportuali potrebbe creare opportunità per aziende italiane specializzate in tecnologie per la sicurezza, sistemi di gestione dei flussi passeggeri e soluzioni integrate per la logistica aeroportuale.

title_en: Tender for completion and equipping of Prokop rail station announced
title_it: Gara per il completamento della stazione Prokop
content_en: (Photo: Dejan Aleksić) The Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure has announced an international tender for the execution of works on the arrangement and complete equipping of the interior of the Belgrade Center (Prokop) rail station, as part of the project to modernize the rail sector in Serbia. The tender covers the final phase of the station construction, including a full interior arrangement of the station complex, the construction and equipping of platforms and tracks, the installation of modern technical, security and information systems, as well as the arrangement of access roads and public spaces . The works will be carried out in accordance with FIDIC rules, and the agreed completion deadline is 425 days from the introduction of the contractor to the job . The criterion for awarding the contract is the most economically advantageous tender, with the price carrying 60% of the total number of points. The project is financed by the World Bank and the French Development Agency (AFD), as part of the project to modernize the rail sector in Serbia. Interested bidders can submit their bids by February 23, and more details can be found HERE . I. Z. Nalazi se neposredno uz Bulevar Franš d'Eperea (deo koridora 10), u prokopu između ovog pravca, Bulevara kn. Aleksandra Karađorđevića i Bulevara Vojvode Putnika podno Topčiderskog brda. title_en: Second supercomputer in operation since March – Construction of Data Center in Nis planned to begin in 2026
title_it: Serbia rafforza supercomputer e data center
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Wright Studio/shutterstock.com) Serbia already has one supercomputer that is being provided free of charge to all technical faculties, institutes, science and technology parks and startups. The installation of the second supercomputer is underway and will be put into operation in March 2026, while the third supercomputer will arrive at the end of 2026, announced Mihailo Jovanovic, Director of the Office for IT and eGovernment. – In terms of the power of supercomputers, Serbia will certainly be among the three or four strongest countries in Europe, but a major task remains - the application of artificial intelligence in as many sectors of society as possible. The implementation has already begun, through the intensive introduction of AI assistants, and Serbia was among the first in the region to launch the implementation of AI assistants in public services – Jovanovic told Blic. The role of supercomputers in the 21st century, as Jovanovic says, is becoming increasingly important. – Today, data is more valuable than oil, and once you have a large amount of data, by processing it on supercomputers in a very short period of time and using various algorithms, you can significantly improve many sectors of society. Today, the growth of gross domestic product is also being measured by the strength of a country when it comes to supercomputers. In a way, the sovereignty of a country is also measured by the possession of a supercomputer – he emphasizes. Also, as he added, intensive application of AI assistants has begun in various sectors of society, including the first AI assistants in eGovernment, while in parallel the introduction of AI solutions in the scientific and technological community has been launched. – So, already on the electronic government portal you can talk and communicate with artificial intelligence that helps you use electronic government services more easily. We will raise this on many other sites, including the “Svoj na svome” site that helps citizens register their rights to real estate as easily as possible – he emphasized. Expansion in Belgrade, new Data Center in Nis Next year, it is planned to start expanding the Data Center in Belgrade. This is the first data center, it is much smaller than the one in Kragujevac, but as Jovanovic says, a project to expand the Belgrade data center and build a new one in Nis is already underway. – Namely, we are making a project to build a State Data Center in Nis. Of course, in the 21st century, the need for data centers and such capacities is incredible. Elektroprivreda Srbije must also support us in this construction, because data centers consume a significant amount of electricity, but I am optimistic that next year we will start expanding both the Belgrade data center and the new state data center – said Jovanovic. Kancelarija za informacione tehnologije i elektronsku upravu Beograd Office for IT and eGovernment Mihailo Jovanović State Data Center Kragujevac Data Center Belgrade Data Center Niš supercomputer artificial intelligence Your comment Send
content_it:
La Serbia dispone già di un supercomputer, messo a disposizione gratuitamente di tutte le facoltà tecniche, istituti, parchi scientifici e tecnologici e startup. Nei primi mesi del 2026 entrerà in funzione un secondo supercomputer, mentre un terzo arriverà entro la fine dello stesso anno, ha annunciato Mihailo Jovanović, direttore dell’Ufficio per le Tecnologie Informatiche e l’Amministrazione Digitale.  

Secondo Jovanović, grazie a questa potenza di calcolo, la Serbia si collocherà tra i primi tre o quattro paesi europei in termini di capacità di supercalcolo. L’attenzione si concentra ora sull’applicazione dell’intelligenza artificiale (IA) in quanti più settori possibili. L’implementazione è già iniziata con l’introduzione di assistenti basati su IA nei servizi pubblici, posizionando la Serbia tra i primi paesi della regione in questo ambito.  

Jovanović sottolinea che “oggi i dati valgono più del petrolio” e che, grazie ai supercomputer, è possibile elaborare grandi quantità di informazioni in tempi brevi, migliorando significativamente diversi settori. La forza di un Paese in termini di supercalcolo è ormai un indicatore rilevante anche per la crescita del PIL e per la sovranità digitale.  

Già oggi, sul portale dell’amministrazione digitale è possibile interagire con un assistente virtuale per accedere più facilmente ai servizi pubblici. Questa funzionalità verrà estesa ad altri siti, tra cui “Svoj na svome”, dedicato alla registrazione dei diritti immobiliari.  

Nel 2026 sono inoltre previsti l’ampliamento del Data Center di Belgrado e l’avvio della costruzione di un nuovo Data Center statale a Niš. Il progetto richiederà ingenti forniture di energia elettrica, per cui sarà fondamentale il supporto di Elektroprivreda Srbije. Come riportato da ekapija.com, Jovanović si è detto ottimista sull’avvio dei lavori già il prossimo anno.  

Questo sviluppo infrastrutturale e digitale potrebbe rappresentare opportunità per aziende italiane attive nel settore dei data center, dell’energia e delle soluzioni di intelligenza artificiale.

title_en: Edina Selesković, artist from BiH: Sarajevo taught me empathy, New York courage, and between those two worlds I created my own language without borders
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: (Photo: Uros Abram) Edina Selesković is one of the most prominent contemporary artists from the former Yugoslavia whose work spans sculpture, multimedia, performance and large-scale public installations. Born in Bosnia and Herzegovina, formed between Sarajevo and New York, she started her artistic journey in the early nineties in the United States of America, where she graduated from the renowned Corcoran School of Art in Washington. Since then, her career has included more than a hundred exhibitions around the world and collaborations linking art, science and technology, including a project with NASA. She has won numerous international awards and is a regular member of BHAAAS and the International Academy of Sciences and Arts of Bosnia and Herzegovina. She is the only artist whose work simultaneously belongs to the global scene and remains deeply rooted in the experience she carries from Sarajevo, building a bridge between identity, innovation and social responsibility. In a conversation with eKapija, Edina talks about how living between two worlds shaped her expression, how the audience becomes the author of her works, why censorship and restrictions became crucial for her creative growth, and how art and business intertwine in modern society. Your artistic practice encompasses sculpture, multimedia, performance and public installations. What personal experiences shaped you the most to choose this interdisciplinary approach? - Interdisciplinarity came naturally to me, almost by necessity. I grew up between different worlds - between Bosnia, which shaped me as a person, and New York, which shaped me as an artist. Those two experiences - one deeply emotional and historical, the other radically open and experimental - taught me that art does not have to have boundaries. Sculpture gave me form, performance movement, public space a purpose, and multimedia made it possible to intertwine it all into a unique expression. I think that it was precisely living between different cultures and systems that made me choose plurality, not one form. How do your experiences influence the topics you cover in your works? - My works almost always bear traces of the places I come from and the places I`ve passed through. Sarajevo taught me empathy, layering and resilience - that`s why my themes are often imbued with memory, identity and communities. New York taught me courage, conceptual thinking and the idea that art can be both a tool and a platform. Those two experiences together define my themes: freedom, togetherness, the possibility of change, questioning the system and, perhaps most importantly, the human story behind every great narrative. Projects like Think Freedom or Beating Heart actively involve the audience. What inspires you most about the interaction between art and the viewer? - The moment when the audience becomes the author inspires me the most. When it touches the installation, when it leaves a message, when it recognizes itself in a story that is not only mine - then art crosses the border of the aesthetic and becomes a shared experience. Interaction is not decoration for me; she is the essence. People bring meaning, breath and energy to the work. This is why public spaces and participatory projects are so important to me - they democratize art and make it possible for it to happen everywhere and to everyone. (Photo: Nemanja Micevic) What moment in your career do you consider to be crucial for the transition from the local art scene to the international one? - In my case, the path may have been the opposite of the usual one - first I built my career on the New York and American stage, and only after twenty years of living in America did I return to Bosnia and Herzegovina, where my work only then became present in our area. The key moment was certainly going to the United States in 1991, where I graduated from the Washington Academy and started exhibiting there. Those were my first professional steps, but coming to New York changed everything - suddenly my career started to develop in a direction I never dared to dream about. Williamsburg, the artistic part of New York, was then emerging - raw, energetic, incredibly open to new ideas - and it was in that environment that I first felt the true freedom and global reach of art. Returning to Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2011 opened a new chapter in my life and career, when I no longer had the luxury of independent existence in the world of art, but the responsibility to try to become an initiator of positive changes. How do you balance creative freedom with the requirements of commissioned or public projects? - Balance is always a challenge, but I believe that commissioned projects do not have to limit creativity. On the contrary - limitations sometimes become a springboard. It is important for me to understand the essence of the order, but also to keep an authentic voice. When there is mutual trust, the project becomes a collaboration rather than a compromise. In public installations, I feel a special responsibility because the work must communicate with an audience that did not ask for it, but will meet it every day - therefore it must be clear, empathetic and honest. You might not believe me, but the biggest step forward and personal growth in my career happened precisely because of censorship. She taught me that sometimes limitation is what pushes you into deeper authenticity, into bolder expression, and into creation that can`t be easily silenced. In that paradox, I discovered my own strength and the importance that art always remains honest, even when its doors are closed. Do you think art and business have a common thread that connects them? How can those two spheres complement each other? - Art and business have much more in common than it seems at first glance. Both require vision, courage, the ability to take risks and faith in an idea that does not yet exist. In modern society, especially in culture, sustainability has become necessary - and that`s where art and business meet. Business can provide infrastructure and resources, and art can provide meaning, identity and value that cannot be measured in numbers. When these two spheres come together in the right way, projects that change communities are created - Planet Sarajevo is one of them. My experience as a lecturer at the IEDC Bled business school, on the Art & Leadership program, further confirmed to me that artists and leaders can learn a great deal from each other. Art opens up space for intuition, imagination and empathy, while leadership brings structure, strategy and accountability. When these two perspectives meet, it is not just a better manager or a better artist - but a completely new way of thinking about the world and the change we can create. Planet Sarajevo (Photo: SQ QUANTUM GROWTH AGENCY) Is there a work or installation that is particularly meaningful to you personally and why? - Think Freedom carries a special emotional weight, because it contains thousands of messages from young people from all over the world about what freedom is. It`s not just a work of art; it is an ongoing global dialogue. Every place where the installation was exhibited brought a new story and a new emotion. It`s a project that`s been traveling for a decade now, it`s left a mark on many communities - and on me. It taught me that art can be a beacon, but only if people participate in it. You participated in the Planet Sarajevo project, which was declared the best tourism product of the year at the Tourism Expo Sarajevo 2025. Can you tell us a little more about the project itself and what its importance is? - Planet Sarajevo is a specific project full of challenges and emotions - a multimedia museum that combines archives, art, VR, AI, performative design and documentary material into one complete story about a city that has shaped generations. The award for the best tourist product of the year, as well as awards for cultural innovation by Poslovni novina and two golden No Limit awards in a short period, confirm that Sarajevo is not only a destination for the past, but also for innovation. Planet Sarajevo shows how the city can be told in a contemporary, emotional and relevant way. It is a space that connects culture, education and tourism - and that`s why its importance goes beyond the classical museum. It becomes a platform, meeting place and bridge between generations. (Photo: Almin Zrno) Does art work for you more as a means of personal expression or a tool for social and cultural change? - For me, art is always bidirectional. It starts from the intimate - from the questions we carry inside - but it gets its full meaning only when it goes out into the public space and touches others. I don`t believe in art that remains only personal or in that which is only socially useful. It must be true, emotional and courageous. If it achieves this, then it can change both the artist and society. (Photo: Almin Zrno) What`s the biggest lesson you`ve learned from working on international projects and collaborating with different artists? - The biggest lesson is that creativity is born from encounters. When you work with people from different cultures, you realize that art has a universal language, but also that each community colors it with shades of its own history and emotions. I learned that the key is to be open - to the process, to mistakes, to unexpected ideas. International projects have taught me patience, cooperation and deep humility in the face of the fact that art is never finished. It is my vocation, but more than that - it is my mission. title_en: Post of Serbia, Roads of Serbia and several other public enterprises officially transforming into limited liability companies
title_it: Trasformazione di enti pubblici in SRL
content_en: Main Post Office Belgrade (Photo: Belgrade_City/Pixabay) The Post of Serbia and several other public enterprises are officially transforming into limited liability companies. The Serbian Government has made decisions to change the legal form of several, so far, public enterprises and their transition to the limited liability company form. As can be seen in the latest edition of the Official Gazette, in addition to the Post of Serbia, this change also applies to the Roads of Serbia, Srbijavode, the Textbook Institute, the Public Enterprise for Shelters and the Public Enterprise for Broadcasting Equipment and Connections. These companies will, as planned, continue to perform the activities of public enterprises, i.e. as before the change in legal form. The assets and liabilities of these companies will remain the same, court and other proceedings will continue, and previously signed contracts will remain in force, it is emphasized in the decisions on changes in the legal form of these companies. When it comes to the capital assets of the previous public companies, they will be converted into shares in a limited liability company. content_it: Il governo serbo ha deciso di trasformare diverse aziende pubbliche in società a responsabilità limitata (SRL). Secondo quanto pubblicato nella Gazzetta Ufficiale, tra gli enti interessati figurano Poste della Serbia, Strade della Serbia, Srbijavode, l’Istituto per i Libri di Testo, l’Azienda Pubblica per i Rifugi e l’Azienda Pubblica per le Apparecchiature e i Collegamenti Radiotelevisivi. Come riportato da ekapija.com, le imprese continueranno a svolgere le medesime attività di pubblico interesse anche dopo la modifica della forma giuridica. Patrimoni, passivi, procedimenti giudiziari e contratti già sottoscritti resteranno invariati. Il capitale degli enti pubblici sarà convertito in quote sociali delle nuove SRL. Questa riforma rientra nel più ampio processo di trasformazione del settore pubblico in Serbia, con l’obiettivo di modernizzare la gestione e migliorare l’efficienza operativa. Tale evoluzione potrebbe aprire nuove opportunità per le imprese italiane interessate a collaborazioni o partnership in settori strategici come le infrastrutture, le telecomunicazioni e i servizi pubblici.

title_en: Serbia to get largest supercomputer in region by end of 2026
title_it: Serbia avrà il supercomputer più potente della regione
content_en: (Photo: Taylor Vick/Unsplash) Serbia should become the owner of the largest supercomputer cluster in Southeast Europe, intended for the development and application of artificial intelligence, by the end of 2026, or early 2027. This was confirmed at a meeting of the Director of the Office for IT and eGovernment Mihailo Jovanovic with the French Ambassador to Serbia Florence Ferrari and representatives of the French company Bull SAS. As announced, the implementation of the project is entering the final phase of preparation, and the ratification of the intergovernmental agreement between Serbia and France is expected at the spring session of the National Assembly. This would fulfill all formal conditions for the full implementation of the contract worth EUR 50 million. Jovanovic reminded that the commercial preliminary contract for the procurement of the new supercomputer had been signed in April 2025, while the concrete results of the project were expected during 2026. – This system will enable Serbia to have the largest supercomputer cluster in the region by the end of 2026 and the beginning of 2027, which will be intended for the development of solutions based on artificial intelligence and its application in various sectors – said Jovanovic. According to him, EUR 36 million will be invested in the supercomputer itself, along with the accompanying software and Mistral models of generative artificial intelligence, while an additional EUR 14 million is intended for the development of AI projects and services in the areas of healthcare, e-government, energy and transport. The new supercomputer will be based on 640 nVidia GraceHopper superchips, distributed in 160 computer nodes, with a data storage space of 2.5 petabytes. A special space with advanced water cooling systems has already been designed in the State Data Center in Kragujevac, in which the existing and new supercomputers will be connected into a single whole. The French Ambassador Florence Ferrari assessed that artificial intelligence was one of the key areas of cooperation between France and Serbia, emphasizing that the new supercomputer would contribute not only to the development of Serbia, but also to strengthening the overall innovation capacities of the European Union. Bull SAS announced that the company would be responsible for delivering the supercomputer and developing a joint center for artificial intelligence, which would monitor its implementation in practice. Kancelarija za informacione tehnologije i elektronsku upravu Beograd Ambasada Republike Francuske Beograd Bull SAS Florence Ferrari Mihailo Jovanović supercomputer artificial intelligence Your comment Send
content_it:
La Serbia diventerà proprietaria del cluster di supercomputer più grande del Sud-Est Europa, dedicato allo sviluppo e all’applicazione dell’intelligenza artificiale, entro la fine del 2026 o l’inizio del 2027. Lo ha confermato il Direttore dell’Ufficio per l’informatica e l’amministrazione digitale, Mihailo Jovanović, nel corso di un incontro con l’ambasciatrice francese in Serbia, Florence Ferrari, e rappresentanti dell’azienda francese Bull SAS.  

Il progetto è entrato nella fase finale di preparazione e si prevede che l’accordo intergovernativo tra Serbia e Francia venga ratificato durante la sessione primaverile dell’Assemblea nazionale, soddisfacendo così tutte le condizioni formali per l’attuazione del contratto da 50 milioni di euro.  

Jovanović ha ricordato che il contratto preliminare per l’acquisto del supercomputer è stato firmato nell’aprile 2025, con risultati concreti attesi nel corso del 2026. Il sistema, basato su 640 superchip NVIDIA GraceHopper distribuiti in 160 nodi e dotato di 2,5 petabyte di spazio di archiviazione, sarà installato nel Centro dati statale di Kragujevac, già dotato di un’apposita infrastruttura con sistemi avanzati di raffreddamento ad acqua.  

L’investimento di 36 milioni di euro riguarderà il supercomputer, il software associato e i modelli Mistral di intelligenza artificiale generativa, mentre ulteriori 14 milioni saranno destinati allo sviluppo di progetti e servizi basati sull’IA nei settori sanità, e-government, energia e trasporti.  

L’ambasciatrice Ferrari ha sottolineato che l’intelligenza artificiale rappresenta uno dei pilastri della cooperazione tra Francia e Serbia, evidenziando il ruolo del nuovo supercomputer nel rafforzamento delle capacità innovative non solo della Serbia, ma dell’intera Unione Europea. Bull SAS sarà responsabile della fornitura del supercomputer e dello sviluppo di un centro comune per l’intelligenza artificiale.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa infrastruttura strategica potrebbe rappresentare un’opportunità per aziende italiane attive nei settori dell’informatica, dell’ingegneria dei sistemi e dei servizi digitali avanzati.

title_en: Siniša Palić, director of the Satwork company: For 20 years, we have been a reliable technology partner in the digitization of transport
title_it: Satwork: 20 anni nel digitale per i trasporti
content_en: (Photo: Satwork) Satwork d.o.o. company Banja Luka, a regional leader in the field of satellite vehicle tracking and development of advanced telemetry solutions, is proudly celebrating two decades of existence this year. The company is the owner of its own software solution, SatIRS. which is protected as an author`s work and has the relevant ISO certificates, which guarantees the quality of the service and the security of information. On this occasion, we spoke with the company`s director, Siniša Palić, about the vision, challenges and formula for success. This year, Satwork is celebrating its 20th anniversary. How would you describe the company`s journey from the early days to today`s leadership position in the vehicle satellite tracking market? - Satwork`s path was a constant evolution. When we started, the concept of satellite tracking was new, and we had a vision to offer a solution that is as reliable as world standards, and adapted to the specifics of our market. The key to success was in the development of our own software (SatIRS), which gave us control over the functionalities and quick adaptation. The leadership position is the result of commitment to the quality of the 24/7 service and continuous investment in development. Today, Satwork is not just a provider; we are a strategic partner to our clients in digitizing and optimizing their business. What motivated you to embark on an entrepreneurial venture with Satwork 20 years ago, and what are the most important values to you in running the company? - Motivation came from a combination of opportunity and faith in technology. I wanted us to create a solution that will improve processes, bring savings and control. As for the values, the key ones are: Innovation and expertise - we must be creators, not just users of technology; Reliability - in our business, top customer support 24/7 is a guarantee of service quality and Partnership - our goal is the long-term success of the client, because this is the only way to ensure our long-term success as well. All these values ​​led to the fact that Satwork gradually grew from a provider into an advanced analytical platform that provides clients with concrete and automatic savings in business. What people or experiences shaped your approach to business and leadership over these two decades the most? - My leadership was shaped by my first clients and our technical team. I realized that solving problems, not selling products, was the key. In the process, I must point out that we have not had spectacular jumps in revenue and earnings. We worked independently, step by step, often choosing the difficult path, without large investors. But that`s exactly how we`ve built deep stability and resilience - that`s the key reason for our 20-year longevity. For us, stability is more important than speed. Satwork is a laboratory of ideas built on trust and giving the team autonomy. We consider our people to be our biggest strength. In the meantime, Satwork has expanded its operations to Belgrade and Podgorica, and you also operate in the region through partners. What are the biggest differences in customer needs in different markets? - The expansion was a natural step. Our success lies in the ability to offer a single system with modular adaptability. In the dynamic market of Serbia, clients are looking for advanced analytics and integration with ERP systems. In Montenegro, the focus is on efficiency and durability of construction and tourism equipment. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, clients are highly sensitive to costs and focused on the prevention of fuel misuse. Our flexibility as a software company allows us to quickly adapt to any specific requirements. Your SatIRS system is developed by an in-house engineering team. To what extent did innovation and local expertise contribute to your success and recognition on the market? - The development of the SatIRS platform in our house is a pillar of our success. Our local expertise provides us with flexibility and speed of reaction when the implementation of new functionalities is required. Our software is developed for sophisticated integration with top-of-the-line hardware and telemetry devices. This positions us as a technological leader, because we offer continuous development, local support and an author`s solution that guarantees security and growth with the client`s needs. Which services or functionalities of Satwork are most in demand today and why? - The market is looking less and less for just monitoring, and more and more for detailed, preventive analytics. Basic fuel monitoring and control is still the most sought after because it brings the fastest return on investment through the prevention of misuse. Then there`s SatECO – which enables driving style analysis to reduce consumption and increase safety. The SatTACHO service, which enables remote downloading of data from the digital tachograph and tacho analytics, automatic analysis of offenses, which eliminates high fines and reduces administration, is an increasingly current service. At Satwork, you are pioneers in implementing modern technologies and IoT solutions. How do you see the development of the sector in the next 5-10 years, and what is Satwork`s role in that transformation? - We believe that the future of the sector lies in deep analytics and predictive solutions, more precisely active forecasting. The vehicle will become just one sensor in the broader supply chain. Our mission is to make SatIRS the central platform for managing mobile resources. Also, the future is in proactive vehicle management, using advanced analytical methods for predictive maintenance. Our role is to be a reliable technology partner in the digitalization of transport. What are your next goals? Are you planning new innovations, market expansion or additional services within the SatIRS platform? - Our goals are focused on scalability, integration and optimization. Innovation is always part of the plan, just like market expansion. All these goals aim to transform Satwork from a provider into an advanced analytics platform that gives our clients concrete and automatic business savings. One of the goals in the coming year is more active promotion on the market of our SatRAPID, a service for advanced optimization of service operations, drastically reducing downtime in processes. We already have feedback and top ratings from our clients regarding the functionality of this service. We will continue to expand sectoral solutions, for example on the digitalization of railway traffic, where we have already developed SatRAIL, a service for electronic records of the operation of the towing vehicle and the towing staff. This is an innovative and unique solution on our market in the field of digitalization and management of railway transport systems. There will certainly be more new services in the coming period because each new service inspires our users for some new requests. We always look back to our clients and our ideas are based on the clients` real needs for solutions that will improve their processes and reduce costs. SATWORK d.o.o. Banja Luka Satwork SatIRS SatRAIL SatRAPID diary of success special edition newsletter vehicle satellite tracking Diary of success who are the people who run the business world Your comment Send
content_it:
Satwork d.o.o. di Banja Luka, leader regionale nel tracciamento satellitare di veicoli e nello sviluppo di soluzioni telematiche avanzate, celebra quest’anno il suo ventesimo anniversario. L’azienda possiede una propria piattaforma software, SatIRS, registrata come opera d’autore e certificata ISO, a garanzia di qualità e sicurezza dei dati.  

In un’intervista con il direttore Siniša Palić, egli ha sottolineato come la visione iniziale fosse quella di offrire una soluzione affidabile, conforme agli standard internazionali ma adattata alle specificità del mercato locale. La chiave del successo è stata lo sviluppo autonomo del software, che ha permesso flessibilità, aggiornamenti rapidi e un servizio continuo 24/7.  

I valori fondanti di Satwork sono l’innovazione, l’affidabilità e la partnership con i clienti, con l’obiettivo di generare risparmi concreti e automatizzati. L’azienda, cresciuta in modo organico senza investitori esterni, attribuisce la propria longevità alla stabilità, alla fiducia nel team e all’autonomia operativa.  

Oltre alla sede di Banja Luka, Satwork è presente a Belgrado e Podgorica, operando anche tramite partner regionali. Le esigenze dei clienti variano: in Serbia si richiedono analisi avanzate e integrazioni ERP; in Montenegro, efficienza e durata per attrezzature turistiche e da costruzione; in Bosnia ed Erzegovina, il controllo sui costi, in particolare sul consumo di carburante.  

Tra i servizi più richiesti figurano il monitoraggio del carburante, l’analisi dello stile di guida (SatECO) e il servizio SatTACHO per la gestione remota dei tachigrafi digitali. Satwork punta ora a trasformarsi da fornitore di servizi a piattaforma analitica avanzata, con nuove soluzioni come SatRAPID per l’ottimizzazione operativa e SatRAIL per la digitalizzazione del trasporto ferroviario.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’azienda continuerà a sviluppare innovazioni basate sulle esigenze reali dei clienti, con l’obiettivo di migliorare l’efficienza e ridurre i costi. La crescente digitalizzazione del settore dei trasporti offre opportunità alle imprese italiane specializzate in tecnologie IoT, telematica e software per la logistica, potenziali partner in un mercato in espansione.

title_en: Export of ICT services in first ten months EUR 3.727 billion – 12% higher year-on-year
title_it: Export ICT in crescita del 12%
content_en: Illustration (Photo: metamorworks/shutterstock.com) During the first ten months of 2025, ICT services exports reached EUR 3.727 billion, which represents a 12% increase compared to the same period in 2024, said Mihailo Jovanovic, Director of the Office for IT and eGovernment. According to him, these results confirm that Serbia maintains a leading position in the region in the field of ICT sector development. – In the coming year, we expect further implementation of capital innovation infrastructure projects - the expansion of science and technology parks in Nis and Cacak, as well as the commissioning of the Innovation District in Kragujevac and the Industrial and Technology Park in Krusevac, and the expansion of the National Platform for the Development of Artificial Intelligence. With further investment in digitalization, new electronic public administration services, the application of artificial intelligence and biotechnology, we expect to maintain the growth trend in ICT services exports in 2026 – stressed Jovanovic. Additional indicators indicate that the surplus in ICT services in the first ten months of 2025 amounted to EUR 2.929 billion. Naučno tehnološki park Niš d.o.o. Nei primi dieci mesi del 2025, le esportazioni di servizi ICT hanno raggiunto 3,727 miliardi di euro, con un aumento del 12% rispetto allo stesso periodo del 2024, ha dichiarato Mihailo Jovanović, Direttore dell’Ufficio per l’Informatica e la Pubblica Amministrazione Elettronica. Secondo quanto riportato da ekapija.com, tali risultati confermano la posizione di leadership della Serbia nella regione nello sviluppo del settore ICT.  

Per il prossimo anno, sono previsti ulteriori interventi infrastrutturali legati all’innovazione, tra cui l’ampliamento dei parchi scientifici e tecnologici di Niš e Čačak, l’entrata in funzione del Distretto dell’Innovazione a Kragujevac e del Parco Industriale e Tecnologico a Krusevac, nonché l’espansione della Piattaforma Nazionale per lo Sviluppo dell’Intelligenza Artificiale.  

Grazie a continui investimenti nella digitalizzazione, nuovi servizi di e-government, l’impiego di intelligenza artificiale e biotecnologie, si prevede di mantenere la tendenza positiva anche nel 2026. Un ulteriore indicatore evidenzia che, nei primi dieci mesi del 2025, il saldo attivo dei servizi ICT ha raggiunto 2,929 miliardi di euro.  

Le opportunità di collaborazione nel settore ICT, in particolare nei campi dell’intelligenza artificiale, della digitalizzazione e dell’innovazione tecnologica, risultano di grande interesse per le aziende italiane attive in questi ambiti.

title_en: Tehnis planned across from STP Nis: Opening of Data Center, construction of  three new faculties and five institutes announced
title_it: Nuovo polo tecnologico a Niš
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Pixabay / Akela999) On a plot of land of about 10 hectares, across from the STP in Nis, a new part of the city with the working name Tehnis will be built and it will house a Data Center, three faculty buildings, five institutes and a student campus, announced the President of the Nis City Assembly Igor Novakovic. Novakovic says that a contract has been signed for the construction of a Data Center in Nis. - It is a new building, a new facility and Data means everything that is digital, and what the Republic does, from eGovernment, citizen data from the Ministry of the Interior, from other institutions, the army, banks that will be updated in the Data Center in Nis. The electrical power for operation is 30 megawatts, so we will also have to build a new 110/10 transformer station – said Novakovic. He says that the center will be built across the street from the Science and Technology Park, on 10 hectares of land belonging to the Mija Stanimirovic barracks, which is intended for " sports and greenery ". - It is a pasture whose purpose we will change to research and development , and the entire area from "Philip Morris" to Somborski Boulevard will be changed to research and development. It will be a new part of the city - a new district with the working name Tehnis. The construction of three new faculties, five institutes, a student campus and accompanying facilities is planned - announces the President of the Nis Parliament. He says that a new building will finally be built there for the Faculty of Science, which has been struggling with the problem of space for years. However, he did not specify who will finance all this, how much it will cost and when it will be built. Opis: Na zemljištu površine oko 10 hektara, prekoputa NTP-a u Nišu, biće izgrađen novi deo grada sa radnim nazivom Tehnis i u njemu će se nalaziti Data centar, tri zgrade fakulteta, pet instituta i studentski kampus. Centar će se graditi prekoputa Naučno-tehnološkog parka, na 10 hektara zemljišta koje pripada kasarni. (2025) Vidi sve Naučno tehnološki park Niš d.o.o.
