content_it:
Come riportato da ekapija.com, sono iniziate le attività preparatorie per la realizzazione del complesso commerciale e direzionale di Air Serbia a Surčin. Il Segretariato per la pianificazione urbana e le costruzioni di Belgrado ha rilasciato il permesso per l’esecuzione dei lavori preliminari alla Fase 1 del progetto, ubicato sulle particelle catastali 3684/3, 3685/1 e 3734/15. L’avvio dei lavori è previsto per il 28 dicembre, con termine fissato al 1° aprile del prossimo anno.

Il complesso prevede tre edifici indipendenti: la sede amministrativa di Air Serbia, un edificio direzionale e un hotel, per una superficie lorda complessiva di 24.215 m². La prima fase riguarda la costruzione della sede amministrativa (piano terra + 4 piani + seminterrato), con una superficie di 7.985 m², destinata ad accogliere inizialmente 480 dipendenti, con possibilità di espansione fino a 620. Il completamento è previsto per giugno 2026.

La seconda fase, parzialmente sovrapposta alla prima, prevede un hotel di 304 posti letto (piano terra + 5 piani), per una superficie di 8.234 m², con consegna attesa nel primo trimestre del 2027. L’ultima fase, entro il 2030, riguarda un secondo edificio direzionale, identico nella struttura e dimensioni alla sede Air Serbia.

Tutti gli edifici avranno una pianta a triangolo arrotondato e facciate a tenda continua in vetro e pannelli pieni; l’hotel includerà frangisole verticali e un balcone coperto affacciato sulla pista dell’aeroporto.

L’opportunità offerta da questo sviluppo potrebbe interessare aziende italiane attive nei settori dell’edilizia, degli arredi direzionali, dei sistemi vetrati e delle soluzioni alberghiere specializzate.

title_en: Serbia close to merging with EU electricity market
title_it: Serbia vicina all'integrazione nel mercato elettrico UE
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Vereshchagin Dmitry/shutterstock.com) Minister of Mining and Energy Dubravka Djedovic Handanovic said today that Serbia has been a leader within the Energy Community for the third year in a row in harmonizing with EU regulations and so far the only contracting party of this organization that has fulfilled the conditions for merging with the European Union electricity market. Djedovic Handanovic, on the occasion of the Annual Implementation Report for 2025, published by the Energy Community Secretariat, emphasized that Serbia is the first in the Western Balkans to harmonize its legislative framework in the electricity sector. - We have completed our task, which is also part of the Reform Agenda, or the EU Growth Plan. This is the first time that a country that is not a member of the EU meets the conditions to merge with its electricity market and the verification process, conducted by European institutions, is now underway - the minister emphasized. She expressed hope that this process would be quick, because, as she stated, as soon as it is completed, we can connect to the EU electricity market, specifically with the market of Hungary, as our first neighbor, with which we also have a common exchange, which also includes Slovenia. The Minister emphasized that being part of the EU energy market means multiple benefits for Serbia - they relate to faster trade and exchange of electricity, market sustainability, access to better prices, but also to greater energy security in the event of certain challenges or interruptions in supply in neighboring countries, so that we can react faster. She reminded that a set of new laws in the field of oil, gas and mandatory reserves was recently adopted, which continued the process of harmonization with EU regulations, and emphasized that Serbia will continue to increase its energy reserves. - In the last two years, we have significantly increased our mandatory reserves of oil and oil derivatives, which reached 44 days of last year's imports, and the stocks of Eurodiesel alone increased by 72 percent. Good preparedness and reserves of oil derivatives have allowed our citizens not to experience any shortages and give us additional security in the difficult situation we are facing as a result of the sanctions on NIS - said Djedovic Handanovic. One of the main topics at today's Ministerial Meeting of the Energy Community in Vienna was the start of the implementation of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The European Commission has published a proposal for amendments to the CBAM Regulation, which, as of the beginning of 2026, has yet to go through the adoption procedure in the EU institutions. These changes also include some of the issues that Serbia has been raising in the past two years in order to obtain fairer rules for Serbian exporters to the EU. The method of calculating the emission factor for electricity production has been changed, so that the total national production mix will be taken into account, which will reduce the costs of CBAM by about 40 percent. Djedovic Handanovic said that this change, together with some other proposed ones, will also reduce the negative consequences of CBAM on investments in RES. - We are also in the most favorable position when it comes to market integration, and this progress enables the conclusion of a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding with the European Commission, which would determine adequate conditions and deadlines for exemption from the application of CBAM, including progress in the application of carbon pricing instruments - the minister emphasized. In the past year, Serbia has increased its average compliance in all areas measured by the report from 55 to 63 percent. This is the best result in the Western Balkans region, and the second overall, after Moldova, and is above the average of all contracting parties, which this year is 53 percent. Serbia has the best results in the areas monitored in the field of decarbonization, where it has further improved its score this year and is the leader among all contracting parties in the Energy Community with 83 percent. The Serbian delegation at the meeting of the Ministerial Council of the Energy Community in Vienna consisted of Jovana Joksimovic, Assistant Minister of Mining and Energy for International Cooperation, European Integration and Project Management, and Rados Popadic, Assistant Minister for the Electricity Sector. Ministarstvo rudarstva i energetike Republike Srbije Ministry of Mining and Energy Energy Community Dubravka Đedović Handanović Jovana Joksimović Radoš Popadić Your comment Send
content_it: La ministra serba dell’Energia e delle Miniere, Dubravka Đedović Handanović, ha annunciato che la Serbia è il primo Paese dei Balcani occidentali ad aver allineato il proprio quadro normativo al diritto europeo nel settore elettrico, risultando per il terzo anno consecutivo leader nella Comunità dell’Energia. È inoltre l’unica parte contraente dell’organizzazione ad aver soddisfatto tutti i requisiti per l’integrazione nel mercato elettrico dell’Unione Europea. Il processo di verifica da parte delle istituzioni europee è attualmente in corso. La ministra ha espresso fiducia in un’approvazione rapida, che permetterebbe alla Serbia di connettersi inizialmente al mercato elettrico ungherese, con il quale esiste già un exchange comune che include anche la Slovenia. L’integrazione nel mercato UE garantirebbe al Paese benefici quali maggiore sicurezza energetica, accesso a prezzi più competitivi e una reazione più tempestiva a eventuali crisi di approvvigionamento nei Paesi vicini. Parallelamente, la Serbia ha potenziato le proprie riserve obbligatorie di petrolio e derivati, che hanno raggiunto i 44 giorni di importazioni del 2024, con un incremento del 72% delle scorte di gasolio. La Serbia ha anche ottenuto progressi significativi nella revisione del meccanismo CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism): la nuova proposta della Commissione europea, che entrerà in vigore nel 2026, prevede il calcolo delle emissioni in base al mix energetico nazionale, riducendo i costi CBAM del 40% e attenuando l’impatto negativo sugli investimenti nelle energie rinnovabili. Tale avanzamento potrebbe consentire la stipula di un memorandum bilaterale con la Commissione UE per una deroga graduale al CBAM. Secondo la Relazione annuale di attuazione 2025, la Serbia ha migliorato la sua conformità complessiva dal 55% al 63%, risultato migliore dei Balcani occidentali e secondo solo alla Moldavia. Eccelle in particolare nella decarbonizzazione, con l’83% di allineamento, posizionandosi al primo posto tra tutti i membri della Comunità dell’Energia. Come riportato da ekapija.com, questi sviluppi aprono opportunità per le imprese italiane nei settori della fornitura di tecnologie energetiche, infrastrutture elettriche e consulenza per l’adeguamento normativo.

title_en: Putin: Russia has considerations about NIS, dialogue with friends in Serbia underway
title_it: Putin: dialogo in corso su NIS
content_en: (Photo: Drop of Light/shutterstock.com) Russian President has stated that Russia has “considerations” about how and in what direction the solving of the issue of Naftna industrija Srbija (NIS) might go and that dialogue with Serbia is underway, as reported by the Russian news agency TASS. “We have considerations about how, in what way and in what direction we can move together. We have such dialogue underway with our friends in Serbia. We hope we will find the solution needed,” Putin said. During the combined Direct Line Q&A session and year-end press conference, he said that Russia assumed that “friendly Serbia” would perform its obligations in respect of NIS company. – We have the intergovernmental agreement with Serbia concerning adoption of any restrictions whatsoever in respect of this commercial organization. We certainly assume that the leaders of Serbia that are friendly to us will take it into account and will perform obligations they undertook. Otherwise the question arises: How to invest funds in the economy of the country? Where are the security guarantees if even intergovernmental agreements do not work? – Putin said. NIS a.d. Novi Sad NIS Vladimir Putin Your comment Send
content_it: Il presidente russo Vladimir Putin ha dichiarato che la Russia sta valutando “opzioni” su come e in quale direzione procedere nella risoluzione della questione relativa a Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS) e che è in atto un dialogo con la Serbia, secondo quanto riportato dall’agenzia di stampa russa TASS. “Abbiamo delle considerazioni su come, in che modo e in quale direzione possiamo muoverci insieme. Tale dialogo è già in corso con i nostri amici in Serbia. Speriamo di trovare la soluzione necessaria”, ha affermato Putin. Nel corso della tradizionale conferenza stampa di fine anno, ha sottolineato che la Russia si aspetta che la “Serbia amica” rispetti gli obblighi assunti nei confronti di NIS. “Abbiamo un accordo intergovernativo con la Serbia che prevede l’adozione di qualsiasi restrizione nei confronti di questa organizzazione commerciale. Diamo per scontato che i leader serbi, nostri amici, ne terranno conto e adempiranno agli obblighi assunti. Altrimenti sorge una domanda: come investire capitali nell’economia del Paese? Dove sono le garanzie di sicurezza, se nemmeno gli accordi intergovernativi vengono rispettati?”, ha aggiunto. Come riportato da ekapija.com, la posizione espressa da Putin evidenzia la sensibilità strategica del dossier NIS per Mosca. Tale contesto potrebbe creare opportunità per aziende italiane nei settori energetico e petrolchimico, qualora si aprissero nuovi spazi di cooperazione o ristrutturazione nello scenario balcanico.

title_en: “Trump the Serb”: Removing Russian energy from Western Balkans a strategic interest of US
title_it: Interesse strategico USA: ridurre gas russo nei Balcani occidentali
content_en: Illustration (Photo: SergBob/shutterstock.com) US President Donald Trump has signed the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), of which the Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity section is an integral part. The section “Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity” also states that the dependence of the countries of the region on Russian sources of fossil fuels and natural gas ties their economies and policies to Russia and hinders their aspirations for European integration. – Reducing the reliance of the Western Balkans on Russian natural gas supplies and fossil fuels is in the national interest of the United States. The growing influence of China in the Western Balkans could also have a deleterious impact on strategic competition, democracy, and economic integration with Europe – the section states. Among other things, it also states that the state of democracy in Serbia is worrying and that the conditions for holding elections are unfair. The Act, parts of which relate to the Western Balkans and Serbia, also considers accusations by Serbian officials that peaceful protesters, opposition parties and civil society are “attempting to destabilize the government” as worrying. Donald Trump National Defense Authorization Act Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity Your comment Send
content_it:
Il presidente statunitense Donald Trump ha firmato la National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), che include una sezione specifica denominata “Democrazia e prosperità nei Balcani occidentali”. Tale sezione sottolinea che la dipendenza dei Paesi della regione dalle fonti russe di combustibili fossili e gas naturale lega le loro economie e politiche estere alla Russia, ostacolando le aspirazioni di integrazione europea. Si afferma esplicitamente che ridurre questa dipendenza è nell’interesse nazionale degli Stati Uniti.  

Il testo esprime inoltre preoccupazione per la crescente influenza della Cina nei Balcani occidentali, ritenuta potenzialmente dannosa per la concorrenza strategica, la democrazia e l’integrazione economica con l’Europa. Viene segnalata con particolare apprensione la situazione della democrazia in Serbia, ritenuta allarmante, e si evidenziano le condizioni non eque per lo svolgimento delle elezioni. Preoccupanti sono considerate anche le accuse lanciate da funzionari serbi secondo cui manifestanti pacifici, partiti di opposizione e la società civile starebbero “cercando di destabilizzare il governo”.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’atto rafforza l’impegno strategico degli USA nella regione, con implicazioni significative per la sicurezza energetica e la governance democratica. Le imprese italiane attive nel settore energetico, nelle infrastrutture e nei servizi tecnici potrebbero trovare nuove opportunità derivanti da questa spinta verso l’indipendenza energetica e l’allineamento europeo.

title_en: Government determines port area of Bulk Cargo Terminal in Krnjaca - Republic of Serbia to have pre-emptive rights to port infrastructure
title_it: Nuovo terminal merci alla rinfusa a Belgrado
content_en: (Photo: ECOlogica URBO/Zahtev za određivanja obima i sadržaja studije o proceni uticaja na životnu sredinu, screenshot) At its last session, the Government of Serbia adopted the Regulation on determining the port area of the Bulk Cargo Terminal of the New Port of Belgrade in Krnjaca. The port area of the Bulk Cargo Terminal of the New Port of Krnjaca has been determined, as stated, in accordance with the Water Transport Development Strategy of the Republic of Serbia from 2015 to 2025, spatial and urban planning documents and planning documents relating to water management. The planned total area of the port area of this terminal is slightly more than 57 hectares. An integral part of the port area is also the Terminal's anchorage, delimited by coordinate points. - Based on this regulation, the port area and the pre-emptive rights of the Republic of Serbia to port infrastructure and superstructure will be recorded in the real estate cadastre. The Ministry responsible for transport affairs will submit the necessary documentation to the competent attorney's office, which will implement the record - it is stated in the adopted document. Let us remind that, in August of this year, when it comes to this terminal, which has been announced for years, a more concrete step was taken after a long time, by selecting companies that will perform technical control of the project for the construction permit for this project, and in the tender that the Port Governance Agency announced in early July. The winners of that tender were the Institute of Transportation CIP, Axis gradjevinski biro from Sremska Kamenica and Statik from Kovin, who were the only ones to submit a bid for this job. The construction of the Bulk (Aggregate) Cargo Terminal of the Port of Belgrade is planned on the left bank of the Danube, approximately from rkm 1161 to rkm 1159+500 in Krnjaca. Phase-based construction is planned in two phases. The first phase of construction includes the construction of the operational quay, the formation and arrangement of the terminal territory, the formation of the terminal water area, the construction of the embankment on the sides of the terminal territory, the construction of internal roads, water supply, hydrant and sewage networks, electrical installations with lighting and telecommunications. The first phase also includes the construction of an administrative building with vehicle entrance control and a building next to the vehicle scale, the construction of a connection and distribution plant, the construction of two transformer stations, as well as a fence with pedestrian and vehicle gates. The second phase of construction includes the construction of port operator facilities according to the dynamics of the activation of the entire complex, which is not the subject of this project. As previously announced, the project of the terminal in question also includes a raw material landfill, sub-terminals for sand and gravel separation, sub-terminals for aggregate for concrete and concrete asphalt bases, a corridor for the passage of the railway track, traffic areas, parking and green areas. The public procurement for the development of a project for a building permit for the construction of a bulk cargo terminal in Belgrade was carried out by the Port Governance Agency in 2023. Let us remind that, exactly two years ago, the Port Governance Agency submitted a request to the relevant ministry to determine the scope and content of the study on the environmental impact assessment of the project for the construction of a bulk (aggregate) cargo terminal of the new port in Belgrade , in Krnjaca. At that time, it was indicated that the total value of the investment would be around EUR 83.4 million and it was announced that the construction of the terminal would begin in 2023 and would be completed in 2027. This terminal will be one of two planned terminals at two locations in Belgrade, within the port area of the new port of Belgrade. In addition to the terminal in Krnjaca, according to earlier information from eKapija, Belgrade will get a new main port upstream of the Pupin Bridge, on the Banat side, but not at the location of the "Belgrade Amazon" - Beljarica, which was previously controversial because it is the habitat of a large number of protected bird species, but not far from it. In October of this year, the Port Governance Agency submitted a request to the Ministry of Environmental Protection for approval of the Environmental Impact Assessment Study of the Project for the Construction of a Bulk Cargo Terminal for the New Port of Belgrade. content_it:
Il Governo serbo ha adottato un regolamento che definisce l’area portuale del Terminal per merci alla rinfusa del Nuovo Porto di Belgrado a Krnjaca, riconoscendo alla Repubblica di Serbia diritti preordinati sull’infrastruttura e la sovrastruttura portuale. L’area complessiva del terminal è di circa 57,9 ettari e comprende anche l’area di ancoraggio delimitata da punti di coordinate geografiche. Tale regolamento prevede l’iscrizione dei diritti della Serbia al catasto immobiliare, su iniziativa del Ministero dei Trasporti.

Il progetto, annunciato da anni, ha recentemente compiuto un passo concreto con l’aggiudicazione dell’incarico per il controllo tecnico del progetto esecutivo: a risultare vincitrici sono state l’Istituto per i Trasporti CIP, Axis građevinski biro di Sremska Kamenica e Statik di Kovin. La costruzione del terminal, situata sulla sponda sinistra del Danubio tra il km 1161 e il km 1159+500, avverrà in due fasi. La prima prevede la realizzazione della banchina operativa (630 metri), sei posti di ormeggio (105 metri totali), la sistemazione dell’area a terra e delle acque antistanti, strade interne, reti idriche e fognarie, impianti elettrici, illuminazione, telecomunicazioni, recinzioni, edifici amministrativi e due cabine elettriche. La seconda fase riguarderà invece le strutture per gli operatori portuali, in base all’attivazione progressiva del complesso.

Il progetto include anche aree per lo stoccaggio di materie prime, sottoterminali per la separazione di sabbia e ghiaia, sottoterminali per aggregati destinati a calcestruzzo e bitumi, un corridoio ferroviario, parcheggi e spazi verdi. Il valore stimato dell’investimento è di circa 83,4 milioni di euro, con inizio lavori previsto nel 2023 e completamento entro il 2027.

Il terminal di Krnjaca è uno dei due previsti per il Nuovo Porto di Belgrado; l’alto sorgerà a monte del ponte Pupin, sul lato del Banato, ma non nella zona di Beljarica, precedentemente contestata per la presenza di specie protette. Nel 2023, l’Agenzia per la gestione portuale ha bandito la gara per il progetto esecutivo, mentre nell’ottobre 2024 ha presentato al Ministero della Protezione Ambientale la richiesta di approvazione dello studio di impatto ambientale.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’edificio amministrativo sarà costituito da 18 container disposti su due livelli (piano terra + primo piano), con uffici, sala riunioni e locale per il monitoraggio video. Nell’area retrostante saranno costruiti 12 edifici destinati agli operatori portuali, numero massimo previsto per la località.

Per le imprese italiane, il progetto offre potenziali opportunità nei settori delle infrastrutture portuali, della movimentazione merci, delle costruzioni e dell’impiantistica specializzata.

title_en: Zoran Bošković, founder and CEO of Sistemiv and co-founder and CEO of Planeta Sport: If the human is not at the center of the digital transformation, it will not succeed
title_it: Trasformazione digitale centrata sull'uomo
content_en: In an era where markets are rapidly evolving and consumers expect instant and seamlessly coordinated services, an organization`s ability to combine speed, accuracy and stability has become crucial. Zoran Bošković, founder and CEO of Sistemiv and co-founder and CEO of Planeta Sport , explains in an interview for eKapija how large systems can maintain business continuity even in years full of uncertainty, when every operational detail matters. His experience shows that today`s leadership means more than making decisions - it is about a clear vision, organized processes and empowering teams to function independently, but in harmony. Bošković especially points out that digital transformation is not only a matter of introducing new tools, but of changing the way of working and thinking. Through his startup Sistemiv , he develops solutions that enable companies to model and adjust processes in real time, while maintaining control and standards. In his opinion, successful organizations are those where people understand workflows, have room for initiative and can influence results - because the real power of technology lies in the people who use it. The year behind us was a challenging one for almost all industries. How do you see it from the perspective of the leader of a large system like Planeta Sport? - The year behind us has once again shown how important stability and clarity are in business. When you run a large retail system, with many stores, people and processes, uncertainty is felt not only at the level of strategy, but daily in the operational. It is in such circumstances that it becomes clear how important well-organized processes, good communication and teams, that know how to react without improvisation, are. For me, this was a year that confirmed that long-term thinking and a systemic approach yield results even when the market is under pressure. When you have clear workflows and people who understand their role as a whole, the organization can remain stable even in the most demanding circumstances. In such years, leadership is most visible in the ability to maintain focus and not make hasty decisions. Stability is not achieved by big moves, but by consistently managing day-to-day operations. How do you see the future of retail in Serbia and the region, especially in the context of digitization and changes in customer habits? - Retail in the region is undergoing serious transformation. Customers expect speed, accuracy and a consistent experience, regardless of the sales channel. It requires much more than a good product or a strong offer. It requires connected processes, real-time data, and organizations that can quickly adapt. Those who invest in operational efficiency and clearly defined workflows will have an edge. Digitization is no longer something that distinguishes companies, but a basic requirement to remain competitive. Customers today are very quick to recognize organizations that have internal discipline and those that rely on instant coping. That is why in the coming period the winners will be systems that manage to combine speed, accuracy and operational stability. In addition to Planet Sport, you also launched Sistemiv. How did that idea come about? - Sistemiv was created from a very practical experience of working in large systems. For years I have observed how processes exist but are not clearly defined, documented or linked. People know how something is done, but that knowledge often remains in the heads of individuals and does not exist as part of the system. Changes were often IT-dependent and took too long, while the business waited. The idea was to create a platform that allows processes to be clearly modeled, linked and changed in real time, without losing control. This is where the No-code and Low-code approach naturally follows, which allows business teams to actively participate in process management, without the need for programming. This is how sSuite was born, as a solution for orchestrating business processes, based on the BPMN 2.0 standard, with a focus on the people who use those processes on a daily basis. We wanted processes to stop being an abstract or exclusively IT topic, but a tool that business really understands and uses. Sistemiv was born from the need to simplify complex systems, but without losing standards and reliability. Do the companies in the region have enough flexibility today to quickly adapt their business processes to changes in the market? - More and more companies are realizing that traditional work models, where every change requires a long IT cycle, are no longer sustainable. The market changes rapidly, and business must react in real time. We see organizations becoming more willing to take more responsibility for their own processes. In practice, this means that business teams want to be able to adjust their own workflow, rules and priorities, while IT retains control over standards and system stability. Such a balance brings speed, but also safety, which is perhaps the most important combination today. Flexibility is no longer a luxury, but a fundamental organizational capability. Companies that do not develop this in time very quickly enter the mode of constant reaction to problems. You often point out that digital transformation is not a matter of tools, but of ways of working. What does that mean in practice? - In practice, this means that digitizing a bad or unclear process only accelerates problems. If you don`t know how the process is supposed to work, no technology will solve it. Real transformation starts with understanding workflow, responsibilities and goals. Only when the process is clear and measurable, the technology makes sense. Otherwise, we end up with a series of isolated automations that do not deliver systemic value. In such cases, the problems are just moved from one place to another. That`s why at Sistemivo we constantly emphasize orchestration, that is, understanding and connecting the process from beginning to end. What are the most common mistakes companies make when digitizing their processes? - The most common mistake is to focus on the tool instead of the process. Another mistake is expecting quick results without changing your mindset. Digital transformation is not a one-time project, but an ongoing process that requires patience and consistency. When companies accept this, they make changes more easily and achieve stable results. The importance of visibility and measurement is also often overlooked. Without a clear insight into how processes work, there is neither quality optimization nor good decision-making. Companies that introduce measurement and transparency early learn from their mistakes and make decisions based on data, not assumptions. To what extent are human really at the center of digital transformation? - If the human is not in the center, transformation will not succeed. Technology should simplify work, not complicate it. When people understand processes and have the ability to influence them, change is accepted naturally. If not, resistance is inevitable. That`s why I believe in tools that are intuitive and tailored to end users, not just technical teams. People are the ones who give meaning to technology. When technology adapts to people and not the other way around, changes become sustainable. You work a lot with young people, both in a big system and in a tech startup. How do you see their role in the future of doing business? - Young people bring new energy and a willingness to question established ways of working. They often don`t take things for granted, which is a huge advantage in a rapidly changing environment. Our role as leaders is to provide them with an environment where they can learn, make mistakes and grow. When experience and a fresh perspective come together, teams are created that can push boundaries. In such an environment young people mature more quickly as professionals and future leaders. It is an investment that returns multiple times, both to the company and to the organizational culture. What would you highlight as the main lesson from the year behind us and the message for the next period? - The main lesson is that stability comes from clarity. Companies that have organized processes, clear responsibilities and trust in teams can more easily go through uncertain periods. In the following period, I expect an even greater focus on efficiency, orchestration and people. Those who recognize this in time will not only respond to change, but will have the capacity to initiate it themselves. In the years to come, it will not only be good ideas that will make the difference, but the ability to consistently implement them through a clear and stable system. SISTEMIV Planeta sport doo Beograd Sistemiv Planeta Sport Zoran Bošković sSuite special edition newsletter diary of success Your comment Send
content_it:
In un’epoca di mercati in rapida evoluzione e consumatori che richiedono servizi immediati e perfettamente coordinati, la capacità di un’organizzazione di coniugare velocità, precisione e stabilità è diventata cruciale. Zoran Bošković, fondatore e CEO di Sistemiv e co-fondatore e CEO di Planeta Sport, spiega in un’intervista a ekapija.com come grandi sistemi possano garantire continuità aziendale anche in anni incerti, dove ogni dettaglio operativo conta. Bošković sottolinea che la trasformazione digitale non riguarda solo l’introduzione di nuovi strumenti, ma un profondo cambiamento nel modo di lavorare e pensare.

Attraverso la startup Sistemiv, sviluppa soluzioni che permettono alle aziende di modellare e adattare i processi in tempo reale, mantenendo controllo e standard. Il successo, secondo lui, risiede nelle organizzazioni dove le persone comprendono i flussi di lavoro, hanno spazio per l’iniziativa e possono influenzare i risultati. “La vera forza della tecnologia sta nelle persone che la utilizzano”, afferma.

Riflettendo sull’anno trascorso, Bošković evidenzia come la stabilità derivi da chiarezza, processi ben organizzati e team capaci di reagire senza improvvisare. Per il retail in Serbia e nella regione, il futuro richiederà esperienze omogenee su tutti i canali, processi connessi e dati in tempo reale. La digitalizzazione non è più un vantaggio competitivo, ma un requisito fondamentale.

Sistemiv nasce dall’esigenza di superare modelli tradizionali troppo dipendenti dall’IT. La piattaforma sSuite, basata sullo standard BPMN 2.0 e su un approccio no-code/low-code, permette ai team operativi di gestire attivamente i propri processi. Bošković avverte che digitalizzare processi poco chiari accelera solo i problemi; la vera trasformazione inizia con la comprensione e la misurazione dei flussi di lavoro.

La lezione chiave è che la stabilità deriva dalla chiarezza. Le aziende con processi organizzati, responsabilità definite e fiducia nei team saranno quelle capaci non solo di affrontare il cambiamento, ma di guidarlo. La trasformazione digitale ha successo solo se l’essere umano ne è al centro, poiché la tecnologia deve semplificare il lavoro, non complicarlo.

Le imprese italiane, con la loro forte tradizione manifatturiera e di gestione dei processi, potrebbero trovare nel modello proposto da Sistemiv un valido supporto per migliorare l’agilità operativa e la resilienza delle proprie filiere, specialmente in un contesto di crescente complessità.

title_en: Americans stop import of tires from Zrenjanin’s Linglong – Reason: “Forced labor”
title_it: Stop alle importazioni USA di pneumatici dalla Serbia
content_en: (Photo: Vladislav Gajic/shutterstock) The U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has issued a Seizure Order on shipments of automobile tires manufactured in Serbia by the company Linglong International Europe doo Zrenjanin. The decision is effective immediately, and CBP officers at all ports of entry to the U.S. will detain shipments of these tires due to evidence that reasonably indicates the use of forced labor in their production, a statement from yesterday said. This order was issued for violating a provision of the law that prohibits the entry into the United States of goods produced through forced labor. When CBP has evidence that imported goods were produced through forced labor, the Agency, as it is emphasized, takes measures to detain such shipments through such orders. – The message is clear: The United States will not tolerate forced labor in supply chains – said CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott. – Americans should not have to compete with products made through exploitation – said Acting Executive Assistant Commissioner Susan Thomas of CBP’s Office of Trade. – By preventing forced-labor goods from entering U.S. commerce, CBP helps ensure American workers and businesses compete on a level playing field. The order, which concerns the Zrenjanin factory, is the result of a CBP investigation and review of information indicating that Linglong is producing automobile tires using forced labor. CBP said it analyzed worker statements, photographs, employment contracts, field focus group notes, screenshots of text messages, open-source NGO reports, media reports, and academic research. – The evidence demonstrated that workers at Linglong are subject to nine International Labor Organization indicators of forced labor: retention of identity documents, intimidation and threats, isolation, excessive overtime, withholding of wages, debt bondage, abusive living and working conditions, deception, and abuse of vulnerability. The facts underlying these indicators show, by reasonable suspicion, that workers are engaged in forced labor – CBP stated. It added that importers of detained shipments can request destruction or re-export of the shipments, or try to prove that the goods were not produced by forced labor. B. P. La U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) ha emesso un ordine di sequestro nei confronti delle spedizioni di pneumatici per autovetture prodotti in Serbia dalla società Linglong International Europe doo di Zrenjanin. La decisione, immediatamente efficace, prevede il fermo da parte della CBP di tutti i carichi di tali pneumatici alle frontiere statunitensi, a causa di evidenze che indicano in modo ragionevole l’impiego di lavoro forzato nella loro produzione.

L’ordine è stato adottato per violazione della normativa statunitense che vieta l’ingresso di merci realizzate mediante lavoro forzato. L’agenzia agisce con tali misure qualora disponga di prove sull’origine illecita delle merci importate.

«Il messaggio è chiaro: gli Stati Uniti non tollereranno il lavoro forzato nelle catene di approvvigionamento», ha dichiarato il Commissario della CBP Rodney Scott. Susan Thomas, Commissario Esecutivo Vicario dell’Ufficio Commercio della CBP, ha aggiunto: «I cittadini americani non devono competere con prodotti realizzati tramite sfruttamento. Bloccando l’ingresso di merci frutto di lavoro forzato, la CBP garantisce condizioni eque per i lavoratori e le imprese statunitensi».

L’indagine della CBP, che riguarda specificamente lo stabilimento di Zrenjanin, si basa sull’analisi di dichiarazioni di lavoratori, fotografie, contratti di lavoro, note di gruppi focali, screenshot di messaggi, report di ONG, articoli di stampa e ricerche accademiche. Le prove raccolte indicano che i lavoratori di Linglong sono soggetti a nove indicatori di lavoro forzato stabiliti dall’Organizzazione Internazionale del Lavoro: trattenuta di documenti d’identità, intimidazioni e minacce, isolamento, straordinari eccessivi, trattenuta di salari, vincolo da debito, condizioni abitative e lavorative abusive, inganno e abuso di vulnerabilità.

Gli importatori dei carichi bloccati possono richiederne la distruzione o la riesportazione, oppure dimostrare che le merci non sono state prodotte con lavoro forzato, come riportato da ekapija.com. L’episodio potrebbe aprire opportunità per produttori europei, inclusi quelli italiani, di pneumatici, in un contesto in cui gli acquirenti statunitensi cercano fornitori alternativi rispettosi degli standard internazionali.

title_en: Contract for design and construction of first line of Belgrade subway signed – Procurement of 32 sets included
title_it: Firmati accordi per la prima linea della metropolitana di Belgrado
content_en: (Photo: Nacrt plana generalne regulacije šinskih sistema u Beogradu sa elementima detaljne razrade druge linije metro sistema II etapa) The contract for the design and construction of the traffic system for the first phase of Line 1 of the Belgrade subway, as well as the Financial Protocol between the Government of Serbia and the Government of France on cooperation in the field of financing the first phase of the Belgrade subway project, have been signed, the Ministry of Finance announced. The contract for the design and construction of the traffic system for the first phase of Line 1 of the Belgrade subway was signed by the Minister of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure Aleksandra Sofronijevic, the Alstom Europe Region President Andrew DeLeone, the Director of the Public Utility Company Belgrade Metro and Train Andreja Mladenovic and the Secretary of the Secretariat for Public Transport Slaven Andric, while the Financial Protocol was signed by the Minister of Finance Sinisa Mali and the Ambassador of France to Serbia Florence Ferrari. – The protocol envisages financial support in the form of a loan from the French Treasury in the amount of EUR 150 million for the implementation of the Belgrade subway project, one of the most important infrastructure projects in Serbia – said the Minister of Finance Sinisa Mali, as said in the statement. He emphasized that those two contracts represented an important step in the implementation of the first line of the Belgrade subway, which aimed to improve public transport and which represented an environmentally friendly mode of transport. – Serbia will have a modern capital with everything that a city of several million people needs, and Belgrade will get its long-awaited subway, after several decades of waiting and empty promises – stated Mali. He pointed out that priority, strategic projects took a long time, but that with the construction of the subway, Serbia was finally entering a phase when the first results of many years of preparations would be visible. The Minister of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure Aleksandra Sofronijevic emphasized that cooperation with French partners on the project to build the first line of the Belgrade subway was one of the most significant examples of successful interstate cooperation. – This is a clear indicator that Serbia has the capacity to implement complex and strategic infrastructure projects. The construction of the subway is not just an investment in transport infrastructure, but an investment in sustainable development, improving the quality of life of citizens and the future of Belgrade as a modern European capital. This project confirms that Serbia is investing in infrastructure in a planned and responsible manner that will serve generations to come – said Sofronijevic. The French Ambassador to Serbia Florence Ferrari said that she was pleased with that day's signing of the commercial contract with Alstom for the train sets of the first line of the Belgrade subway and the financial protocol that would enable its financing. – This signing represents a new, decisive and concrete stage of this project, which is important both for our bilateral relations and for France’s engagement in supporting strategic projects that benefit the citizens of Serbia. The arrival of the subway in Belgrade will improve the quality of life of Belgraders by reducing traffic congestion and carbon emissions, which will also improve the air quality in the city – said Ferrari. The commercial contract with Alstom includes the development of project and technical documentation, procurement, transportation and execution of works on the installation of equipment and materials, testing and commissioning of the Traffic System of the first phase of Line 1 of the Belgrade Subway. This contract envisages the procurement of a total of 32 sets of subway trains, which represents the total need for the entire Line 1, as well as the implementation of supporting systems necessary for the safe and reliable functioning of subway traffic. When fully completed, the first subway line will connect Zeleznik and Mirijevo, the second line is planned for the Bezanija-Mirijevo section, while line three will connect Banjica and Bezanija. Il Ministero delle Finanze ha annunciato la firma del contratto per la progettazione e la costruzione del sistema di trasporto della prima fase della Linea 1 della metropolitana di Belgrado, nonché del Protocollo Finanziario tra il Governo della Serbia e il Governo francese per il finanziamento del progetto. Il contratto è stato firmato dalla Ministra delle Costruzioni, Trasporti e Infrastrutture Aleksandra Sofronijević, dal Presidente di Alstom Europa Andrew DeLeone, dal Direttore dell’azienda pubblica Belgrade Metro e Train Andreja Mladenović e dal Segretario per il Trasporto Pubblico Slaven Andrić. Il Protocollo Finanziario è stato invece sottoscritto dal Ministro delle Finanze Siniša Mali e dall’Ambasciatrice di Francia in Serbia Florence Ferrari.

Il protocollo prevede un prestito del Tesoro francese di 150 milioni di euro per la realizzazione del progetto, definito dal Ministro Mali «una delle più importanti infrastrutture in Serbia». Egli ha sottolineato che i due accordi rappresentano un passo cruciale per dotare Belgrado di una metropolitana moderna, attesa da decenni, che migliorerà il trasporto pubblico e offrirà una soluzione ecologica alla mobilità urbana. La Ministra Sofronijević ha definito la collaborazione con la Francia un esempio di eccellente cooperazione intergovernativa, evidenziando che il progetto non è solo un investimento infrastrutturale, ma anche in sostenibilità e qualità della vita.

L’Ambasciatrice Ferrari ha ribadito l’importanza del progetto per i rapporti bilaterali e per il sostegno francese a iniziative strategiche a beneficio dei cittadini serbi, sottolineando i vantaggi in termini di riduzione del traffico e delle emissioni inquinanti. Il contratto con Alstom prevede la fornitura di 32 treni – sufficienti per l’intera Linea 1 – e l’installazione dei sistemi necessari al funzionamento sicuro della metropolitana. La Linea 1 collegherà Zemun (Zeleznik) a Mirijevo; le Linee 2 e 3 sono rispettivamente previste tra Bežanija-Mirijevo e Banjica-Bežanija. Come riportato da ekapija.com, questo progetto rappresenta un’opportunità per le imprese italiane attive nel settore delle infrastrutture, dei trasporti e della fornitura di sistemi ferroviari di collaborare in futuri lotti o forniture complementari del sistema metropolitano di Belgrado.

title_en:
Arijana Maksimcuk, owner of Telemax company:
In business, there is no waiting - you either create or you disappear
title_it: Leadership femminile nel tech bosniaco
content_en: (Photo: Nikola Maksimčuk) Ariana Maksimchuk entered entrepreneurship when the circumstances were anything but favorable. In the post-war period, without safe templates and ready-made paths, she decided to build her own system of values ​​and work. Telemax was born from the need for creation, freedom and constant pushing of boundaries, and its founder is today considered one of the rare female leaders in the engineering and technological business in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Today, more than two decades later, this company is synonymous with new technologies and innovations, and its story is an example of perseverance, courage and a vision that does not compromise with mediocrity. - I have to admit that my life path was determined by my "female compass" - I knew first what I didn`t want, and from that my decision to embark on the adventure of an independent business was born. What I knew very well was that I could not function as a person in the state system and the rules that apply there. I founded my own company at the age of 40 with a clear vision of never seeing myself in retirement, because my temperament and spirit do not accept a life that is not filled with creation and pushing boundaries. First of all, by myself... More than anything else, I like to create and work, so that when I look back, let`s say in one year, I must see clear results. And that, you will admit, is possible only in your own company or in an international corporation - said the owner of the company Telemax Arijana Maksimchuk in an interview for eKapija. In one of the interviews, you said that you don`t accept the answer "can`t". What is the most important thing you learned about perseverance in working with people, but also through encounters with institutions, bureaucracy and systemic obstacles? - After all, it is, first of all, a matter of character, and then also of business culture, which with us private individuals always stems from this first... I could never accept that something could not be done, just because obstacles appeared. If I spent hours, days, years on a project that is realistic, rational and sustainable, I could not forgive myself if any procedure and bureaucracy stopped me. I could say a lot on that topic, I went through a lot of procedures applying new technologies, which is perhaps the slowest and most difficult process in institutions, because there are no rules for new technologies and anything that goes "out of the box". In my experience, I don`t have unfinished subjects or unsuccessful projects due to institutions and bureaucracy, because I have at least a thousand recipes for mastering it. I am guided by the principle "you can never be as persistent in ignoring as I can be persistent in insisting". There was everything, from sitting in front of offices all day, to chasing around the field and intercepting on the stairs. Some would say that it might be inappropriate. But when you know that you are right and when the existence of dozens of families depends on your results, there is no shame, door or obstacle that can stop me. I only regret my time and energy that was spent on bureaucracy, instead of creation and progress. Life would be better and simpler for everyone in the state if we spent time on creation, and not on waiting for the slow processes that apply in institutions. Because the biggest problem is the slowness and procrastination of the process, and business does not tolerate that. Is what you are saying the fate of all entrepreneurs who embark on innovative businesses? Does it have to be a "difficult road" with us every time? - I have to admit that there are also positive examples of state administration, and here I come back to the fact that everything in life, even in state systems, starts with people. From those who lead and who give their personal, characterful example to the administration they lead. For example, the municipalities of Gradiška and Laktaši give us hope that the administration could one day speed up and follow the businessmen. Just as it is important for me to get a job, perform it well and get paid, it should also be important for decision-makers that someone brings new technology to their environment, applies it successfully and points to new directions for their environment. And they recognized it. That`s how we influence everyone around us, encourage each other to move forward. I didn`t allow any negative energies or obstacles, which were often "invisible" to stop me. Creative energy is much stronger and more powerful than negative energy, as my life and experience have shown. Family support has been key to you from the beginning. What does the process of making strategic decisions look like within the family and company and how do you deal with the fear of the unknown? - My greatest strength is my family and my batteries are charged only if everything is fine in our family and if we are in harmony among ourselves. As a woman, I am particularly sensitive to family dynamics, and that is another, additional responsibility that we, as the gentler sex, have when we are in independent business waters. That`s why we have some of our traditions and ways of recharging our batteries and enjoying ourselves, and I try to nurture that regardless of the pace of life, which is getting faster and faster. I have no fear of the unknown, because when I enter any new project or technology, I prepare very well and have a large database that I use for preparation. I`m not vain and I like to hear a lot of different opinions before making a decision. There are a lot of preparatory meetings with people both here and abroad, where I ask for advice and consultation, and only when my intuition and tables confirm it, do I enter an unknown project. It takes a lot of time, it requires a lot of sacrifice, but that is why it is important that my family understands and follows me. Today, Telemax is a leader in new technologies. How do you cultivate that culture of innovation in an environment that is often not ready for progress? - The slogan of our company is "The Future Today", because in my biography I have many technologies that I applied for the first time in our country. It`s my passion and it turned out to bring the biggest profit. For me it is something natural and very simple. It is probably a matter of talent and a special sensibility for the new and unknown that I recognize as a challenge. I dunno, I seem to have a "sixth sense" for innovation. You lead complex projects that introduce new technologies for the first time in BiH. Which project was the biggest test of your knowledge and endurance personally? - I remember the construction of the Delta shopping mall as an extremely difficult project. And not because of the type of installations and technologies that we had to complete, although we used new technology, but rather the problem of the organization of the construction site and the relationship between the investor and the main contractor, which is still in court today regarding the payment of that project. The pressure felt by all of us who were present as contractors on that building is for me an example of an endurance test. There is no money in the world that will make me participate in anything like that in the future. That`s why I turn to projects that depend on me the most. It is easier for me to move the mountain by myself than to wait, hope and believe that the others will turn one stone at a time. (Photo: Nikola Maksimčuk) You recently said that you haven`t had a single failed or unfinished project. What are you doing differently than most to accomplish this? - I make decisions. As it was that I no longer want to participate in these types of construction projects such as Delta shopping, regardless of the value. This introduced my company to the cycle of new technologies, namely the design and construction of solar power plants and our own solar products, which I sincerely enjoy today. Because in this business, the organization of the construction site is not like in construction, where you always depend on someone. In this business, my company manages everything by itself and I have no other companies that can slow me down, stop me, influence the work, the deadlines, the quality of the execution. When you don`t have someone slowing you down and when everything depends on your skill, dedication and resourcefulness, then you can create top results both for yourself and for the client. Immediately after the publication of the Law on Renewable Sources, in 18 months we installed over 8.5 MW of solar power, which after the Delta project was a real recovery for us and a return to the normal functioning of the company, which I consider our exceptional success. For the same period of time, we achieved a much higher income with the great satisfaction of all employees and without any pressure, out-of-series efforts that we had to invest before. But this type of business that we have chosen requires a lot of additional work. I work a lot on my improvement, I study a lot. I am very persistent, sometimes too much, until I push it to the end and I have a strong intuition as my hidden weapon and I am the most creative in organizing work. I managed quite significant and demanding projects, completely different in terms of technologies, and it was always a new challenge for me. So far, I haven`t had any mistakes or unfinished projects because, in addition to the vision and strategy, I am also very focused on the details. We, as a contractor, have a great responsibility - and that is to complete the work according to the principle of light in hand. Sometimes it is ideal, and sometimes it is very demanding, as I mentioned. However, one thing is common in both cases - we have to finish regardless of the cost. And that`s why we`ve been successfully existing for 23 years. The lack of professional staff is one of the biggest challenges in all sectors. How do you motivate people to learn, grow and stay in the company despite the difficult social and economic environment? - By taking care of employees, good salaries and a humane approach. As a director, I am very demanding and it is not easy to follow me. But I also try to give back to my people not only financially, but also with a lot of empathy for their life and human circumstances. I constantly have several employees with whom I personally work and finally, after many years, I received support in this. I found an excellent HR expert who helps me and my younger son a lot in selecting employees. I learned one great truth, which is that there are no irreplaceable people in the company, so I stopped investing myself where it is obvious that there will be no changes. In the last year, we have employed a lot of new people and changed the energy in the company. It was not an easy task in this time when we are facing a shortage of professional staff. But to be honest, expertise in employment is not such a big problem anymore, everything is learned slowly. The biggest challenge is whether employees will answer the tasks with their psycho profile. It is well known that every company has its own rules and traditions, and I think that every employee can learn a lot in terms of professional knowledge, because we always have older and more experienced experts who accompany younger ones. But if the employee does not have the motivation, the will, and the desire to overcome the obstacles they encounter every day, we as employers cannot "upgrade" them or teach them. What is the main problem of the labor market in your opinion? - Business ethics, dedication, motivation and will to work and create. The resourcefulness that is necessary to possess in order to overcome obstacles. That, I responsibly claim, is becoming the biggest problem for newly employed people. It is already a matter of public policies and business culture that is built, nurtured and encouraged in a systemic and educational society, and this is where I personally see big problems in our environment in the future, because no one is working on it. Neither the school, nor the institutions, and the family is slowly lagging behind in that field. As a society, we are still burdened by backward beliefs and values ​​such as "secure job", "civil service"... But this is a topic that should be devoted to more than one question, and I would stop there. Perhaps you, as creators of public policies, could support us entrepreneurs to jointly and systematically try to change the awareness of this topic? After the prestigious "Captain Miša Anastasijević" award, you also won the "Lady in Business" award. What does female leadership mean to you personally, and where do you see the greatest obstacles, but also the greatest opportunities for women in the economy? - After 30 years of my directorial and leadership role, I was recognized by the media and people who started to deal with the topic of female leadership, which is a very rare phenomenon in our region. Because it is much easier and more painless in life to be a classic woman than a woman leader and decision maker. Not because women are weak or not valuable enough, but because society is created in such a way that, although it gives a certain space to women to develop in business, on the other hand, it expects her to keep all those other roles that are extremely demanding. The process in society that helps create a greater number of women leaders is a process in which, to begin with, stereotypes that apply in our region must be changed in society. It is the most difficult process and that is why so few women appear in leadership positions. Unfortunately, women leaders who have courage, family support and the power and knowledge to do something really worthy of respect appear very rarely in our area. I am very sorry that the female energy, which is positive, much fairer and not burdened by the competitive spirit like the male, does not have more space and support. We all know that with women in leadership positions, we would have a more humane society, and that is why we must all work to support today`s girls so that they are stronger, more resilient and win our battles tomorrow. The processes are so slow, but that doesn`t mean we shouldn`t fight every day. A typical women`s business is, for example, banking, where you have the largest number of women employees, and you do not have a single woman as a general director in BiH. That`s why I think that this question is very difficult to answer, and this again opens up a new topic of the "glass ceiling" that women in business face. Everything is given to you, but not to the top... Nevertheless, I responsibly claim that with the support of decision-makers, directors, owners or themselves - women can do everything, they have a chance in all areas, as I have successfully worked for 30 years in a typically engineering male business. You often point out that "a happy family is the number one success." How do you balance your personal life and running a business that requires 15 hours of work a day? - Only good and precise organization and work on yourself both on tools in the business and on new recipes in the kitchen, which is a pleasure for my loved ones! I embraced my "invisible work" and with great pleasure I am both a cook and grandmother, I prepare ajvar and make a ritual out of it. I may sleep less, but my spirit is more hungry for inspiration than rest. In the time of global turbulence, wars and economic changes - what would you advise young entrepreneurs who are just entering the business world today? - I would honestly think about it, because very little can be predicted, and there are great turbulences and changes that you could not have predicted. But all those who feel inside that they have strength, that they want something of their own, must be quick and must have the courage to venture into the unknown. I would also add that they must carefully evaluate whether their family can follow this and be open and honest with their loved ones about this topic. Because the statistics of family firms are not good in the sense of sustaining the business and passing it on to the second generation. There are many cases of disturbed relationships within the family due to business, and that is why I would appeal for openness and conversation without "having to". A deal builds a house in life, and in business as well. How do you see the personal and also the development of Telemax in the next decade? - Telemax remains in solar energy and renewable sources and, of course, new technologies in that area, and it seems to me that the conditions for the younger son to take over the helm of the company next year are being met. In that case, I will have more time for my favorite hobbies that have been neglected for the last 20 years, and of which I have plenty - from traveling and destinations I want to see, to learning and mastering new AI tools, which will make it easier for us to complete daily tasks and meet our daily needs. Of course, the most important thing is spending more time with grandchildren and loved ones. But I`m looking forward to the future! Because despite the challenges, the new era brings us lifelong learning and new opportunities to turn our dreams into reality. So... You can expect more new and innovative projects from me 😊. Telemax d.o.o. content_it:
Arijana Maksimčuk ha fondato Telemax in un periodo post-bellico privo di modelli sicuri, diventando una delle poche donne a guidare un’azienda nel settore ingegneristico e tecnologico in Bosnia ed Erzegovina. Oggi, dopo oltre vent’anni, Telemax è sinonimo di innovazione e tecnologie rinnovabili. “Ho fondato la mia azienda a 40 anni con la visione di non andare mai in pensione – ha dichiarato Maksimčuk in un’intervista a ekapija.com – perché il mio spirito non accetta una vita senza creazione e superamento dei limiti”.

La sua filosofia è chiara: “In affari non si aspetta – o si crea o si scompare”. Rifiuta la parola “non si può” e ha affrontato burocrazia e ostacoli sistemici con perseveranza, arrivando a trascorrere intere giornate davanti agli uffici pur di portare a termine i progetti. “La lentezza delle istituzioni è il vero nemico del business”, afferma.

Dopo l’esperienza difficile della costruzione del centro commerciale Delta, ha scelto di concentrarsi su progetti autonomi, in particolare impianti fotovoltaici. Nei 18 mesi successivi all’entrata in vigore della legge sulle fonti rinnovabili, ha installato oltre 8,5 MW di potenza solare, riportando l’azienda a una crescita sostenibile.

Per Maksimčuk, il successo deriva da una combinazione di intuizione, preparazione e attenzione ai dettagli. Sottolinea anche l’importanza del supporto familiare e di un approccio umano verso i dipendenti: “Competenza si impara, ma motivazione e spirito di iniziativa sono qualcosa che non si può insegnare”.

Critica la mancanza di etica professionale e di resilienza tra i giovani lavoratori, attribuendola a politiche pubbliche e un sistema educativo inadeguati. Riguardo alla leadership femminile, lamenta la persistenza di stereotipi e del cosiddetto “soffitto di vetro”, pur affermando con convinzione: “Con il supporto giusto, le donne possono eccellere in qualsiasi settore”.

Il futuro di Telemax punta sulle energie rinnovabili, con un passaggio generazionale imminente al figlio minore. “Il mio sogno è dedicare più tempo ai nipoti e ai viaggi, ma anche imparare nuovi strumenti di intelligenza artificiale”, conclude.

Le imprese italiane attive nel settore delle energie rinnovabili, delle tecnologie solari e della consulenza ingegneristica potrebbero trovare opportunità di collaborazione con aziende dinamiche come Telemax, aperte all’innovazione e con una solida rete operativa in Bosnia ed Erzegovina.

title_en: Improving energy efficiency of Military Medical Academy – Rehabilitation of hospital according to German model for EUR 211 million
title_it: Riqualificazione energetica della Clinica Militare per 211 milioni
content_en: (Photo: Shutterstock/Nikola_Goga) The project “Greening the Public Sector - Rehabilitation of the Military Medical Academy” is a significant step forward in improving energy efficiency and sustainable resource management in the military healthcare system. This was stated by Serbian Minister of Defense Bratislav Gasic, presenting a new project financed within the framework of bilateral cooperation between Serbia and Germany. Green energy for sustainability The project, worth a total of EUR 211 million, is being implemented in coordination with the German Development Bank and the German Ministry of Mining and Energy. Minister Gasic emphasized that the goal of the project was to reduce energy consumption and use renewable sources through the preservation and protection of the natural environment. The Military Medical Academy is, as he stated, one of the largest military hospitals of the tertiary level of healthcare in Southeast Europe, where a council for any type of intervention can be formed under one roof in ten minutes. He pointed out that the “Rehabilitation of the Military Medical Academy” project was being implemented in three phases, with the first phase planned to begin in the third quarter of 2026. This phase would include the rehabilitation of the building structure, the reconstruction of the roof on the lower part of the building with an increase in thermal resistance to heat transfer, the reconstruction of the system for preparing hot sanitary water using waste heat using heat pumps, the reconstruction of water connections, and more. New equipment and cooling systems Gasic said that work was underway to ensure that the MMA received new cooling systems by June 30 the next year and that 1,200 beds were replaced with new hospital beds according to global standards. Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany Anke Konrad pointed out that the MMA was the largest medical institution in Serbia and one of the largest in Europe, and that one of the main goals of the project was to reduce gas, water and electricity consumption. Konrad emphasized that the project had been supported by the German Development Bank with EUR 50 million and the EU with EUR 5 million. The announcement of this tender is being carried out under the international competitive tender procedure and offers a very wide range of contractual options under internationally recognized contractual conditions, the ambassador stated. Konrad emphasized that it was important that the procurement was carried out according to the standards of the German Development Bank, all of which ensured the transparency of the project. Fotografije: Opis: Vojnomedicinska akademija (VMA, ustaljeno „Ve-Me-A”) je ustanova tercijarne zdravstvene zaštite i centar za postdiplomsko školovanje vojnomedicinskog kadra u Srbiji. Kompleks akademije se prostire na površini od 21 hektara, zgrada VMA ima oko 180.000 kvadratnih metara i podeljena je na 60 tehničko-tehnoloških celina. U svom sastavu ima 26 klinika, 25 operacionih sala, 11 instituta, Polikliniku sa različitim specijalističkim i supspecijalističkim kabinetima, Nacionalni centar za kontrolu trovanja, Centar hitne pomoći, Centar za transplantaciju organa, tkiva i ćelija itd. Godišnje se u njoj bolnički zbrine oko 30.000 pacijenata (vojnih i civilnih osiguranika), obavi isto toliko hirurških intervencija i više od 500.000 specijalističkih pregleda. VMA ima oko 2.500 zaposlenih, od čega preko 500 lekara i 160 profesora i drugog nastavnog osoblja. U njoj se školuje oko 400 lekara (na specijalističkim studijama iz oblasti medicine, stomatologije, farmacije, biohemije, molekularne biologije, veterine, fizičke hemije i psihologije), domaći i strani studenti, a obavlja se i praktična nastava srednjih i viših medicinskih škola. content_it:
Il progetto “Greening the Public Sector – Riqualificazione dell’Accademia Medico-Militare” rappresenta un passo significativo verso il miglioramento dell’efficienza energetica e della gestione sostenibile delle risorse nel sistema sanitario militare serbo, come dichiarato dal Ministro della Difesa serbo Bratislav Gašić. L’iniziativa, del valore complessivo di 211 milioni di euro, è finanziata nell’ambito della cooperazione bilaterale tra Serbia e Germania, in collaborazione con la Banca tedesca di sviluppo (KfW) e il Ministero tedesco dell’Energia e delle Risorse Minerarie.

L’obiettivo principale è la riduzione dei consumi energetici mediante l’impiego di fonti rinnovabili e il risparmio di gas, acqua ed elettricità. L’Accademia Medico-Militare di Belgrado, uno dei maggiori ospedali militari d’Europa con circa 180.000 m² di superficie, 26 cliniche e oltre 30.000 ricoveri annuali, sarà riqualificata in tre fasi. La prima, prevista per il terzo trimestre del 2026, includerà il rifacimento strutturale, la ricostruzione del tetto con miglioramento dell’isolamento termico, l’installazione di pompe di calore per il recupero del calore di scarto e l’adeguamento delle reti idriche.

Entro il 30 giugno del prossimo anno saranno inoltre installati nuovi sistemi di raffreddamento e sostituiti 1.200 letti con modelli conformi agli standard internazionali. Il progetto beneficia di un contributo di 50 milioni di euro dalla KfW e di 5 milioni dall’Unione Europea. La gara internazionale sarà condotta secondo le procedure competitive internazionali e gli standard della Banca tedesca di sviluppo, garantendo trasparenza e conformità alle migliori pratiche. Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’ampia gamma di lotti tecnici e la portata dell’intervento offrono opportunità rilevanti per le imprese italiane specializzate in efficienza energetica, impianti tecnologici e fornitura di attrezzature sanitarie.

title_en: Preparations and analyses of justification for development of nuclear program in Serbia underway
title_it: Serbia avvia analisi per programma nucleare
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Unsplash/Lukas Lehotsky) Preparations and analyses of justification for the development of a nuclear program in Serbia are underway, said Assistant Minister of Mining and Energy Rados Popadic at the conference "Towards a Nuclear Future - European Partnerships for the Serbian Energy Transition" at the French Embassy in Belgrade. - Serbia, like other European countries, is in the process of energy transition in which new sources of baseload energy are necessary to exit coal-fired production - he said. Popadic emphasizes that last year and this year Serbia undertook "a large number of activities to develop strategic guidelines and documents in the field of energy related to nuclear energy". - We have lifted the ban on the construction of nuclear power plants that had been in force since 1989 and have begun several years of preparations and analysis of the justification for the development of a nuclear program, in accordance with the recommendations of the International Atomic Energy Agency, with the aim of ensuring long-term and sustainable energy security - Popadic said. He stated that Serbia, by amending the Energy Law, has begun the first phase of the development of a nuclear program for peacetime purposes. He added that memorandums of understanding had been signed with the French Electric Power Company (EDF), the South Korean company KHNP, and the Russian Federation, and that cooperation was at a similar level with the United States. - There are initiatives to expand cooperation with other countries whose experiences are useful in decision-making during the first phase in which we are working on improving the regulatory framework, strengthening human capacities, exchanging knowledge, organizing professional training, and informing the public - said Popadic. The neighboring countries - Slovenia, Hungary, Bulgaria, and Romania - already have nuclear power plants and are planning their further development, and it is useful for Serbia to review their experiences and initiate a public dialogue on the role of nuclear energy, he noted. Popadic emphasized the importance of cooperation in this process between the ministries of science, finance, environmental protection, the Vinca Nuclear Institute, the Directorate for Radiation and Nuclear Safety and Security (SRBATOM), universities and faculties. Fotografije: Opis: Institut za nuklearne nauke „Vinča” osnovan je 1948. godine kao istraživački centar za realizaciju nuklearnog programa SFR Jugoslavije. Oblasti istraživanja su: fizika, hemija, biologija, energetika, zaštita od zračenja i zaštita životne sredine, zdravlje i životna sredina, nauka sa akceleratorima, nauka o materijalima. Sve ove oblasti pripadaju grupi prirodnih i tehničkih nauka. Zbog multidisciplinarnosti rada u institutu, on je sposoban da odgovori na glavne strateške pravce istraživanja koji su postavljeni na nivou države: novi materijali i nanonauke, energetika, biomedicina i zaštita životne sredine. Institut za nuklearne nauke „Vinča” osnovan je 1948. godine kao naučni centar za istraživanje najsavremenijih tema u osnovnim prirodnim naukama — fizici, hemiji i biologiji. Zapravo, baš tim redom. Zadatak da osnuje institut dobio je profesor Pavle Savić, fizikohemičar, koji je pozvan nazad u Jugoslaviju iz Instituta za fizičke probleme u Moskvi, gde je radio u laboratorijama akademika, kasnije Nobelovca, Pjotra Leonidoviča Kapice od poslednje godine Drugog svetskog rata. Izgradnji Instituta za ispitivanje materija, kako ga je zvao, odnosno Instituta za fiziku, kako je kasnije glasio zvanični naziv, Pavle Savić je posvetio sve svoje snage, volju i predanost. Uz njega je učestvovalo nekoliko kolega entuzijasta, ali je sve bitnije poslove uradio upravo on sam. Zna se, recimo, da je većinu početnih laboratorija (za fiziku, hemiju i biologiju) sam projektovao i nadgledao izgradnju, tako što je boravio u blizini gradilišta, na seoskom imanju i spavao na slami u ambaru. Kasnije je koordinisao opremanje instituta instrumentima za naučna istraživanja, koje je dobrim delom uspeo da dobije iz inostranstva na račun ratnih reparacija. Okupio je u Institutu tadašnju mladu naučnu elitu Jugoslavije, uglavnom od stručnjaka entuzijasta koji su tek završili školovanje. Radila su se istraživanja koja su definitivno dala prepoznatljiv doprinos početku takozvane „nuklearne ere” u svetu. U prvo vreme najviše su bila zastupljena istraživanja iz fizike i hemije, a nakon par godina institutu se pridružuje i Dušan Kanazir, koji otpočinje razvoj bioloških disciplina, pre svega u vezi sa efektima radioaktivnog zračenja. I Kanazir i Savić kasnije su bili predsednici Srpske akademije nauka i umetnosti. Ubrzo nakon početka, institutu je bila namenjena realizacija državnog nuklearnog programa istraživanja, koji je okončan 1968. godine. Od te godine institut nastavlja istraživanja u okviru mešovitog (ne samo nuklearnog) koncepta.
