content_it:
L’assistente del ministro per le Miniere e l’Energia, Rados Popadić, ha dichiarato nel corso della conferenza “Verso un futuro nucleare – Partnership europee per la transizione energetica serba”, tenutasi presso l’Ambasciata francese a Belgrado, che sono in corso preparativi e analisi per giustificare lo sviluppo di un programma nucleare in Serbia. “La Serbia, come altri Paesi europei, è in transizione energetica e necessita di nuove fonti di energia di base per abbandonare la produzione da carbone”, ha affermato.  

Popadić ha ricordato che negli ultimi due anni il Paese ha intrapreso numerose attività per elaborare linee guida strategiche e documenti nel settore energetico legati all’energia nucleare. È stato abolito il divieto, vigente dal 1989, alla costruzione di centrali nucleari e sono iniziate analisi pluriennali conformi alle raccomandazioni dell’Agenzia internazionale per l’energia atomica, finalizzate a garantire una sicurezza energetica a lungo termine e sostenibile.  

Con la modifica della legge sull’energia, la Serbia ha avviato la prima fase dello sviluppo di un programma nucleare a fini civili. Sono stati firmati memorandum d’intesa con la francese EDF, la sudcoreana KHNP e la Federazione Russa, e la cooperazione con gli Stati Uniti procede su un livello analogo. Sono inoltre in atto iniziative per ampliare la collaborazione con altri Paesi, al fine di rafforzare il quadro normativo, potenziare le competenze tecniche, scambiare conoscenze, organizzare formazioni professionali e informare l’opinione pubblica.  

Popadić ha evidenziato l’importanza di valutare le esperienze dei Paesi vicini – Slovenia, Ungheria, Bulgaria e Romania – che già dispongono di centrali nucleari e ne prevedono l’espansione. Ha infine sottolineato la necessità di una stretta collaborazione tra i ministeri della Scienza, delle Finanze e della Tutela ambientale, l’Istituto nucleare Vinča, la Direzione per la sicurezza radiologica e nucleare (SRBATOM), nonché università e facoltà.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa fase preliminare apre potenziali opportunità per aziende italiane attive nel settore energetico, in particolare in ambiti quali la consulenza tecnica, la formazione, la sicurezza nucleare e la fornitura di tecnologie specializzate.

title_en: Extension of gas arrangement until March 31 agreed
title_it: Proroga accordo gas fino al 31 marzo
content_en: Illustration (Photo: bibiphoto/shutterstock) Serbia has reached an agreement to extend gas supplies for another three months, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said. - We have an agreement to extend gas supplies for another three months, until March 31, so people can be safe and rest easy, Serbia will have both electricity and enough gas for the upcoming winter season - Vucic said. Regarding the nationalization of NIS , he said that we should wait until January 15. - We will wait until the last moment, but even then we will not seize, but we will buy. We are waiting for the Russians to complete their part of the work, we hope that they will complete it by January 15, but then we will try to pay for it if necessary, even beyond what it is worth - Vucic said. When it comes to the energy situation and the upcoming period, as he added, the state has information that Gazprom is talking, among others, with the Hungarian MOL . - We have no problem with secondary sanctions. We cannot import the 6,000 tons of diesel per day that we consume. We have been successful in doing so for exactly 75 days now and I am proud of that - he added. NIS a.d. Novi Sad MOL Serbia d.o.o. Beograd Naftna industrija Srbije ad Novi Sad Gazprom MOL gas arrangement with Russia sanctions on NIS sale of NIS nationalization of NIS Your comment Send
content_it:
La Serbia ha raggiunto un accordo per prorogare le forniture di gas per altri tre mesi, fino al 31 marzo, ha dichiarato il presidente serbo Aleksandar Vučić. “Abbiamo un accordo per estendere le forniture di gas fino al 31 marzo, affinché la popolazione possa sentirsi al sicuro. La Serbia avrà sia elettricità che gas sufficiente per la prossima stagione invernale”, ha affermato.  

In merito alla nazionalizzazione di Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS), Vučić ha precisato che si attende il 15 gennaio: “Aspetteremo fino all’ultimo momento, ma anche allora non procederemo a un sequestro: acquisteremo. Stiamo attendendo che i russi completino la loro parte di lavoro; speriamo entro il 15 gennaio, dopodiché cercheremo di pagare, se necessario, anche oltre il valore effettivo”.  

Riguardo alla situazione energetica, il presidente ha aggiunto che lo Stato è a conoscenza di contatti tra Gazprom e la compagnia ungherese MOL. “Non abbiamo problemi con le sanzioni secondarie. Non possiamo importare i 6.000 tonnellate quotidiane di gasolio che consumiamo, ma da 75 giorni riusciamo a farlo con successo, e ne sono orgoglioso”, ha concluso, come riportato da ekapija.com.  

L’accordo prolungato offre stabilità al mercato energetico serbo, creando contestualmente opportunità per aziende italiane attive nel settore energetico e nella fornitura di tecnologie collegate all’efficienza energetica e alla diversificazione delle fonti.

title_en: Dušan Torbica, President of Elnos Group Management Board: Solutions, not excuses - the formula for success in 18 markets
title_it: Elnos Group: soluzioni, non scuse
content_en: Reliability is the key to our success. We do not rely on old glory. We strive to be better today than yesterday and we look at each day as a new opportunity. This was announced by Dušan Torbica, the president of the Elnos Group , which marks eight decades of tradition this year, three decades of modern business and operates in a total of 18 markets in the region and Europe. - We have great trust from our partners because we adhere to three rules: deadline, quality, safety. When circumstances change, we look for solutions, not excuses. Today, we are a group with more than 900 employees that is big enough to take on the most demanding jobs - says Torbica. This year you celebrate eight decades of tradition and three decades of modern business. When you look back, what would you say shaped the Elnos Group today the most? - I would say, in short - reliability. That is the key to our success. We are always guided by the principle: what is agreed must be implemented. If you give your word and don`t put it into action, it can last a day, a month, even a year, but at some point your business story has to take a downward trajectory. And that`s the "secret". As much as it is important to us that we are satisfied with the completed work, I can freely say - we are even more happy when our business partners tell us that we have exceeded their expectations. Reputation is hard to build and easy to lose. That`s why we never took any risks and that`s why we`re where we are. Today, we are working on really big projects, but we approach every job, despite, as you mentioned, eight decades of tradition and three decades of modern business, as if it were the first. What do I want to say? In our work, there is no place for amateurism. We do not rely on old glory. We strive to be better today than we were yesterday. Every day for us is a new opportunity. Construction of WPP Cibuk 2 - 155 MW The energy transition is accelerating all over Europe. From the point of view of Elnos Group, what does it mean for the development of new knowledge and professional profiles within the company? Is the structure of the competencies you need most changing? - Absolutely. But that doesn`t mean we had to make radical changes in our staffing policy. We already have quality staff and we are constantly working to make them even more skilled and expert. We are constantly offering our people new training. In 2025, we reached an impressive figure of 8,000 hours of training. The members of our team do not consider it an obligation, but an opportunity. It is interesting that our employees have the possibility to propose trainings, and the quality of implementation is monitored through the annual employee satisfaction survey. What, exactly, is our goal? At Elnos Group, we believe that our employees are our greatest capital and that their development and success form the foundation of the company`s progress. In the economy today, what was valid a year ago is no longer valid, and in the energy sector, these trends are changing even faster. Therefore, we have experience, which we are building up daily. When you follow that recipe, there`s no obstacle you can`t overcome, and you can`t be surprised by any rule change in the market. Jubilee celebration in the Sava Center What was the role of your employees for all these successes you achieve? - They are our greatest value. Through all these decades behind us, we knew one thing - without a satisfied employee, we cannot expect results. Their satisfaction is a guarantee of success. People make a company successful, not vice versa. When the worker "grows", the company grows as well. When your team members are motivated, results are guaranteed. Any collective will have a bright future when the epicenter of its attention is a human being. Trends are changing. The rules of the market are changing. However, if you have quality staff, you are capable of successfully overcoming any challenge. That`s why I like to say that I`m lucky to work with people who consider the success of our company their own success. In such a working environment, decision-making is much simpler. Construction of the 380 kV transmission line Conneforde-Cloppenburg-Merzen in Germany The Elnos Group is equally successful both domestically and on numerous, extremely demanding European markets. What`s the "secret"? - Yes, we work all over Europe. In all those countries, 18 in total, three rules are the same: deadline, quality, safety. That`s our standard. We are flexible enough to adapt to any regulation, climate, terrain. We have a lot of trust from our partners, because everything we agree on, we achieve within the agreed time. When circumstances change, we look for a solution, not an excuse. Today, we have more than 900 employees and we are big enough and professional enough to take on the most demanding jobs. That`s why Elnos Group is successfully operating today from Scandinavia to South-Eastern Europe. Our network consists of stable resource centers in six countries and member companies that implement complex projects in energy, infrastructure and industry - from design to EPC execution and digitization. Our member network enables us to provide localized delivery and support throughout Europe. Recently, a contract was signed with the Sinohydro company on the construction of the Vetrozelena wind farm, which will be the largest individual wind project in the Balkans. What does this project mean for Elnos Serbia, and how will it affect the further development of competences and the positioning of Elnos in the field of renewable energy sources in the region? - Exactly, Elnos Serbia has signed an EPC contract with Sinohydro Corporation Limited, a subsidiary of Power China Construction Group, for the construction of the Vetrozelena wind farm, which will be the largest single wind project in the Balkans. Vetrozelena will have a total power of 300 MW, and 48 turbines with a single power of 6.25 MW. Elnos Srbija , as a member of the Elnos Group, will undertake the implementation of the complete connection to the transmission system of Elektromreža Srbija. This work includes the construction of a 35/400 kV substation with four 90 MVA transformers, a 400 kV connection and distribution plant with six fields, a connection two-system 400 kV transmission line 7.5 kilometers long, as well as accompanying infrastructure upgrades within the power distribution and telecommunications network. This project represents another contract concluded under the EPC principle, within which Elnos Srbija realizes complete engineering. The expertise and dedication of our engineers, technicians and fitters, comprehensive knowledge and rich experience on similar projects, along with the financial and organizational stability of the company, give us firm confidence that we will realize this project successfully and within the agreed deadlines. Certainly, just as you said, this project will contribute to the additional development of our competences, but also to the strengthening of our position in the field of renewable energy sources. After signing the contract with Sinohydro Corporation Limited In which phases of the energy transition is Elnos Group participating? - We are present in all phases of the energy transition - from renewable sources and substations to digitization and industrial automation. We operate through more than 20 legal entities and representative offices organized in accordance with local legislation and standards. This type of organization enables us a high degree of flexibility, competitive deadlines and strong technical support. In the past decades, we have implemented more than 1,000 complex projects across the continent, with a constant expansion of our geographical reach and technical capacities. Operating in several countries, members of the Elnos Group take on different but related roles that together form the whole of our business system. Some are experts in field work. Others are design and engineering centers, with teams that create complex technical solutions. The third ones deal with the production and assembly of equipment, maintenance and digital integrations. This functional diversity makes Elnos Group a flexible and reliable system - capable of managing even the most complex projects independently. With such a foundation, we can be builders, innovators, and guardians of stability in the coming decades as well. What are the plans of the Elnos Group for 2026? - We are continuing the same course. We will carry out numerous contracted projects. In the year ahead, the energy industry will continue to seek a balance between supply security and accelerated transition. It is precisely between the aspiration towards stability and the need for innovation that the key steps will take place that will shape the energy future. Our plans are aligned with European energy goals, but are just as firmly rooted in the region we come from. And in 2026, we will continue to strengthen our role, carrying out projects that connect the stability of networks, renewable sources and new technologies. We want to be even more present, faster and closer to partners who build the energy future together with us. Because the future is not waited for - it is built, consistently and with dedication, project by project, megawatt by megawatt. Elnos Srbija doo Beograd ELNOS BL d.o.o. content_it:
L’affidabilità è la chiave del successo del Gruppo Elnos, che quest’anno celebra 80 anni di tradizione e 30 di attività moderna, operando in 18 mercati in Europa e nei Balcani. Come affermato da Dušan Torbica, presidente del Consiglio di Amministrazione, la filosofia aziendale si basa su tre pilastri: rispetto delle scadenze, qualità e sicurezza. “Quando le circostanze cambiano, cerchiamo soluzioni, non scuse”, ha dichiarato Torbica, sottolineando che il gruppo, con oltre 900 dipendenti, affronta ogni progetto con la stessa determinazione, indipendentemente dalla sua esperienza storica.

Il Gruppo Elnos attribuisce il proprio successo alla continua formazione del personale: nel 2025 sono state erogate 8.000 ore di training, spesso proposte dagli stessi dipendenti. Il coinvolgimento e la soddisfazione del personale sono considerati fattori cruciali per la crescita aziendale.

Elnos Serbia ha recentemente firmato un contratto EPC con Sinohydro per la realizzazione del parco eolico Vetrozelena, il più grande singolo impianto eolico nei Balcani (300 MW). Il progetto include la costruzione di una sottostazione 35/400 kV, una linea di trasmissione da 7,5 km e relative infrastrutture.

Il Gruppo partecipa a tutte le fasi della transizione energetica, dalla produzione da fonti rinnovabili alla digitalizzazione e automazione industriale, grazie a una rete di oltre 20 entità legali e uffici di rappresentanza. Per il 2026, Elnos prevede di consolidare ulteriormente il proprio ruolo nella realizzazione di progetti che integrino sicurezza energetica, rinnovabili e innovazione tecnologica.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’approccio di Elnos potrebbe offrire interessanti opportunità di collaborazione per imprese italiane attive nei settori dell’energia, infrastrutture e ingegneria, grazie alla sua apertura a partnership internazionali e al suo modello operativo flessibile su mercati europei.

title_en: Share of renewable energy sources in gross final energy consumption in Serbia increases to 25.8% in 2024
title_it: Energie rinnovabili in Serbia al 25,8%
content_en: Illustration (Photo: PhotographyByMK/shutterstock.com) The share of renewable energy sources in gross final energy consumption in Serbia reached 25.8% in 2024, which is only slightly higher than the previous year when the share was 0.4% lower, according to the RES Serbia portal. Eurostat data shows that Serbia is slightly above the European Union average, where the share of renewable energy sources last year was 25.2%. Among the European Union member states, Sweden recorded the highest share of renewable energy sources in gross final energy consumption, as much as 62.8%. Sweden primarily relied on solid biomass, hydropower and wind. Finland followed with 52.1%, relying on solid biomass, wind and hydropower, while Denmark was third with 46.8%, with the majority of renewable energy coming from solid biomass, wind and biogas. The lowest shares of renewable sources were recorded in Belgium (14.3%), Luxembourg (14.7%) and Ireland (16.1%). Serbia and the region The biggest improvement is recorded in the heating and cooling sector, where renewable sources account for 37.2% of total consumption. In electricity production, the share of RES is 32%, while in transport the situation has been almost unchanged, at only 0.6% for four years. Compared to the countries of the region, Serbia lags behind, according to Eurostat data. Albania leads with as much as 46.9%, while Montenegro is at 40.8%. The growth rate in Serbia is slower than in the EU, while the EU has almost tripled the share of RES in two decades (from 9.6% to 25.2%), Serbia has only doubled it (from 12.7% to 25.8%). Targets by 2030 The revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), adopted in 2023, raised the binding target from the previous 32% to 42.5% of RES in gross final energy consumption, with ambitions to reach 45%. According to the National Energy and Climate Plan, Serbia has set targets by 2030: 33.6% share of RES in total energy consumption, 45% in electricity production, 41% in the heating and cooling sector, and 3.2% in transport. Nel 2024, la quota delle fonti di energia rinnovabile nel consumo finale lordo di energia in Serbia ha raggiunto il 25,8%, in lieve aumento rispetto all’anno precedente, quando era pari al 25,4%, secondo il portale RES Serbia. I dati di Eurostat indicano che la Serbia si colloca leggermente al di sopra della media dell’Unione Europea, che nel 2023 era al 25,2%. Tra gli Stati membri dell’UE, la Svezia ha registrato la quota più elevata (62,8%), seguita da Finlandia (52,1%) e Danimarca (46,8%). Le quote più basse sono state osservate in Belgio (14,3%), Lussemburgo (14,7%) e Irlanda (16,1%).

In Serbia, il settore con i maggiori progressi è quello del riscaldamento e raffrescamento, dove le rinnovabili coprono il 37,2% del consumo. Nella produzione elettrica la quota è del 32%, mentre nei trasporti si attesta allo 0,6%, un valore pressoché invariato da quattro anni. Rispetto ai Paesi della regione, la Serbia è in ritardo: l’Albania registra il 46,9% e il Montenegro il 40,8%. Negli ultimi vent’anni, l’UE ha quasi triplicato la quota di rinnovabili (dal 9,6% al 25,2%), mentre la Serbia l’ha raddoppiata (dal 12,7% al 25,8%).

La Direttiva rinnovabili riveduta (RED III), adottata nel 2023, fissa per l’UE un obiettivo vincolante del 42,5% al 2030, con l’ambizione di arrivare al 45%. Secondo il Piano Nazionale per l’Energia e il Clima, la Serbia punta al 2030 a una quota del 33,6% di rinnovabili nel consumo energetico totale, con obiettivi settoriali del 45% nell’elettricità, 41% nel riscaldamento e raffrescamento e 3,2% nei trasporti, come riportato da ekapija.com.

Questo contesto potrebbe offrire opportunità alle imprese italiane attive nel settore delle energie rinnovabili, in particolare nelle tecnologie per il riscaldamento da fonti rinnovabili e nell’efficienza energetica, ambiti in cui la Serbia deve ancora compiere significativi progressi.

title_en: Petrol for Serbia via Constanta
title_it: Benzina per la Serbia via Costanza
content_en: Illustration (Photo: VGstockstudio/shutterstock.com) The Constanta Oil Terminal, operator of the state-owned oil terminal on the Black Sea, announces that it wants to diversify its business and will be able to receive imported petrol for distribution on the Romanian market and in neighboring countries, reports Profit.ro. The company's new plans envisage the modernization of the storage infrastructure, the implementation of modern measurement and control equipment, the expansion of the product portfolio, as well as the expansion of capacities in strategic areas of the port. In the medium term, the main goal is to automate all technological flows, minimize the risk of human error, optimize transfer times and increase work safety, reports the National Oil Committee of Serbia. - The oil terminal intends to diversify its operational flows and adapt to the future needs of the Romanian and regional markets, in order to remain a visited regional hub. This will allow it to receive imported gasoline for distribution to the Romanian market and neighboring countries, areas that could suffer from gasoline supply problems after the NIS Pancevo, Lukoil Romania and Lukoil Burgas refineries were closed as a result of the sanctions, the company announced. In recent years, projects have been implemented to increase storage capacity, so in the future, the goal will be to modernize existing and improve the safety of equipment. The company will continue to look for "green" projects, for which it can access funds and improve environmental conditions. NIS a.d. Novi Sad NIS a.d. content_it: Il Terminal Petrolifero di Costanza, gestore dell'impianto statale sul Mar Nero, intende diversificare la propria attività e sarà in grado di ricevere benzina importata per la distribuzione sul mercato rumeno e nei Paesi vicini, secondo quanto riportato da Profit.ro. I nuovi piani aziendali prevedono la modernizzazione delle infrastrutture di stoccaggio, l'installazione di sistemi moderni di misurazione e controllo, l'ampliamento del portafoglio prodotti e l'incremento delle capacità nelle aree strategiche del porto. L'obiettivo a medio termine è l'automazione di tutti i flussi tecnologici, la riduzione al minimo del rischio di errore umano, l'ottimizzazione dei tempi di trasferimento e il miglioramento della sicurezza sul lavoro, come riportato dal Comitato Nazionale del Petrolio della Serbia. Il terminal mira a diversificare i propri flussi operativi e ad adattarsi alle future esigenze dei mercati rumeno e regionale, mantenendosi un hub regionale di riferimento. Questo permetterà di ricevere benzina importata per i mercati che potrebbero subire carenze a seguito della chiusura, per effetto delle sanzioni, delle raffinerie NIS di Pančevo, Lukoil Romania e Lukoil Burgas. Negli ultimi anni sono stati realizzati progetti per aumentare la capacità di stoccaggio; in futuro, l'obiettivo sarà la modernizzazione degli impianti esistenti e il potenziamento della sicurezza. L'azienda continuerà inoltre a ricercare progetti "verdi", per accedere a finanziamenti e migliorare le condizioni ambientali. Questa evoluzione potrebbe offrire opportunità alle imprese italiane attive nella fornitura di tecnologie per l'automazione, la sicurezza industriale e le soluzioni ambientali nel settore energetico.

title_en: Dalibor Arbutina, director of PE Nuclear facilities of Serbia: In the next five years, we can lay the foundations of nuclear power in Serbia
title_it: Fondamenta per il nucleare in Serbia
content_en: (Photo: JP Nuklearni objekti Srbije) Dalibor Arbutina has been running the Public Enterprise Nuclear Facilities of Serbia for more than ten years. For the next five years, he believes, it is crucial to establish a legal framework, strengthen the regulatory body and develop study programs that will ensure the continuous development of staff. Serbia, he says, has the experts and infrastructure for the first stages of nuclear projects, but the success depends on a coordinated approach between the state, educational institutions and international partners, in order to make nuclear power a safe and sustainable part of the energy mix. Arbutina points out that the future of nuclear energy in Serbia depends on the strategic decisions of the state, investment in education and retention of experts. For more than a decade, you have been running the Nuclear Facilities of Serbia. How does that long-term experience help you to perceive the real possibilities of Serbia in the development of nuclear energy today? What experiential milestones have most shaped your current perspective? - I had my first real engineering job and experience in this field at the Public Enterprise Nuclear Facilities of Serbia on the realization of the project of repacking and transporting spent nuclear fuel of the research nuclear reactor RA to the country of origin, the Russian Federation and it was while working on that project that I had the opportunity to meet and see all the activities in action, which were necessary to realize such a complex and non-routine job, in our country and with our people and experts, and with the great support of experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency and the Russian Federation as the carrier of the technology. With that generation of young engineers, who over time became top experts, I have been working continuously since then on the rehabilitation of the historical legacy of previous nuclear programs. In addition to ongoing temporary problems that we successfully solve with the help of the Government of the Republic of Serbia and the relevant ministry, we also manage to realize the set goals and manage the nuclear facilities in a safe and secure manner. You often point out that Serbia has experts capable of carrying out nuclear projects in the first phase. What do you base that assessment on and what should be done to further strengthen that staff? - The program for the introduction of nuclear energy is not only based on knowledge of reactor technology, but is a synergy of several technical areas on which the safety of nuclear facilities depends. In relation to classic thermal power plants, for whose work we have both experts and experience, nuclear power plants differ only in the part that generates heat, which generates steam that drives the turbines, i.e. in that nuclear part. The public enterprise has two nuclear research reactors and a team of experts which has been working all these years on their maintenance and rehabilitation, but also teams of experts in the following nuclear fields which guarantee the safety and security of those facilities such as radiation safety, nuclear safety and manage radioactive waste. With the preserved staff who transferred from the Institute of Nuclear Sciences Vinca to the Public Enterprise Nuclear Facilities of Serbia, of which I am the head, a new team of personnel has developed, which can be the basis for expanding the necessary personnel base for the programs chosen by the state. At times, this company faced staff fluctuation, especially in the wave of development of the IT sector in Serbia, which is not good for long-term planning. It takes time to develop highly skilled specialists for this kind of program, and with the help of IAEA experts, they can also gain the necessary experience for work and decision-making. However, it is necessary to ensure the conditions so that experts do not leave, and for that we need the help of the state, as we have had until now. Are there Serbian experts abroad who could help us in introducing nuclear energy? - Several times in the past, and even these days, the public could hear about the negative side effects of the passing of the Law on the Prohibition of the Construction of Nuclear Power Plants in the SFRY. A large number of experts active at the time, in the best years of their careers, left the country in the nineties. Young people`s interest in studying relevant programs has also decreased to a negligible level, so faculties that had dedicated study programs, such as the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering in Belgrade, have closed such programs. In the meantime, those experts who left the country then retired. We know from the meetings we have had, and from publicly available publications, that there is a certain smaller number of younger people who had personal interests in this field and chose to study abroad and stay in the field working there. Several associates from our company also decided to improve their skills at jobs abroad. When we talk about the future of nuclear energy in Serbia, what do you consider to be a realistic time frame for the country to enter the process of building a nuclear power plant? - That time frame will depend on the selected strategy for the introduction of nuclear power in Serbia. The public can still hear arguments for various options: from participation in a nuclear power plant in the area, through small modular power plants to the construction of one or more large, standard nuclear power plants. It is self-evident that those time frames can be significantly different, and the longest would be for the construction of a large power plant. The deadlines for the construction of large power plants are getting shorter and shorter, so today it can be seen that they range from 7 to 15 years, depending on the model, type, supplier and available resources. Every investor today, including the state, has an interest in returning invested funds as quickly as possible. This will certainly be one of the criteria for the selection of the supplier. What are the possible locations for the construction of a NPP in Serbia? - In the period when the SFRY was planning the construction of the Krško NPP and called for a tender for a number of new power plants, certain tests of suitable locations in the SFRY were carried out, several of which were in the Republic of Serbia. It remains to be seen how favorable they would be today in the new circumstances. The International Atomic Energy Agency has issued a series of publications on the criteria for site evaluation for a nuclear power plant. Those criteria have a focus on safety, environmental impact and economy, and the availability of significant amounts of cooling water sources, low population density, geological stability, seismic integrity, simple transport solutions and accessibility, connection to the electricity grid and public acceptance are set as conditions. The requirements should meet the balance of the reliability of project solutions in relation to external natural risks and social needs. Small modular power plants (SMR) are often presented in the world as a faster solution for energy transition. How realistic are they as an option for Serbia and which models would be the most acceptable? - Several technical solutions make small modular power plants the optimal solution for certain situations. The state has not yet chosen the optimal path for the Republic of Serbia to introduce nuclear energy into the energy mix. The choice will depend on many factors, such as financial solutions, implementation deadlines and current energy needs. Small modular nuclear reactors differ from standard reactors in terms of size, power, the fact that inherent safety measures are built in, design flexibility, and the ability to relatively easily expand capacity on site. They are also made suitable by certain technical solutions such as the less frequent need for overhaul and fuel replacement, for example. One of the advantages of these reactors is that their construction is faster compared to standard reactors, because they are delivered to the selected location. Taking into account the fact that they are small, it is possible to locate them in locations that would not be suitable for standard reactors. Their size and design flexibility, which ranges from so-called 10 MW(e) to 300 MW(e) microreactors make it possible to install them in different locations, such as small remote communities, industrial plants in inaccessible locations and the like. The output of small modular reactors can range up to 300 MW(s) per unit, which is about 1/3 the production capacity of standard nuclear reactors. Which models would be acceptable for Serbia, will depend on the characteristics of the location and the energy needs of the defined priority to be solved at that moment. What are all the countries that export civilian nuclear energy technology? - Currently, the largest exporters of nuclear power plants and nuclear technologies are Russia, China, the USA, South Korea and France, (not necessarily in this order, depending on which element of technology we are talking about). Today, the USA is mainly focused on new generations of small modular reactors. During the construction of NPPs abroad in recent years, in some cases, construction costs have been drastically exceeded. What are ways to avoid it? Is there even work for our construction industry? - The construction costs will also depend on the type of power plant that Serbia decides on. If we are talking about small modular power plants, it is to be expected that in that case there will be no breach of the planned deadlines and costs, because the finished product is delivered. When it comes to large reactors, many circumstances can lead, and have led in the known past, to breaking the deadlines and thus the construction costs. Although it is known that nuclear power plants are not experimental plants, where it is not known what can happen during construction, but facilities with multiple tested and implemented technical solutions, deadlines are occasionally missed. The causes are mostly local in nature, from political and financial, to locational - new findings that require additional work or to new technical solutions that have been reached in the meantime, and which are safer and still chosen despite the delay they cause. The best solution to avoid cost overruns would be not to overrun the deadlines, which means that all preparatory work would have to be completed in detail and completely, up to the level that is foreseen for that phase. Whether there will be work for our construction industry will depend on the type of power plant chosen. But a nuclear power plant is not only a reactor building, but also a series of accompanying functional facilities and systems in the environment of the power plant, for the realization of which there could be room in principle, as long as it is oriented and prepared for such tasks. The biggest challenge in the public sphere is the trust of citizens. How would you explain today`s nuclear safety standards and how different they are from people`s perceptions? - Public perception of the risks of nuclear technologies was primarily a consequence of the seen effects that nuclear energy can have on the population and the environment (the first military application of nuclear energy in 1945 on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, as well as accidents at nuclear power plants with global effects, more Chernobyl than Fukushima). Although nuclear accidents are rare events, because they cause serious damage, they generate a strong signal about the unusually high risk of nuclear power plants, which contributes to forming its negative perception. Research has shown that even in countries with a large number of nuclear power plants and a stable exploitation history without accidents, the consequences of major accidents, regardless of the distance of those facilities, have contributed to a decrease in public confidence in nuclear energy. However, on the other hand, accidents contribute to improving safety requirements and standards. For each accident at nuclear facilities, and especially for those with the greatest consequences (Three Mile Island 1979, Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011), a detailed analysis of the cause, flow, measures taken and their effectiveness and consequences is carried out, and based on these so-called "lessons learned", the technical, organizational and personnel requirements regarding the safety of nuclear facilities are significantly improved, which, on the other hand, also affects the increase of public trust. Research has shown that public confidence in nuclear energy is higher in communities that already have nuclear facilities installed. As a result, today`s generations of nuclear power plants are being built according to innovative and stricter safety requirements and based on operational experience that today amounts to 20378 reactor-years (according to IAEA data). If Serbia makes a strategic decision to enter the nuclear energy sector, what would be the three most important steps that we must take in the next five years? - The most important steps would refer to the establishment of a legal and institutional framework for the introduction of nuclear energy, strengthening of the regulatory body, and establishment of study programs at the relevant faculties. In addition, it is necessary to recognize the necessary institutional infrastructure for responding in the event of an accident and to work on raising those elements and linking them. And in the process, at some point reopen the site review and microsite testing for the nuclear power plant. content_it:
Dalibor Arbutina, direttore dell’Azienda Pubblica “Impianti Nucleari della Serbia”, ritiene che nei prossimi cinque anni il Paese debba porre le basi per l’introduzione dell’energia nucleare. Ciò richiede l’adozione di un quadro normativo adeguato, il rafforzamento dell’autorità di regolamentazione e lo sviluppo di programmi di studio per formare e trattenere esperti qualificati. Secondo Arbutina, la Serbia dispone già di competenze e infrastrutture per le fasi iniziali di progetti nucleari, grazie al lavoro svolto negli anni presso l’Istituto di Scienze Nucleari Vinča, oggi trasferito all’Azienda Pubblica. Il Paese possiede due reattori di ricerca e personale specializzato in sicurezza nucleare, gestione delle scorie radioattive e protezione dalle radiazioni.

Il percorso verso un’eventuale centrale nucleare dipenderà dalla strategia scelta: partecipazione a impianti regionali, centrali modulari di piccole dimensioni (SMR) o grandi reattori standard. Le SMR, con potenze da 10 a 300 MW(e), offrono tempi di realizzazione più brevi e maggiore flessibilità di collocazione, ma la decisione finale dovrà considerare esigenze energetiche, risorse finanziarie e fattibilità tecnica. Tra i principali esportatori mondiali di tecnologia nucleare civile figurano Russia, Cina, Stati Uniti, Corea del Sud e Francia.

L’esperienza internazionale dimostra che i costi di costruzione possono lievitare soprattutto nei grandi impianti, a causa di ritardi legati a fattori politici, finanziari o tecnici. Una pianificazione accurata e completa delle fasi preliminari è essenziale per evitarli. Anche il settore edile serbo potrebbe beneficiare di opportunità, soprattutto per le infrastrutture accessorie all’impianto nucleare.

Infine, Arbutina sottolinea l’importanza di ricostruire la fiducia del pubblico, superando percezioni legate a incidenti passati. Le attuali centrali nucleari sono progettate con standard di sicurezza molto più elevati, basati su decenni di esperienza operativa – oltre 20.000 anni-reattore secondo l’AIEA. Come riportato da ekapija.com, i tre passi cruciali per la Serbia nei prossimi cinque anni sono: definire il quadro legale, rafforzare l’autorità di regolamentazione e avviare programmi accademici mirati. Tali misure potrebbero aprire opportunità di collaborazione per imprese italiane specializzate in infrastrutture energetiche, tecnologie nucleari e formazione tecnica avanzata.

title_en: Serbia preparing for nuclear energy – Memorandum signed with World Institute for Nuclear Safety
title_it: Serbia punta sull'energia nucleare
content_en: Illustration (Photo: SpaceKris/shutterstock.com) The PE Nuclear Facilities of Serbia has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the World Institute for Nuclear Security (WINS), which, as stated, further strengthens the institutional and expert basis for the development of the nuclear sector in Serbia. The agreement comes at a time when Serbia lifted the moratorium on the construction of nuclear facilities, introduced 35 years before, at the end of 2024, and represents, it is added, one of the key steps in preparing the country for potential future nuclear projects. The Memorandum defines WINS’s strategic support in the areas of consulting, technical guidance, customized training and strengthening institutional capacities, with the aim of improving the readiness of the regulatory framework, project development and overall infrastructure. Special emphasis is placed on nuclear safety as the foundation of future development. The cooperation will include strengthening professional capacities and professional development of employees, including the participation of the staff of the Nuclear Facilities of Serbia in the WINS Academy programs , as well as joint work on topics such as cybersecurity, threat assessment, protection against insider threats, nuclear safety regulations, security culture and supply chain security. The memorandum also envisages cooperation in the field of management of nuclear and other radioactive materials that are outside regulatory control, as well as activities aimed at improving gender equality, diversity and inclusion in the nuclear sector, both in Serbia and internationally. WINS Executive Director Lars van Dassen emphasized that, at a time when Serbia was considering new nuclear projects, it was essential that nuclear safety was embedded in the very foundations of that development. According to him, by combining the international expertise of WINS and the national leadership of the Nuclear Facilities of Serbia, the conditions are created for building the knowledge, capacity and trust necessary to face modern security challenges. Dalibor Arbutina, Director of the Public Enterprise Nuclear Facilities of Serbia, assessed that the signing of the memorandum represented an important milestone in the long-standing cooperation with WINS. As he stated, the previous cooperation has enabled employees to gain valuable knowledge in the field of nuclear safety and security, and the new agreement further strengthened technical capacities, regulatory readiness and commitment to the development of a safe and inclusive nuclear sector. JP Nuklearni objekti Srbije Beograd World Institute for Nuclear Security WINS Lars van Dassen Dalibor Arbutina nuclear power plants Your comment Send
content_it:
L’Azienda pubblica “Impianti Nucleari della Serbia” ha firmato un Memorandum of Understanding con il World Institute for Nuclear Security (WINS), rafforzando ulteriormente le basi istituzionali ed esperte per lo sviluppo del settore nucleare nel Paese. L’accordo arriva dopo che, alla fine del 2024, la Serbia ha revocato il moratorio sulla costruzione di impianti nucleari, in vigore da 35 anni, e rappresenta una tappa chiave nella preparazione per futuri progetti in ambito nucleare.

Il Memorandum prevede il supporto strategico di WINS in consulenza, assistenza tecnica, formazione personalizzata e rafforzamento delle capacità istituzionali, al fine di migliorare la preparazione del quadro normativo, lo sviluppo dei progetti e l’infrastruttura complessiva, con particolare attenzione alla sicurezza nucleare come fondamento dello sviluppo futuro.

La collaborazione includerà lo sviluppo professionale del personale, anche tramite la partecipazione ai programmi della WINS Academy, oltre a iniziative congiunte su temi come cybersecurity, valutazione delle minacce, protezione da insider, normative sulla sicurezza nucleare, cultura della sicurezza e sicurezza della catena di approvvigionamento. È prevista anche la cooperazione nella gestione di materiali nucleari e radioattivi fuori dal controllo normativo, nonché azioni per promuovere parità di genere, diversità e inclusione nel settore nucleare, sia in Serbia che a livello internazionale.

Il direttore esecutivo di WINS, Lars van Dassen, ha sottolineato l’importanza di integrare la sicurezza nucleare fin dalle fondamenta dello sviluppo del settore in Serbia. Dalibor Arbutina, direttore generale dell’Azienda pubblica “Impianti Nucleari della Serbia”, ha definito il Memorandum una pietra miliare nella consolidata collaborazione con WINS, che ha già permesso al personale di acquisire competenze preziose e ora rafforzerà ulteriormente capacità tecniche e preparazione normativa.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa iniziativa apre nuove opportunità per le imprese italiane specializzate in infrastrutture energetiche, tecnologie per la sicurezza nucleare e servizi di consulenza tecnica nel settore energetico.

title_en: Chinese Haitian planning to expand factory in Ruma by additional 50,000 m2 - New jobs also announced at plastic injection molding machine production facility
title_it: Haitian espande fabbrica in Serbia
content_en: Ruma factory (Photo: Haitian International) Chinese company Haitian , one of the global leaders in the production of CNC machines and high-pressure plastic injection molding machines, plans to expand its production facility in Ruma by another 50,000 square meters in the second phase of the investment, the Ruma municipality announced. The new production complex is located in the "Rumska petlja" industrial zone, where more than 64,000 m2 of production space was built in the first phase on a total of 350,000 m2 of land. The factory has already entered trial production, and the first machines have been successfully placed on European markets, including Italy. Haitian currently employs around 100 workers in Ruma, while at full capacity the number of employees is expected to triple. The company announced that the expansion of production will also be accompanied by the development of the local supplier network, as well as cooperation with domestic subcontractors. - This is one of the most technologically advanced factories in Serbia. This is important not only for Ruma, but also for the entire country, because here we see technology for the 22nd century. Four years ago, when we had our first conversation with a Chinese investor, there was a field in this place, at "Rumska petlja", and today we have a factory that will very quickly improve Ruma, but also the entire country. The Haitian factory will be a major step forward for Serbia, primarily in terms of technological innovation. I can rightly say that this is the most significant investment in Ruma in the last four to five decades - said the President of the Municipality of Ruma, Dusan Ljubisic. He added that, while investors were improving production, the local government was improving business conditions in the Rumska petlja industrial zone. In the first half of next year, a second layer of asphalt will be laid in the work zone, thanks to funds from the Provincial Government. A training center will also be launched at the Technical School in Ruma for the needs of this and other investors. - The idea is that young people stay in their city and work, for a good salary, in the most technologically developed and advanced plants. The arrival of Haitian also implies higher salaries, as well as the engagement of subcontractors and local suppliers. Haitian will put Ruma on the world map of manufacturers of these machines and their arrival will show its real effects in the years to come - concluded Dusan Ljubisic. Opis: Kompanija Haitian Machinery u Rumi poseduje fabrički kompleks za proizvodnju industrijskih injekcionih mašina i mašina za sečenje i livenje. Kompleks je na parceli od oko 250.000 m2, a u planu je proizvodnja od ukupno 250 mašina godišnje. Vidi sve Opština Ruma Haitian Machinery Ruma d.o.o. content_it:
La multinazionale cinese Haitian, leader mondiale nella produzione di macchinari CNC e presse ad iniezione plastica ad alta pressione, prevede di espandere il proprio stabilimento a Ruma (Serbia) di ulteriori 50.000 metri quadrati nella seconda fase dell’investimento, come annunciato dal comune locale. Il complesso produttivo, situato nella zona industriale “Rumska petlja”, ha già completato la prima fase con oltre 64.000 m² di superficie produttiva su un’area totale di 350.000 m². Lo stabilimento ha avviato la produzione sperimentale e le prime macchine sono state commercializzate con successo sui mercati europei, tra cui l’Italia.

Attualmente Haitian impiega circa 100 lavoratori a Ruma, ma a regime la forza lavoro triplicherà. L’azienda prevede inoltre lo sviluppo di una rete di fornitori locali e collaborazioni con subfornitori serbi. Il sindaco di Ruma, Dušan Ljubišić, ha definito lo stabilimento “una delle fabbriche più tecnologicamente avanzate in Serbia”, sottolineandone il ruolo strategico per il Paese in termini di innovazione tecnologica e definendolo “l’investimento più significativo a Ruma negli ultimi 40-50 anni”.

Parallelamente agli investimenti privati, l’amministrazione locale sta migliorando le infrastrutture della zona industriale, con nuovi strati di asfalto previsti nel primo semestre del prossimo anno grazie a fondi provinciali. È inoltre in programma l’apertura di un centro di formazione presso la Scuola Tecnica di Ruma per rispondere alle esigenze di Haitian e di altri investitori. L’arrivo dell’azienda cinese, secondo le autorità locali, porterà a salari più elevati, maggiore occupazione e posizionerà Ruma sulla mappa globale dei produttori di macchinari per lo stampaggio a iniezione.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa espansione rappresenta un'opportunità per le imprese italiane del settore delle macchine utensili e della subfornitura industriale, date le già avviate esportazioni del gruppo cinese verso il mercato italiano e la crescente integrazione locale della produzione.

title_en: Nis soon to become National Center for Certification and Testing of Autonomous Vehicles and Drones
title_it: Niš centro nazionale per veicoli autonomi
content_en: Illustration (Photo: iSam iSmile/shutterstock.com) After the eighth E-mobility Forum was held at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Belgrade, organized by this faculty and the National Association for Autonomous and Electric Vehicles (NAAEV), Ivan Vulovic, President of the NAAEV Board of Directors, stated that the initiative to determine the status of the Smart Mobility Center - Nis project as a project of special importance for Serbia would be submitted to the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure in the coming days. As he explained, this project has been part of the Serbian Mobility Development Strategy and the accompanying Action Plan since its initiation in 2020 and, as such, is one of the key steps towards improving the country’s technological and industrial position. The central event was the signing of the Memorandum of Cooperation between the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and the renowned companies Bozankaya and Hybrid Innovations, which opened up new opportunities for joint projects, research and student internships in the field of electromobility. The Memorandum of Cooperation was signed by the Dean of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Dr. Vladimir Popovic, PhD, Vice President and CTO of Bozankaya Emrah Dal and Director of Hybrid Innovations Abdulhamid Yildirim. Emrah Dal emphasized the importance of the development of public urban transport, as well as strategic cooperation with the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, which is important for the advancement of innovation and the development of new technologies, as well as for the creation of professional staff who will lead the energy and technological transition in the region in the future. – The Faculty of Mechanical Engineering is the largest and oldest scientific and research institution in the field of mechanical engineering in the Balkans, and we are proud of our tradition. This year we enrolled 700 new students, which is a truly fantastic success in a complex year. We are a small country, but with a strong engineering tradition, knowledge and staff. The growing importance of electromobility is additionally emphasized by the current geopolitical circumstances and the challenges brought by the energy crisis – said Dean Popovic. Asked why Nis was recognized as an ideal location for the establishment of a national 5G/6G center for autonomous mobility, Popovic says that this city has a unique combination of prerequisites - a strong university and technical base, favorable traffic and infrastructure conditions, as well as an exceptional geostrategic position on Corridor 10, at the crossroads of roads connecting the four seas. These factors naturally position it as a potential national and regional center for testing, research and development of autonomous vehicles and drones. – In addition to a clear state strategy and rapid institutional support, it is necessary to strengthen the connection between the academic community and the economy, develop partnerships and implement innovative financing models. Such an approach would enable the attraction of investments, retention of young talents and accelerated growth of high-tech industries, along with the balanced technological development of Serbia – he says. As he adds, the development of “CPM-Nis” will contribute to the creation of highly qualified jobs in the fields of engineering, IT, energy, robotics and aerospace technologies, as well as the strengthening of startup ecosystems and industrial partnerships . – At the same time, the domestic economy gains access to testing, certification and validation capacities that currently do not exist in the region, which significantly increases its competitiveness and accelerates the implementation of innovations – says Popovic. By positioning “CPM–Nis” as a regional center for autonomous vehicles, drone technology and smart transport, conditions are created for attracting foreign partners and investments, he notes. – The center becomes a national hub for the development of autonomous, electric and smart mobility, opening up space for the development of green technologies and new business models in the field of transport and energy – emphasizes Popovic. In addition to reducing carbon dioxide (CO2) and PM particle emissions and improving traffic safety, the center will enable the wide application of drones in the public interest, from surveillance and space management to monitoring critical infrastructure and agriculture, to support security and emergency services . At the same time, the capacities of universities and educational institutions will be strengthened, regional cooperation will be improved and strategic infrastructure of national importance for the state, industry and the academic community will be built. The “CPM–Nis” project proposal has the potential to provide Serbia with an internationally recognizable role in the field of smart and autonomous mobility, with faster implementation, efficient use of funds, and a significant development effect for Nis and the entire country. content_it:
Dopo l'ottavo Forum sull'e-mobilità, tenutosi alla Facoltà di Ingegneria Meccanica di Belgrado e organizzato con l’Associazione Nazionale per Veicoli Autonomi ed Elettrici (NAAEV), il presidente del consiglio di amministrazione della NAAEV, Ivan Vulović, ha annunciato che nei prossimi giorni verrà presentata al Ministero delle Costruzioni, dei Trasporti e delle Infrastrutture la proposta di riconoscere il progetto “Smart Mobility Center – Niš” come di interesse strategico per la Serbia. Il progetto, parte integrante della Strategia serba per la Mobilità e del relativo Piano d’Azione dal 2020, rappresenta un passo fondamentale per rafforzare la posizione tecnologica e industriale del Paese.

Durante l’evento è stato firmato un Memorandum of Cooperation tra la Facoltà di Ingegneria Meccanica e le aziende Bozankaya e Hybrid Innovations, aprendo la strada a collaborazioni su progetti, ricerca e tirocini nel campo dell’elettromobilità. Il preside della facoltà, prof. Vladimir Popović, ha sottolineato la tradizione ingegneristica serba e l’importanza crescente dell’elettromobilità in un contesto di crisi energetica.

Niš è stata individuata come sede ideale grazie alla sua solida base universitaria, alle condizioni infrastrutturali favorevoli e alla posizione geostrategica sul Corridoio 10, crocevia tra quattro mari. Il progetto “CPM-Niš” mira a diventare un centro nazionale e regionale per la certificazione, il collaudo e lo sviluppo di veicoli autonomi, droni e tecnologie smart mobility, creando occupazione qualificata in ingegneria, IT, robotica e aerospazio.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, il centro permetterà all’economia serba di accedere a capacità di testing e validazione finora assenti nella regione, migliorando la competitività e accelerando l’innovazione. L’iniziativa punta anche a rafforzare il legame tra università e industria, attrarre investimenti esteri e sviluppare modelli green nel trasporto e nell’energia. Per le imprese italiane attive nei settori della mobilità sostenibile, aerospaziale, droni e infrastrutture intelligenti, si prospetta un’importante opportunità di collaborazione in un mercato in crescita con ambizioni europee.

title_en: Serbia to get first factory for production of “highly sophisticated drones” in spring
title_it: Prima fabbrica di droni sofisticati in Serbia
content_en: (Photo: iSam iSmile/shutterstock.com) The first large drone factory will open in Serbia at the end of March or beginning of April, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic announced, emphasizing that highly sophisticated drones would be manufactured there. – Soon, at the end of March, beginning of April, at the latest in 2026, I expect the opening of the first large drone factory in our country. I am proud to point out that these will be highly sophisticated drones, which we are working on with a major foreign power – he stated. He emphasized that it was not about Serbia’s Komarac 1 drone, which the country was otherwise satisfied with, or Komarac 2, but about highly sophisticated drones that they would work on, as he said, with a major foreign power. – There will be production here in Serbia – added Vucic. Let us remind that it was recently announced that the Czech military and mechanical industry holding CSG, which also operates in Serbia, had purchased a majority stake in the Serbian manufacturer of engines for unmanned aerial vehicles MUST Solutions . content_it: La prima grande fabbrica di droni aprirà in Serbia alla fine di marzo o all’inizio di aprile, ha annunciato il presidente serbo Aleksandar Vučić, sottolineando che vi saranno prodotti droni “altamente sofisticati”. “Presto, entro la fine di marzo o l’inizio di aprile, al più tardi nel 2026, prevedo l’apertura della prima grande fabbrica di droni nel nostro Paese. Sono orgoglioso di sottolineare che si tratterà di droni altamente sofisticati, sviluppati in collaborazione con una grande potenza straniera”, ha dichiarato. title_en: New Yugo and Stojadin to be presented at EXPO 2027
title_it: Nuovo Yugo e Stojadin all'EXPO 2027
content_en: (Photo: Pixabay.com/Qimono) Aleksandar Bjelic from Globo Company and graphic designer Darko Marceta have announced that in two years they will present a prototype of the renewed automobile brand Yugo at the specialized exhibition EXPO 2027 in Belgrade, which will be in running condition. Car collector and new owner of the rights to the name and model Yugo Aleksandar Bjelic wants to protect the name and bring it back to the roads. Born in Germany and never lived in the former Yugoslavia or Serbia. A Serb by origin, and as a collector of classic and sports cars, and of course Zastava vehicles, he decided to initiate the protection of the Zastava brand himself with the ultimate goal of bringing back Yugo, not only as a brand, but also as a vehicle. Designer Darako Marceta helped him with this, and the first Yugo will be ready for Expo 27. – We presented the model in Munich at the designer fair, and that was a big step for the entire project. We received positive comments and that is the reason why we can continue with the project – Darko Marceta points out. Some more big news, the same team has also renovated the Zastava 101. Work is being accelerated on the project so that this model can also be found at Expo 2027, and the new Stojadin has a completely new interior and exterior design. For now, this team is looking for a factory that will produce these models, and Egypt is also mentioned, where Zastava had its own car assembly plants and where it was very successful in production. The recipe is clear: the new “ace,” as many people popularly call it, will be cheap and affordable, and its electrification is also planned. – The next step is two more models. Negotiations are underway with manufacturers who could produce it. The prototype is being made in Zrenjanin – adds Marceta. The interior and exterior are in line with trends, but still much more modest than in Chinese models. It is more traditional. It is interesting that our neighbors, the Croats, are extremely interested in this model and most of their portals write that the Zastava 128 is returning in full glory. content_it:
Aleksandar Bjelić della Globo Company e il designer Darko Marčeta hanno annunciato che tra due anni presenteranno un prototipo funzionante del rinnovato marchio automobilistico Yugo all’EXPO 2027 a Belgrado. Bjelić, collezionista di automobili e nuovo titolare dei diritti sul nome e sul modello Yugo, intende proteggere il marchio e riportarlo sulle strade. Nato in Germania e di origine serba, ha deciso di avviare personalmente la tutela del marchio Zastava, con l’obiettivo di rilanciare il Yugo non solo come brand ma anche come veicolo reale. 

Il progetto ha già ottenuto riscontri positivi, tra cui la presentazione del modello alla fiera del design di Monaco. Lo stesso team sta inoltre rinnovando il modello Zastava 101, ora denominato Stojadin, con un design completamente nuovo per interni ed esterni, da presentare anch’esso all’EXPO 2027. 

Attualmente, il team è alla ricerca di uno stabilimento produttivo; tra le opzioni citate figura anche l’Egitto, dove Zastava in passato gestiva impianti di assemblaggio con successo. Il nuovo veicolo sarà economico e accessibile, con prevista anche una versione elettrificata. Il prototipo è in fase di realizzazione a Zrenjanin, e sono già in corso trattative con potenziali produttori per altri due modelli. L’interesse per il progetto è particolarmente vivo in Croazia, dove i media parlano del ritorno glorioso della Zastava 128. 

Come riportato da ekapija.com, il progetto potrebbe offrire opportunità alle aziende italiane attive nel settore automotive, in particolare nei comparti di design, componentistica e tecnologie per la mobilità elettrica.
