content_it:
La ministra serba dell’Energia e delle Miniere, Dubravka Đedović Handanović, ha dichiarato che la priorità del governo è assicurare un approvvigionamento affidabile e continuo di prodotti petroliferi sul mercato interno, in attesa della risposta dell’amministrazione statunitense riguardo alle sanzioni contro la NIS.  

La ministra ha incontrato rappresentanti di MOL Serbia, EKO Serbia, OMV Serbia e del Segretario generale dell’Associazione delle compagnie petrolifere della Serbia per discutere la stabilità dell’approvvigionamento. “Il nostro obbligo è garantire che ogni stazione di servizio, cliente all’ingrosso e cittadino disponga di carburante a sufficienza per le proprie esigenze – ha affermato, secondo quanto riportato dal ministero – Le aziende con cui ho parlato sono fondamentali per la stabilità dell’offerta, poiché sono i principali importatori di prodotti petroliferi in Serbia e riforniscono la maggior parte del mercato dopo NIS”.

Ha sottolineato che le importazioni di derivati petroliferi a dicembre seguiranno la domanda di mercato, la logistica e le capacità disponibili, con l’aspettativa che tutto avvenga secondo i piani per mantenere stabile l’offerta. In caso di necessità, lo Stato è pronto a utilizzare le riserve obbligatorie di prodotti petroliferi.

Per rafforzare ulteriormente la sicurezza dell’approvvigionamento, sono previsti l’arrivo di 20.000 tonnellate di gasolio Euro e 38.000 tonnellate di benzina tra dicembre e gennaio destinate alle riserve strategiche nazionali. La ministra ha inoltre evidenziato l’importanza della pianificazione strategica e dei colloqui diplomatici in corso con Paesi vicini e istituzioni UE per aumentare le forniture regionali destinate al mercato serbo. Sono stati elaborati diversi scenari operativi in relazione alle sanzioni statunitensi su NIS, entrate in vigore il 9 ottobre, e il governo è pronto ad agire per preservare la stabilità del mercato durante le trattative in corso sul futuro della società.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa situazione potrebbe aprire opportunità per aziende italiane operanti nel settore petrolifero e nella logistica energetica, qualora si rendessero necessarie nuove fonti di approvvigionamento o partnership strategiche.

title_en: Contractors selected for development of preliminary design for reconstruction of wastewater treatment plant in Velika Plana
title_it: Gara assegnata per depuratore di Velika Plana
content_en: (Photo: Ivan Bandura/unsplash) The Velika Plana Municipal Administration has awarded the contract for the development of a preliminary design and obtaining location requirements for the expansion and reconstruction of the central wastewater treatment plant in the Velika Plana settlement. The job was entrusted to a group of bidders consisting of Geodetski biro Gaus from Pinosava and Enviro System doo from Belgrade. The value of the contract is 11.4 million dinars including VAT. The contract includes the development of a preliminary design for the expansion and/or reconstruction of the central wastewater treatment plant, as well as the complete obtaining of location requirements as the first phase of the municipal infrastructure improvement project. content_it: L’Amministrazione comunale di Velika Plana ha assegnato il contratto per la redazione del progetto preliminare e l’ottenimento dei requisiti urbanistici necessari all’ampliamento e alla ricostruzione dell’impianto centrale di trattamento delle acque reflue nel centro abitato di Velika Plana. L’incarico è stato affidato a un raggruppamento temporaneo composto da Geodetski biro Gaus di Pinosava ed Enviro System doo di Belgrado. Il valore del contratto ammonta a 11,4 milioni di dinari IVA inclusa. L’intervento prevede la redazione del progetto preliminare per l’ampliamento e/o la ricostruzione dell’impianto di depurazione, nonché l’intero iter per ottenere i requisiti di localizzazione, costituendo la prima fase di un più ampio progetto di miglioramento delle infrastrutture comunali, come riportato da ekapija.com. Tale iniziativa potrebbe offrire opportunità alle imprese italiane specializzate in tecnologie per il trattamento delle acque reflue e nella progettazione di infrastrutture idriche.

title_en: Innovations, autonomous systems and energy of the future at the VIII E-Mobility Forum
title_it: Forum E-Mobility: innovazione e mobilità sostenibile
content_en: Ivan Vulovic (Photo: Mašinski fakultet u Beogradu) Organized by the National Association of Autonomous and Electric Vehicles (NAAEV) and the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade, the VIII E-Mobility Forum will be held on November 26 and 27, dedicated to modern mobility, autonomous systems and technological innovations. The program also includes the third Student Innovative Mobility Challenge (SIM-C), a competition of student teams from Serbia, which will once again present the most creative solutions in the field of future mobility. At the opening ceremony of the Forum, the audience will be addressed by professor Vladimir Popovic, PhD, Dean of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, and Ivan Vulovic, President of the NAAEV Board of Directors, as well as H.E. Ilhan Saygili, Ambassador of the Republic of Turkey to Serbia. Professor Vladimir Popovic, PhD (Photo: Mašinski fakultet u Beogradu) The first panel of the forum will be dedicated to the role of Serbia as a regional center of scientific and technological innovations, with a special focus on Nis as a city of smart mobility, but also how cities and institutions are positioning themselves in the development of new technologies and infrastructure solutions that will shape the transport of the future. The panel “Academy - SIM Challenge 2025” will present innovative solutions from student teams, as well as the experiences of the winners of previous cycles of the competition. Within this part of the program, the winners of this year’s SIM Challenge will also be announced, which further encourages the development of young talents and their inclusion in modern technological trends. A special address in this part will be given by a representative of EUTA / European Training Academy, who will provide students with useful information on the possibility of participation and how to manage projects financed from EU funds. Panels with many interesting topics (Photo: Mašinski fakultet u Beogradu) On the second day, the panel titled “Autonomous Systems - Vehicles, Robotics and Algorithm Responsibility” focuses on the transformation of the industry through robotics, automation and the improvement of driver assistance systems, as well as responsibility at a time when algorithms are increasingly taking over decision-making processes. “Connected Mobility - Cybersecurity, Interoperability and Data Management,” is the topic of the panel on the security aspects of modern networks, data protection in electric vehicles and the challenges that smart vehicles bring in the sphere of information security, emphasizing the importance of digital security in the era of connected mobility. The last topic of this year’s Forum is “Future Mobility and Energy,” where the role of renewable energy sources in the development of electromobility, the integration of green hydrogen into public transport and modern infrastructure solutions for charging electric vehicles in smart cities will be discussed. This panel aims to connect the vision of energy transition with solutions that directly impact urban transport and sustainable development. 2024 winning team Beoavia (Photo: Mašinski fakultet u Beogradu) Over the course of two days, participants will have the opportunity to learn about the latest technological achievements, innovations and research in the fields of electromobility, autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, robotics and urban mobility. This year’s Forum is supported by the exclusive sponsor “Hybrid Innovations,” “Star Import/Keos” as the premium sponsor, “Vlatacom Institute,” “Elektroprivreda Srbije,” “Inmold Group,” “Belgrade Waterfront,” “Hyundai Serbia,” “Dualtron Serbia,” “Dekra,” “ABB,” “Delta Motors” as official sponsors. The panel discussions will enable an interactive exchange of opinions and experiences and a unique opportunity for direct networking with industry leaders, decision-makers, the startup community and the academic sector. The VIII E-Mobility Forum once again confirms its role in promoting sustainable and smart mobility, bringing together experts who are shaping the future of transport. L’VIII Forum E-Mobility si terrà a Belgrado il 26 e 27 novembre, organizzato dall’Associazione Nazionale dei Veicoli Autonomi ed Elettrici (NAAEV) e dalla Facoltà di Ingegneria Meccanica dell’Università di Belgrado. L’evento è dedicato alla mobilità moderna, ai sistemi autonomi e alle innovazioni tecnologiche. Sarà ospitata anche la terza edizione della Student Innovative Mobility Challenge (SIM-C), competizione tra team universitari serbi per presentare soluzioni creative nel campo della mobilità futura.

All’inaugurazione interverranno il professor Vladimir Popović, preside della Facoltà di Ingegneria Meccanica, Ivan Vulović, presidente del consiglio direttivo della NAAEV, e l’ambasciatore della Repubblica di Turchia in Serbia, S.E. Ilhan Saygili.

Il primo panel esplorerà il ruolo della Serbia come centro regionale di innovazione scientifica e tecnologica, con particolare attenzione a Niš come città della mobilità intelligente. Un altro panel, “Academy – SIM Challenge 2025”, presenterà le soluzioni innovative degli studenti e i risultati delle edizioni precedenti, annunciando i vincitori dell’edizione 2024. Un rappresentante della European Training Academy fornirà inoltre informazioni utili agli studenti sulle opportunità di partecipazione a progetti finanziati dall’UE.

Il secondo giorno sarà dedicato a temi come i sistemi autonomi (robotica, automazione e responsabilità algoritmica), la mobilità connessa (cybersecurity, interoperabilità e gestione dei dati) e il legame tra mobilità futura ed energia, con focus su energie rinnovabili, idrogeno verde nei trasporti pubblici e infrastrutture di ricarica nelle smart city.

Numerosi sponsor sostengono l’evento, tra cui “Hybrid Innovations” (sponsor esclusivo), “Star Import/Keos” (premium sponsor), EPS, Vlatacom, Hyundai Serbia, ABB, Dekra e altri. Il Forum rappresenta un’occasione unica per lo scambio di idee tra esperti, decisori, startup e accademia, rafforzando la Serbia come hub per la mobilità sostenibile e intelligente, come riportato da ekapija.com. La manifestazione offre potenziali opportunità di collaborazione per aziende italiane attive nei settori della mobilità elettrica, delle energie rinnovabili e delle infrastrutture smart.

title_en: Marko Vucetić, Director of the Serbian IT Association: From Turbulence to Stabilization - How to Keep the IT Sector in Serbia Competitive?
title_it: Ripresa e sfide per l'IT serbo
content_en: (Photo: Goran Zlatković) After turbulent years marked by a drop in employment and instability in the IT sector market in Serbia, the situation in 2025 shows signs of stabilization, with slight growth and companies adapting to new technologies, in particular artificial intelligence. The number of job advertisements in previous years recorded drastic drops, but the latest data indicate a slowdown in this trend and a gradual return of demand for IT professionals. Companies are increasingly investing in new technologies and adapting business processes, thereby striving to remain competitive on the domestic and international markets. We talked about the market situation with Marko Vučetić, director of the Serbian IT Association, who points out that the key to stability and further development of the sector is investment in talent, especially young developers, as well as creating a predictable business environment. According to him, our IT experts are the true treasure of the country, because they not only start companies with their knowledge, experience and innovation, but also set new standards on the labor market, like flexible work and additional benefits. At the same time, a stable tax system enables the attraction of foreign investments and long-term planning, which gives Serbia the opportunity to position itself as a competitive IT destination in the region and beyond. How would you describe the current state of the IT industry in Serbia? Where are we in relation to previous years? - I would say that the current situation is slightly better, especially when looking at employment websites. In 2023, employment was drastically reduced compared to 2022, the number of ads fell by 50% in 2023. Then, in 2024, in comparison to 2023, the drop was another 30%. In the course of 2025, we also note a decrease, but significantly smaller, up to 5%. It`s not dramatic. At the global level as well, statistics show a slight increase in employment. After a decrease in the number of ads in 2023, minimal growth is recorded in 2024, but that trend cannot quickly return to the level of 2021 when there were many ads. In your opinion, what are the biggest challenges that IT companies in Serbia are facing today? - The first challenge is AI. Companies are reallocating budgets to new AI teams and projects, as well as on data analytics and cyber security, which has become a serious topic due to the increase in cyber attacks in recent years. And the biggest challenge of the domestic market is to remain price competitive, which enables new projects, employment and attraction of new companies. Our competitors now are countries such as Poland, Romania and Bulgaria. Globally, many countries are implementing systems that attract IT companies, and our association is working to ensure that the market of Serbia remains affordable and attractive for new investments. This summer, the government abolished the Decree on incentives for employers who employ newly settled persons. Were there consequences for the business of IT companies in Serbia? - These changes have certainly affected IT companies and they have spoiled the image of the predictable tax system we must insist on. They also increased the cost of labor, which is very important to explain in the community. Therefore, we do not insist on reducing the wages of employees, on the contrary, we want wages to rise. But at the same time we have to establish a stable and competitive system, which can compete with other countries. We cannot be more expensive than Poland, which is a member of the European Union, well positioned and has quality talents. We need to know where we stand in the market, and consistently work in that position and generate income and profit based on that. What is the situation when it comes to personnel in the IT sector in Serbia, that we are competitive enough to retain local talent? - We did not record a migration of our developers from the market. We have foreign IT experts who are relocating to us and a certain number of foreigners who are leaving Serbia, but that number is not significant for now. However, you have to be careful and take care of it - our people are mostly  staying for now, which is extremely important. As an association, we will try to create a market that, if not ideal, will at least be stable and favorable for our developers. I like to say that our developers are the true treasure of this state - with their knowledge, experience and what they do, they make a huge contribution. They actually introduced some new trends to the labor market, such as working from home, additional benefits and flexibility, which then began to be adopted by other industries. How ready are IT companies in Serbia for the next phase of digital transformation, especially when we are talking about artificial intelligence compared to the world and European market? - I have to admit that I don`t have precise statistics - we didn`t do research, but we notice that a lot of investment is being made. This must certainly be a priority, both through the association and within the companies themselves, because adapting to AI is key, not only for individuals, but also for companies themselves. The more ready they are to work with AI tools and implement them in systems, the more competitive they will be in the market. Without AI, we can only lag behind in the future. This is exactly where I see the biggest opportunity - we have extremely high-quality and capable engineers, and this is a chance to advance as an IT community and to position ourselves on the global technology scene. How do you see the future of the IT sector in Serbia, what is most important for further development? - For further development of the IT sector, two things are most important: investment in talent, especially young developers, and a predictable tax system. Foreign investors must have clear documentation for the next five years in order to be able to plan their business. A predictable system is key to Serbia`s competitiveness in the global battle for large corporations. We have to make progress on that front, and we invest significant effort in this, not only me as the director of the Association, but also our Board of Directors and all members involved in working groups. Ivana Žikić Srpska IT asocijacija Serbian IT Association Marko Vučetić IT market Digitization special edition newsletter Click to success Fast Digital Smart Your comment Send
content_it:
Dopo anni turbolenti segnati da un calo occupazionale e instabilità nel mercato IT in Serbia, il 2025 mostra segnali di stabilizzazione, con una lieve crescita e un’adeguamento delle aziende alle nuove tecnologie, in particolare l’intelligenza artificiale. Se negli anni precedenti gli annunci di lavoro erano crollati drasticamente – con un calo del 50% nel 2023 rispetto al 2022 e un ulteriore -30% nel 2024 – nel 2025 il declino si è ridotto a circa il 5%, indicando una graduale ripresa della domanda di professionisti IT.

Marko Vučetić, direttore della Serbian IT Association, sottolinea che la chiave per la stabilità e lo sviluppo futuro del settore risiede negli investimenti nei talenti, soprattutto giovani sviluppatori, e nella creazione di un ambiente imprenditoriale prevedibile. Gli esperti IT serbi, definiti “il vero tesoro del Paese”, non solo avviano imprese innovative, ma introducono nuovi standard sul mercato del lavoro, come il lavoro flessibile e benefici aggiuntivi.

Tra le principali sfide attuali vi è l’adeguamento all’AI, con le aziende che riallocano budget verso progetti legati all’intelligenza artificiale, all’analisi dati e alla cybersecurity. Parallelamente, è cruciale mantenere la competitività dei costi rispetto a Paesi come Polonia, Romania e Bulgaria. La recente abolizione del decreto sugli incentivi per i datori di lavoro che assumono persone trasferitesi in Serbia ha però minato la percezione di stabilità fiscale, aumentando i costi del lavoro.

Nonostante ciò, non si registra una fuga significativa di talenti locali, anzi, alcuni esperti stranieri si trasferiscono in Serbia. La prontezza delle aziende serbe ad adottare strumenti basati sull’AI è considerata fondamentale per non rimanere indietro a livello globale. La Serbia, grazie alla qualità dei suoi ingegneri, ha un’opportunità concreta per posizionarsi sulla scena tecnologica internazionale.

Per il futuro, secondo Vučetić, sono essenziali due fattori: investire nei talenti e garantire un sistema fiscale stabile e prevedibile, condizione indispensabile per attrarre investimenti esteri e pianificare strategie a lungo termine, come riportato da ekapija.com. Le imprese italiane operanti nel settore informatico e dei servizi tecnologici potrebbero cogliere opportunità di collaborazione con un ecosistema IT serbo in ripresa, caratterizzato da talenti qualificati e costi ancora competitivi.

title_en: Interactive AI Ecosystem Map presented – Serbia’s AI potential in one place
title_it: Mappa interattiva dell'ecosistema AI serbo
content_en: Illustration (Photo: jamesteohart/shutterstock.com) The Office for IT and eGovernment, in cooperation with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), has presented an interactive map of the AI ecosystem of the Republic of Serbia, which shows all the key actors shaping the development of AI in Serbia and their initiatives in one place. Unified data from multiple sources The map integrates data from multiple relevant sources, including data from the Digital Serbia Initiative on domestic AI startups, data on AI projects supported by the Science Fund and the Innovation Fund, as well as data on AI and innovation ecosystem actors and the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, the office announced. All of this data is additionally classified and marked by a number of parameters, from the typology of organizations and projects, to technologies, industries and geographical areas, and interconnected. This allows users to easily independently search, filter and analyze the domestic AI ecosystem from different angles - or use one of 20 predefined views of the domestic AI ecosystem. The strategic importance of AI for the development of Serbia Speaking about the importance of creating the Map of the AI Ecosystem of Serbia, the Director of the Office for IT and eGovernment, Mihailo Jovanovic, emphasized that it was another step in the continuous development of artificial intelligence in Serbia. – The Government of the Republic of Serbia has clearly demonstrated its commitment to the development and application of artificial intelligence by adopting the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence for the Period 2025–2030 and the Ethical Guidelines for its Reliable Development and Use. Mapping the AI ecosystem further strengthens this foundation, as it enables better coordination of all stakeholders, from state institutions and scientific organizations to startups and the private sector, and thus lays the foundation for accelerated technological and social progress – Jovanovic emphasized. Call for community input Although comprehensive, the map is a first pilot version, which will be continuously updated and improved. The domestic AI ecosystem is rapidly developing, so the authors emphasize the importance of community feedback. – Although the map was originally created for the internal planning needs of UNDP and the Office for IT and eGovernment in the field of AI implementation in the public sector, we believed that it could have broader value. That is why we decided to publish it not only as an interactive visualization, but also to make the complete dataset behind it freely available – said Slobodan Markovic, Digital Technology Advisor at UNDP. He invited domestic researchers, companies and organizations to use the map, test its capabilities and send suggestions so that it can be further developed into a common community resource and help in planning new AI initiatives. content_it:
L’Ufficio per le Tecnologie dell’Informazione e l’e-Government della Serbia, in collaborazione con il Programma delle Nazioni Unite per lo Sviluppo (UNDP), ha presentato una mappa interattiva dell’ecosistema nazionale sull’intelligenza artificiale. Lo strumento raccoglie in un unico spazio tutti i principali attori e le loro iniziative nel campo dell’AI in Serbia.

La mappa integra dati provenienti da diverse fonti rilevanti: l’Iniziativa Digitale Serbia sui startup nazionali specializzati in AI, i progetti finanziati dal Fondo per la Scienza e dal Fondo per l’Innovazione, nonché informazioni sugli attori dell’ecosistema dell’innovazione, compresa la Camera di Commercio serba. I dati sono classificati e indicizzati secondo vari parametri – tipologia di organizzazioni e progetti, tecnologie, settori industriali e aree geografiche – e interconnessi tra loro. Ciò consente agli utenti di esplorare, filtrare e analizzare autonomamente l’ecosistema AI da molteplici prospettive o di utilizzare una delle 20 visualizzazioni predefinite.

Mihailo Jovanovic, Direttore dell’Ufficio per le TI e l’e-Government, ha sottolineato che questa iniziativa rappresenta un ulteriore passo nella strategia serba per lo sviluppo dell’AI, rafforzata dall’adozione della “Strategia per lo Sviluppo dell’Intelligenza Artificiale 2025–2030” e delle relative “Linee Guida Etiche”. La mappa, ha aggiunto, favorisce il coordinamento tra istituzioni pubbliche, enti scientifici, startup e imprese, creando le basi per un progresso tecnologico e sociale accelerato.

Slobodan Markovic, Consulente per le Tecnologie Digitali dell’UNDP, ha precisato che, sebbene inizialmente pensata per esigenze interne di pianificazione, la mappa è stata resa pubblica sia come visualizzazione interattiva che con l’intero dataset disponibile gratuitamente. Si tratta di una versione pilota, destinata a essere aggiornata con il contributo della comunità, che invita ricercatori, aziende e organizzazioni a testarla e inviare suggerimenti per trasformarla in una risorsa comune a supporto di nuove iniziative nel settore AI, come riportato da ekapija.com.

L’iniziativa rappresenta un'opportunità per le imprese italiane del settore informatico e dei servizi tecnici di esplorare collaborazioni con l’emergente ecosistema serbo dell’intelligenza artificiale.

title_en: Center for Digital Transformation of CCIS – From Digitalizing the Economy to the Global Recognition of Serbian Startups
title_it: Serbia punta sulle startup digitali
content_en: (Photo: Zapp2Photo/ shutterstock.com) By establishing the Center for Digital Transformation , we set a clear mission for ourselves: to help the Serbian economy - especially micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises - keep pace with global technological changes. Today, digitalization is not a luxury but a prerequisite for survival. Companies that adopt new technologies become faster, more efficient, more accurate, and more competitive; they reduce costs, increase customer satisfaction, and open new business models. This is why, from day one, the CDT’s goal has been to provide systematic support that enables companies to understand, implement, and leverage digitalization in a way that delivers real, measurable results. Over the years, we have built the most structured support model in the region. With more than 7,000 registered companies, over 1,000 completed digital transformation processes, ISO 17024-certified consultants, a Digital Academy, a database of verified IT vendors, and the first AI program for SMEs - all of this has made digital transformation accessible and measurable. We have worked with companies from nearly every sector, helping them adopt new technologies and keep pace with the global market. In this process, we realized that Serbia not only has enormous potential for digital transformation but also possesses talent capable of developing advanced technological solutions that can compete on the global stage. That is why, in addition to supporting the traditional economy, we have opened a new chapter - providing domestic startups with systematic and strategic support to grow in international markets. Our international journey began at the Web Summit in 2024 , where we jointly presented, for the first time, our vision for the global recognition of Serbia’s innovation ecosystem. This was followed by a series of GITEX visits throughout the year - from Morocco, through Singapore and Berlin, all the way to Dubai and GITEX Global. In each of these markets, Serbian startups demonstrated exceptional knowledge, potential, and readiness to compete with the best. They won pitch competitions, attracted the attention of investors, and achieved results that confirm Serbia has innovative teams deserving of a global stage. This cycle of international activities continued with our return to the Web Summit in Lisbon , where we appeared as an ecosystem that is no longer breaking through - but becoming recognized. In addition, GITEX Serbia 2027 has been confirmed, an event that will, for the first time, bring one of the world’s largest technology platforms to our country and open entirely new opportunities for the domestic economy and startups. According to the European Commission’s report, Serbia is recognized as one of the most innovative countries in this part of Europe, with innovation results reaching 51.5% of the EU average in 2025. This places Serbia 31st among EU and neighboring countries, above the average of emerging EU nations. Through the Scale Up mission, we aim to serve as a bridge connecting domestic innovative teams with the largest international markets, events, investors, and partners. CDT remains an institution supporting the traditional economy through digital transformation, but today, alongside that, it also opens doors for startups - enabling them to grow faster, connect with the global ecosystem, and compete shoulder to shoulder with the best. If in previous years we helped companies in Serbia enhance their operations through digitalization, today we are helping our startups take the next step - to enter the international stage, secure their place in the global innovation economy, and demonstrate that Serbia possesses the potential, talent, and vision recognized worldwide. content_it:
Con la creazione del Centro per la Trasformazione Digitale (CDT), la Camera di Commercio serba si è data la missione di sostenere l’economia nazionale, in particolare le micro, piccole e medie imprese, nell’adattamento alle sfide tecnologiche globali. La digitalizzazione è ormai una condizione indispensabile per la competitività: riduce i costi, migliora l’efficienza e apre a nuovi modelli di business.  

Negli anni, il CDT ha sviluppato il modello di supporto più strutturato della regione, con oltre 7.000 aziende registrate e più di 1.000 processi di trasformazione digitale completati. Il centro dispone di consulenti certificati ISO 17024, una Digital Academy, un database di fornitori IT verificati e il primo programma basato sull’intelligenza artificiale per le PMI.  

Parallelamente, è emersa la volontà di valorizzare l’ecosistema innovativo nazionale. Il CDT ha così avviato un programma mirato a sostenere le startup serbe nei mercati internazionali, partecipando a eventi globali come il Web Summit 2024 a Lisbona e le fiere GITEX in Marocco, Singapore, Berlino e Dubai. Le startup serbe si sono distinte per competenze, potenziale e capacità di attrarre investitori.  

È già confermata la prima edizione di GITEX Serbia nel 2027, che porterà nel Paese una delle principali piattaforme tecnologiche mondiali. Secondo la Commissione Europea, nel 2025 la Serbia ha raggiunto il 51,5% della media UE in termini di risultati innovativi, posizionandosi al 31° posto tra Paesi UE e vicini, superando la media delle nazioni emergenti.  

Il CDT, pur continuando a supportare la trasformazione digitale delle imprese tradizionali, ora funge anche da ponte tra le startup nazionali e i mercati globali. Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’obiettivo è consentire alle imprese innovative serbe di consolidare la propria presenza nell’economia globale dell’innovazione. Tale sviluppo apre opportunità di collaborazione per le aziende italiane attive nel digitale, nell’ICT e nei servizi tecnologici avanzati.

title_en: Montenegrin startups shone at the largest European technology conference - Domestic innovations in focus of investors at Web Summit in Lisbon
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: (Photo: Privredna komora Crne Gore) Montenegrin startups attracted great interest from potential investors at the prestigious international technology event Web Summit 2025, which was recently held in Lisbon. The appearance of domestic companies was organized for the first time by the Chamber of Commerce of Montenegro (PKCG), and startups Bucketora , GoGrant, Gold Bear Technologies, Limo express, LoRaSi , My turn , Pillbie and Skenify presented modern solutions from various fields and showed that Montenegro has the knowledge, creativity and potential to be recognized as a technologically innovative destination. Skenify, an AI platform for cyber security aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises in the European market, is one of the solutions presented in Lisbon that confirms that Montenegro can offer competitive innovations in the extremely attractive and rapidly growing cyber security sector. - Cyber ​​security is currently in great focus in Montenegro and a lot is being done to raise its level, both in the private and state sectors. We from the private sector are trying to innovate to help companies, but also the state, to raise that level of security to a higher level as soon as possible - said Branko Džakula, CEO of Secfix, which is behind the Skenify platform. The startup LoRaS i was founded by father and son, Milan and Danilo Marić, and the company is dedicated to developing digital twins through innovative technologies. As the company`s founder and CEO Milan Marić said, their focus is on the development of the Internet of Things (IoT). - We are developing sensors that collect data from the power grid and show us its condition. That is, in essence, the idea that we are trying to promote here - to prevent energy outages such as occurred in the previous period. This is just preparation for the real appearance we will have next year at Web Summit. We are now in the ascendant period of startup development when we are testing our idea and we want to see how it is reacted to. Next year, we will present the product at this same fair, and I expect this to be just a warm-up for next year - he said. Danilo Marić stated that participation in the summit is an opportunity to see what other startups are doing in Europe, but also in the world, and to check how innovative their idea is. - Let`s see how widely it is used in the industry and what exactly investors are interested in, and what is the best way to bring our idea closer to them and ultimately get investments and funds from them. After meetings with investors, we realized that the idea is quite innovative - we focused on energy network monitoring, anomaly detection and performance improvement from that network, but the solution is polyvalent and applicable in other branches of industry. This solution is very scalable and can serve to create a regional or European energy network for energy and information exchange - said Danilo Marić. Although he is visiting Web Summit for the fifth time, Batrić Krvavac presented his startup Pillbie for the first time at the Montenegrin stand. The company is developing a medication dispenser that organizes doses, monitors usage and provides light and sound reminders for correct and timely administration of therapy. - Our product is intended for monitoring the correct intake and adherence to medical therapy and we have been developing it for several years. The summit was an opportunity to present our new application, our new prototype to the European market and eventually to meet potential partners and investors. Given that this is the biggest technological event in Europe, if not wider, I think that the presence of companies from Montenegro is crucial for the further development of our innovative community. I think it is imperative that Montenegrin startups meet at every upcoming Web Summit - Krvavac pointed out. Startup MyTurn develops a solution, i.e. an application that helps parents to delegate household tasks to children in an easier and nicer way. - We have a solution that enables them to assign tasks in a quick way, and the children, on the other hand, see them as some kind of game that they do in real life. We have the largest number of users from Montenegro, but we want to reach as many users as possible outside the territory of the Western Balkans, so participation in this conference means a lot to us. Also, the support of the Chamber of Commerce is of great importance and the fact that in recent years it recognizes innovative companies and provides them with the opportunity to participate in precisely such events, which mean a lot to us in order to reach users and real partners, and to connect with investors. Web Summit is a platform that allows you to reach all actors in our innovative eco-system - said the representative of the startup MyTurn, Milica Matović. GoldBear Technologies presented a global SaaS product for the limo/VIP transport industry — LimoExpress — at the summit. - We develop an enterprise solution for limo agencies that offer VIP transport around the world. We`ve been working on this project for two and a half years, we`ve been on the market for a year and we already have close to 200 clients. These are companies from all over the world, from Australia, through Dubai, Europe and America. Participating in the summit gave us an opportunity to see what new technologies we can implement and where the SaaS industry is going in general. Coming to the Web Summit is of great importance for us in order to create connections with other SaaS founders, to see their experiences, to look for branding partners, and to raise the brand of our product in the world and to learn about new technologies, specifically in the field of artificial intelligence, in order to implement them in our product - said CEO of GoldBear Technologies Nemanja Nikolić. (Photo: Privredna komora Crne Gore) In Lisbon, Bucketora was also presented - an event-based travel platform that allows users to find inspiring events around the world and plan their entire trip - from flights and accommodation to local activities and socializing. - In Montenegro, tourism is one of the most important branches of the economy, and I think that startups that deal with hospitality or any other field of tourism are also very important. I think that their representation can contribute to Montenegro as a country that, in my opinion, has quality staff and people who can present very great ideas. Such summits, in addition to presenting ideas, are very important for networking and finding investments for startups in whatever phase they are in - said Čedomir Burić, representative of Bucketor startups. The attention of visitors to the Montenegrin stand was also attracted by the start-up GoGrant - an AI platform that automates the process of public calls and grants, making them faster, more transparent and more efficient for institutions, donors and foundations. - This is an idea that arose out of a real need in Montenegrin society itself to digitize public procurements and to shorten the application process for those public procurements. At the Web Summit, we want to spread the idea to all countries in the region. We have partners from the region with whom we have already made contact in order to break into those markets as easily as possible. The support of the Chamber of Commerce is important to us, because without them we would not be ready for this kind of summit at this moment - said Milan Marković, co-founder of the company Web Falcon , which is behind the GoGrant startup. The appearance of Montenegrin startups at a joint stand at the prestigious international technological event Web Summit 2025 in Lisbon was an opportunity for domestic innovators to exchange experiences and form partnerships with investors and colleagues from more than 150 countries. The importance of this presentation of Montenegrin startups was also pointed out by the president of the Chamber of Commerce of Montenegro, Nina Drakić. - This event gathers over 70,000 participants from over 150 countries of the world and the participation of Montenegrin startups in it is an exceptional opportunity to improve the visibility of the Montenegrin startup community on the international stage, for domestic startups to find new investors, new partners and to improve the innovative startup community in Montenegro. The Montenegrin innovation community really has the knowledge, potential and creativity to participate in these kinds of events. Through new solutions and innovations, startups contribute to business improvement, simplification of processes, greater efficiency, and this is very important for the diversification of our economy and its further development - said Drakić. In addition to the performance of seven startups at the joint stand, the Chamber of Commerce also organized the visit of 17 other companies from Montenegro to this world technological event. The Web Summit has gathered more than 70,000 participants from over 150 countries and is considered one of the world`s leading technology conferences - a place where technology leaders, innovators, investors and decision makers exchange ideas and build partnerships. The Web Summit also provided exceptional networking opportunities with numerous breakout sessions, exhibit areas, panels, investor meetings, and additional post-conference events. title_en: Digital support for the economy - JKT portal enables faster business start-up and easier access to the services market in Montenegro
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: (Photo: Pixabay.com/ppoppy486) In Montenegro, the Single Contact Point (JKT) portal was recently launched where entrepreneurs and service providers can now find all information about procedures, regulations and competent institutions required for the initiation or performance of activities in one place. The JKT portal provides easy access to data on business registration, recognition of qualifications, costs, licenses and regulations valid in Montenegro and within the EU market. This significantly facilitates business operations and accelerates the process of exercising the rights and obligations of service providers. - JKT is an important step in the process of digital transformation of public administration and contributes to the creation of a more favorable business environment in accordance with European standards. The portal connects state institutions and the economy, making information available, clear and understandable to everyone who wants to start or expand their business - the Ministry of Economic Development said when launching this portal. In this way, Montenegro strengthens the institutional support for the economy and fulfills the obligations from Chapter 3 - Right of business establishment and freedom to provide services in negotiations with the European Union. Why is JKT important? Simplifies business - all information about the necessary steps, documents and regulations is available in one place. It saves time and money - there is no need to go to multiple institutions and search different sources. It supports entrepreneurship and digital transformation – JKT is a digital tool that connects the state and business. The Single Point of Contact portal (JKT) is compliant with EU standards - it meets the obligations of the Services Directive and contributes to the closure of Chapter 3. The goal of the JKT portal is to provide citizens and businesses with easier access to information and reduce bureaucratic obstacles. Everything that once required many steps is now available with one click. title_en: Montenegro introduced artificial intelligence in public services - Chatbot Maša helps in the processes of legalization and issuance of construction permits
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Shutterstock.com/Sutthiphong Chandaeng) Citizens who own illegal objects can now simply and transparently initiate the process of legalization through the legalizuj.me portal, while investors have faster access to information and procedures for issuing construction permits through the gradjevinskadozvola.me portal. Both portals were developed by the Ministry of Spatial Planning, Urbanism and State Property, and an important novelty is the introduction of the chatbot Maša , the first AI assistant in the public services of Montenegro, which provides real-time information to citizens and investors. The digital assistant Maša on the portals legalizuj.me and gradjevinskadozvola.me has the task to provide citizens and investors with faster, simpler and more transparent access to information about the legalization of buildings and the issuance of construction permits. These projects facilitate the work of the Ministry`s officials, but also the access to information for citizens and investors. On the legalizuj.me portal, citizens go through the legalization process in four simple steps, and a list of all the documents they need, as well as the deadlines that must be met, is also available to them. (Photo: Printscreen) The first of the four steps towards legalization is submitting a request on the form prescribed by the ministry, then an elaboration of the survey of the derived state of illegal buildings, proof of registration in the cadastre and photos of all facades of the building. All contacts about the institutions involved in the legalization process are also available on the website. Chatbot Maša answers questions such as: "What documents are needed to legalize a house up to 500 m²?", and if someone does not get an answer, then it will be redirected to emails and other contacts, where the requested information can be obtained. The complete documentation, once collected, must be submitted in person and cannot be submitted through the legalizeuj.me website. The gradjevinskadozvola.me portal allows investors to view the procedures for issuing building permits, deadlines and contacts of the relevant institutions, while Maša helps them easily navigate the process and find the appropriate patterns. How to use Maša: Ask precise and individual questions. Use key terms like "cadastre", "use permit" or "deadlines". The chatbot provides a guide through procedures, but does not replace officers or receive documentation. Maša, namely, represents the first step towards digitalization of public services in Montenegro - provides faster and simpler access to information, relieves officials, but formal procedures still require contact with the relevant authorities. title_en: Draft Law on Plant Protection Products in development – Quality control comes first
title_it: Nuova legge sui prodotti fitosanitari
content_en: (Photo: avemario/shutterstock) The Ministry of Agriculture has begun developing a Draft Law on Plant Protection Products, with the aim of ensuring a high level of protection of human, animal and environmental health, while preserving the competitiveness of domestic agricultural production. As announced by the ministry, the new legal framework regulates the production, registration, trade, safe use, handling and storage of plant protection products. Officials say that the main goal and priority are the production of safe food and competitiveness on the market. More efficient inspections and training (Photo: Photographee.eu/shutterstock.com) The key solutions of the law relate to improving the registration procedure and strengthening the efficiency of plant protection product control, according to a statement from the Ministry of Agriculture. This means that every product on the Serbian market must be registered, i.e. plant protection products must be assessed from multiple aspects, in order to obtain a solution that allows their placing on the market and application. The new law also stipulates mandatory training for professional users on the safe application, handling, storage, transport and disposal of plant protection products, as well as regular periodic checks of the correctness of application devices. The adoption of an Action Plan for the Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products is also envisaged, which will establish objectives, measures, activities and plans for reducing risks as a result of the use of these products. One of the important objectives of the adoption of this law is, as highlighted, further harmonization of national legislation in the field of plant protection products with the EU acquis, which will enable better placement of agricultural products on the domestic and foreign markets. Healthier food and product competitiveness (Photo: Allexxandar/shutterstock.com) The new law should also contribute to the fulfillment of Benchmark 1 for the opening of negotiations in Chapter 12 - Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Policy, as well as the fulfillment of the conditions for the opening of Cluster 5 - Resources, Agriculture and Cohesion. It is expected that the adoption of the Law on Plant Protection Products, the implementation of which will not incur costs for citizens, will have a strong socioeconomic impact, as it ensures, according to the ministry’s assessment, healthier food, more stable production, environmental protection and competitiveness of domestic producers. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management has invited representatives of state bodies and organizations, associations, business entities, experts, as well as other interested parties, to submit their comments, suggestions and proposals on the proposed document by November 25 to the email address listed on the ministry’s website. Il Ministero dell’Agricoltura della Serbia ha avviato l’elaborazione di un progetto di legge sui prodotti fitosanitari, finalizzato a garantire un elevato livello di protezione della salute umana, animale e dell’ambiente, preservando nel contempo la competitività della produzione agricola nazionale. Il nuovo quadro normativo disciplinerà la produzione, la registrazione, il commercio, l’uso sicuro, la manipolazione e lo stoccaggio dei prodotti fitosanitari. L’obiettivo prioritario è la produzione di alimenti sicuri e la competitività sul mercato.  

Tra le principali novità figurano il miglioramento della procedura di registrazione e il rafforzamento dei controlli sui prodotti fitosanitari. Tutti i prodotti presenti sul mercato serbo dovranno essere registrati previa valutazione multidimensionale. È prevista inoltre la formazione obbligatoria per gli utilizzatori professionali riguardo all’applicazione sicura, alla manipolazione, allo stoccaggio, al trasporto e allo smaltimento dei prodotti, nonché controlli periodici obbligatori sui dispositivi di applicazione.  

Il progetto prevede anche l’adozione di un Piano d’Azione per l’uso sostenibile dei prodotti fitosanitari, con obiettivi e misure per ridurre i rischi connessi al loro impiego. La legge mira inoltre ad armonizzare ulteriormente la normativa nazionale con l’acquis dell’Unione europea, favorendo una migliore commercializzazione dei prodotti agricoli sui mercati interno ed estero.  

L’adozione della legge contribuirà al raggiungimento del Benchmark 1 per l’apertura dei negoziati nel Capitolo 12 (Sicurezza alimentare, politica veterinaria e fitosanitaria) e al soddisfacimento dei requisiti per l’apertura del Cluster 5 (Risorse, agricoltura e coesione). Secondo il ministero, la legge avrà un significativo impatto socioeconomico, garantendo alimenti più sani, una produzione più stabile, la tutela ambientale e la competitività dei produttori nazionali, senza comportare costi aggiuntivi per i cittadini.  

Le osservazioni sul progetto possono essere inviate entro il 25 novembre all’indirizzo email indicato sul sito del Ministero dell’Agricoltura, Foreste e Gestione delle Acque della Repubblica di Serbia, come riportato da ekapija.com. L’armonizzazione normativa e il rafforzamento degli standard fitosanitari potrebbero rappresentare un’opportunità per le imprese italiane operanti nel settore agrochimico e nelle tecnologie per l’agricoltura sostenibile.

title_en: Chinese business people interested in food products, focusing on wine, rakija and honey – Cooperation with Yumco also possible
title_it: Interesse cinese per prodotti alimentari serbi
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Sinisa Botas/shuterstock.com) A Serbian delegation, led by Minister of Economy Adrijana Mesarovic, held a series of meetings with companies in the field of information technology in Fuzhou, China, and one of them announced the opening of a research and development center in Belgrade . A company that manufactures sports and functional clothing discussed possible cooperation with the Yumco factory , RTS reported. The Serbian delegation also met with the leaders of the Fujian province, and a business forum was held beforehand, where the benefits of investing in Serbia were presented. The meeting was attended by the two largest retail chains operating in Fujian. Minister of Economy Adrijana Mesarovic points out that the focus was on Serbian wines, rakijas, honey, confectionery , everything that is competitive, fresh fruit and vegetables, which, as she says, they were particularly interested in. – We will continue the discussion and fight for new jobs and the best possible placement of Serbian products in the Fujian province, where we were warmly welcomed. By the way, starting from the city of Xiamen, certain retail chains already have products on their shelves and I hope that consumers are satisfied – said Mesarovic. content_it:
Una delegazione serba, guidata dalla ministra dell’Economia Adrijana Mesarović, ha tenuto una serie di incontri con aziende del settore informatico a Fuzhou, in Cina, tra cui una che ha annunciato l’apertura di un centro di ricerca e sviluppo a Belgrado. È stata inoltre discussa una possibile collaborazione tra un produttore cinese di abbigliamento sportivo e funzionale e la fabbrica serba Yumco di Vranje.

La delegazione ha incontrato anche i rappresentanti della provincia del Fujian, dove in precedenza si era svolto un forum economico dedicato ai vantaggi degli investimenti in Serbia. All’evento hanno partecipato le due maggiori catene della grande distribuzione operanti nella provincia.

La ministra Mesarović ha sottolineato l’interesse dei partner cinesi per prodotti alimentari serbi competitivi, in particolare vini, rakija, miele, prodotti dolciari e ortofrutta fresca. «Continueremo il dialogo per creare nuovi posti di lavoro e per posizionare al meglio i prodotti serbi nella provincia del Fujian, dove siamo stati accolti con grande cortesia. Da Xiamen, alcune catene distribuiscono già nostri prodotti sugli scaffali e spero che i consumatori ne siano soddisfatti», ha affermato.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’iniziativa rientra negli sforzi della Serbia per rafforzare la presenza dei propri prodotti in mercati internazionali strategici. Le imprese italiane del settore agroalimentare potrebbero trarre spunti da questa apertura del mercato cinese verso prodotti di qualità provenienti dai Balcani.

title_en: Open Balkan Wine Vision 2025 from November 22 to 25 at Belgrade Fair
title_it: Open Balkan Wine Vision 2025 a Belgrado
content_en: From a previous edition of the event (Photo: eKapija / Aleksandra Kekić) The fourth edition of the Open Balkan Wine Vision, one of the largest wine and gastronomy fairs in Europe, will be held from November 22 to 25 at the Belgrade Fair, the Chamber of Commerce of Serbia (CCIS) announced. This year, more than 600 exhibitors will present wines, spirits, delicatessen and tourist offers from Serbia and the region, as well as wines from famous regions from all continents. Over the course of four days, Belgrade will be a meeting place for professionals, wine enthusiasts, restaurateurs, traders and all those who believe that wine and food connect people, cultures and traditions. In addition to several thousand wines, spirits and specialties, the fair’s program also includes a wide range of education, workshops, master classes, competitions and panel discussions, as well as unique tastings. The arrival of numerous wine experts has been announced, including holders of the prestigious title of Master of Wine, such as Rod Smith MW, president of the Masters of Wine Institute, the most important global organization of wine experts, the statement says. Visitors will have the opportunity to learn how to taste wines like a Master of Wine expert, to explore the wine regions of Serbia, to get acquainted with the rich rakija tradition, as well as to attend lectures dedicated to indigenous Balkan varieties and the best wines of the world. This year, the fair is once again attended by several hundred wine traders, importers and distributors from all over the world. A special B2B platform for scheduling meetings is available to professional visitors and exhibitors, which allows direct contact and establishing business cooperation in a comfortable, purpose-built space. The finale of the fair will be the announcement of the winner of the major regional competition, the Open Balkan Wine Trophy, where wines from Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania compete for the title of the best, and are evaluated by international experts, including five experts with the title of Master of Wine. The jury will once again be headed by Caroline Gilby MW, one of the most influential international wine experts from our region. The results of the Rakija Trophy competition, which annually brings together the best brandy producers from the Balkans, will also be presented. The culinary part of the fair - the Food Vision event - this year brings a program dedicated to regional gastronomy and hospitality. Visitors can expect culinary spectacles, chef competitions, food and wine pairings, master classes and a series of authentic gourmet gems from the Balkans. Fotografije: +9 Opis: Preteča preduzeća Beogradski sajam bilo je Društvo za priređivanje sajma, formirano 1923. (1933) godine. Postojao je problem adekvatne lokacije, ali povezivanjem Zemuna sa Beogradom i izgradnjom Mosta kralja Aleksandra stvoreni su preduslovi da se i taj problem reši. Godine 1937. na levoj obali Save, na prostoru danas poznatom kao Staro sajmište, izgrađen je sajamski kompleks sa 26 paviljona različite namene i vlasništva, a izlagačima je na raspolaganje stavljeno 17.000 kvadratnih metara prostora pod krovom i još 20.000 na otvorenoj površini. Prvi Beogradski sajam otvoren je 11. septembra 1937. godine. Drugi svetski rat prekinuo je aktivnosti Beogradskog sajma, a sajamski kompleks pretvoren je u nacistički koncentracioni logor, "Jevrejski logor Zemun", u kome je izvršen veliki pogrom Jevreja, odn. kasniji Prihvatni logor za različite taoce. Narodni odbor Beograda 13. maja 1953. godine je doneo odluku o izgradnji novog sajamskog kompleksa. Početku izgradnje je prethodio konkurs na kojem je prva nagrada dodeljena projektu arhitekata Vladete Maksimovića i Milorada Pantovića. Nakon toga se ipak, na inicijativu investitora, odustalo od prihvaćenog prvonagrađenog projekta, sa željom da kroz monumentalniju arhitekturu država bolje prikaže, a beogradska arhitektura da bude ravnopravnije uključena u savremene evropske tokove.Zbog toga je arhitekta Milorad Pantović obišao najmodernije evropske sajmove, i sa novim timom saradnika, inženjerima Brankom Žeželjem i Milanom Krstićem, izneo nov projekat koji je sproveden i kojim je Beogradski sajam dobio izgled kakavi ma danas. content_it: La quarta edizione di Open Balkan Wine Vision, una delle più importanti fiere enogastronomiche d’Europa, si terrà dal 22 al 25 novembre presso il Salone di Belgrado, come annunciato dalla Camera di Commercio e Industria della Serbia (CCIS). Oltre 600 espositori presenteranno vini, distillati, prodotti gourmet e offerte turistiche dalla Serbia, dai Balcani e dalle principali regioni vinicole mondiali. L’evento riunirà per quattro giorni professionisti del settore, enoappassionati, ristoratori e operatori commerciali, promuovendo il vino e il cibo come veicoli di connessione tra culture e tradizioni. Il programma prevede degustazioni, workshop, masterclass, tavole rotonde e concorsi, con la partecipazione di esperti internazionali, tra cui Rod Smith MW, presidente dell’Institute of Masters of Wine. Sarà inoltre attiva una piattaforma B2B per incontri commerciali mirati. L’evento culminerà con l’assegnazione dell’Open Balkan Wine Trophy, competizione regionale tra vini di Serbia, Macedonia del Nord e Albania, valutati da una giuria internazionale guidata da Caroline Gilby MW. Verranno annunciati anche i vincitori del Rakija Trophy, dedicato ai migliori produttori di distillati balcanici. Parallelamente, la sezione Food Vision valorizzerà la gastronomia regionale con show culinari, abbinamenti cibo-vino e dimostrazioni di chef locali. Come riportato da ekapija.com, la fiera rappresenta un’importante opportunità per le aziende italiane del settore vitivinicolo e agroalimentare interessate a espandere la propria presenza nei mercati balcanici.

title_en: Taco Bell coming to Serbia soon
title_it: Taco Bell arriva in Serbia
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Pixabay/samuelfernandezrivera) One of the most famous fast food chains in the world, Taco Bell, is soon opening its doors in the Usce Shopping Center, on the third floor of the new Food Court. After successful openings in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Tastra Bell , the franchise holder for the region, continues to expand the Taco Bell brand to a new market, bringing a unique experience that combines Mexican inspiration and American spirit. The arrival in Serbia is part of a wider regional expansion, which aims to bring global gastronomic trends closer to the domestic market and create a new destination for all fans of delicious, healthier and modern food. Founded in 1962 in California, Taco Bell today operates more than 8,000 restaurants in over 30 countries around the world. The brand is known for its bold combination of flavors, recognizable identity and innovative products that set it apart from classic fast-food concepts. The offer includes numerous favorite products - from tacos, burritos and nachos, to quesadillas and other dishes that are constantly evolving to meet the desires of modern consumers. As announced by the company, the exact opening date will be announced soon, and visitors can expect a modernly decorated space that follows Taco Bell’s global standards - a recognizable interior, vibrant visuals and a unique atmosphere that makes this brand a favorite around the world. content_it: Uno dei marchi di fast food più noti al mondo, Taco Bell, aprirà presto un locale nel centro commerciale Usce a Belgrado, al terzo piano della nuova Food Court. Dopo il successo riscontrato in Bosnia ed Erzegovina, Tastra Bell, titolare del franchising per la regione, prosegue l’espansione del brand introducendolo in un nuovo mercato, con un’offerta che unisce ispirazione messicana e spirito americano. L’ingresso in Serbia si inserisce in una più ampia strategia di crescita regionale, volta ad avvicinare le tendenze gastronomiche globali al mercato locale e a creare una nuova destinazione per gli appassionati di cibo gustoso, più sano e contemporaneo. Fondato in California nel 1962, Taco Bell conta oggi oltre 8.000 ristoranti in più di 30 Paesi. Il brand si distingue per combinazioni audaci di sapori, un’identità riconoscibile e prodotti innovativi che lo differenziano dai tradizionali concetti di fast food. Il menu propone specialità amate da tutti – tra cui tacos, burritos, nachos e quesadillas – costantemente aggiornate in linea con le preferenze dei consumatori moderni. Come riportato da ekapija.com, la data esatta di apertura sarà comunicata a breve; gli ospiti potranno godere di uno spazio arredato secondo gli standard globali del marchio, con interni iconici, grafica vivace e un’atmosfera unica che ha reso Taco Bell un preferito in tutto il mondo. L’arrivo del brand potrebbe rappresentare un’opportunità per fornitori italiani di materie prime alimentari, attrezzature per la ristorazione e servizi specializzati nel settore della ristorazione moderna.

title_en: Serbian companies establishing tractor assembly and fertilizer production plants in Zambia
title_it: Imprese serbe in Zambia: trattori e fertilizzanti
content_en: (Photo: Vedrana Džudža) Some private companies from Serbia are currently in the process of establishing tractor assembly and fertilizer production plants in Zambia, the Zambian Ministry of Defense announced. The newly appointed Serbian Ambassador to Zambia, Jasna Zrnovic, stated that she would lead a Zambian delegation to Serbia at the end of the year to finalize the establishment of the factories, according to the Zambian ministry’s Facebook account. Zrnovic, according to the post, said that Serbian companies wanted to train Zambian experts in tractor assembly and fertilizer production before the factories were built. During yesterday’s visit to Zambian Defense Minister Ambrose Lwiji Lufuma, Zrnovic stated that funds for the factories had already been secured, and that those who would work in the plants would receive training and capacity building in Serbia. She added that her role as the newly appointed envoy (of Serbia to Zambia) would be to strengthen relations between the two countries, especially in the fields of economy and defense. The Zambian Defense Minister welcomed the decision of Serbian companies to establish factories in Zambia. Lufuma said that the tractor and fertilizer factories would boost the development of the agricultural sector, and that they came at a time when the government was promoting greater investment in the sector, the announcement said. The Defense Minister also noted that Zambia was blessed with fertile land and was a good destination for agricultural investments thanks to its favorable climate. Lufuma also called for more partnerships between Zambian and Serbian companies in areas such as agriculture, transport and tourism. B. P. Embassy of Serbia in Zambia Ministry of Defense of Zambia Jasna Zrnović Ambrose Lwiji Lufuma tractor and fertilizer production plants Your comment Send
content_it: Alcune aziende private serbe stanno avviando in Zambia la costruzione di impianti per l’assemblaggio di trattori e la produzione di fertilizzanti, come annunciato dal Ministero della Difesa zambiano. La neoambasciatrice serba in Zambia, Jasna Zrnovic, ha dichiarato, secondo il profilo Facebook del ministero, che guiderà una delegazione zambiana in Serbia entro la fine dell’anno per finalizzare la realizzazione degli stabilimenti. Le imprese serbe intendono formare tecnici zambiani nel settore dell’assemblaggio di trattori e nella produzione di fertilizzanti prima dell’avvio delle fabbriche. Durante un incontro con il ministro della Difesa zambiano, Ambrose Lwiji Lufuma, l’ambasciatrice ha confermato che i fondi per i progetti sono già stati assicurati e che il personale che opererà negli impianti riceverà formazione in Serbia. Zrnovic ha inoltre sottolineato che il suo ruolo sarà quello di rafforzare i legami tra Serbia e Zambia, in particolare nei settori economico e della difesa. Il ministro Lufuma ha accolto con favore l’iniziativa, evidenziando che gli stabilimenti contribuiranno allo sviluppo del settore agricolo zambiano, in linea con la politica governativa di incentivare gli investimenti in agricoltura. Ha inoltre ricordato che lo Zambia, grazie al suo clima favorevole e alla fertilità dei terreni, rappresenta una destinazione ideale per investimenti agricoli, e ha auspicato ulteriori partnership tra imprese serbe e zambiane nei settori dell’agricoltura, dei trasporti e del turismo, come riportato da ekapija.com. Le opportunità emerse potrebbero risultare interessanti anche per aziende italiane specializzate in macchinari agricoli o tecnologie per la produzione di fertilizzanti.

title_en: Contract for construction of first subway line to be signed by December 15 – Serbia also buying supercomputer from France
title_it: Firma del contratto metro entro il 15 dicembre
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Johnson76/shutterstock.com) Many fast and slow trains have passed through Serbia and Belgrade in the past 141 years, since the establishment of rail traffic in our country, but subway trains have not yet had passengers in our capital. When this will happen has been speculated for years, deadlines have been postponed, plans and routes have been changed... If we are to judge by the latest announcement, the one coming from France, the first passengers will board the Belgrade subway in 2028 or 2029 at the earliest. By December 15, the contract for the construction of the first subway line will be signed with the Alstom company, said Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic after talks with French President Emmanuel Macron. – The final commercial contract for the construction of the first subway line will be signed with the French company. So, in the next month, we will complete this work and start finalizing it so that in two and a half years we will have the first subway line, two and a half or three, it doesn’t matter, but Belgrade will finally get a subway – Vucic assures. As he said, they also talked about military-technical cooperation, about the possibility of assembling Airbus helicopters in Serbia. – We also talked about Mistral and Rafale missiles, but we also talked about all other key bilateral agreements – Vucic said. He also mentioned that Serbia was buying a supercomputer from the French that would be very valuable and the only one of its kind in Southeast Europe. content_it: Dopo 141 anni dall’avvio del traffico ferroviario in Serbia, la capitale Belgrado non ha ancora visto circolare treni metropolitani. Tuttavia, secondo le recenti dichiarazioni del presidente serbo Aleksandar Vučić al termine dei colloqui con il presidente francese Emmanuel Macron, il contratto commerciale definitivo per la costruzione della prima linea metropolitana sarà firmato entro il 15 dicembre con la società francese Alstom. “Nei prossimi mesi completeremo gli ultimi passaggi per avviare i lavori e, tra due anni e mezzo o tre, Belgrado avrà finalmente la sua metropolitana”, ha dichiarato Vučić. Durante l’incontro è stata inoltre annunciata l’acquisizione da parte della Serbia di un supercomputer di origine francese, descritto come unico nel suo genere in Europa sud-orientale. I colloqui hanno infine riguardato la cooperazione militare e tecnica, inclusa la possibile assemblaggio in Serbia di elicotteri Airbus e la fornitura di sistemi missilistici Mistral e Rafale. Come riportato da ekapija.com, il progetto rappresenta un passo strategico per le infrastrutture urbane serbe e potrebbe aprire opportunità per imprese italiane specializzate in infrastrutture e subfornitura tecnologica.

title_en: Hungarian Mol could be solution for NIS by buying 11.3% stake
title_it: MOL potrebbe acquisire quota NIS
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Shutterstock/Adam Radosavljevic) Intensive negotiations on the sale of part of the shares of Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS) are underway, and the Russians are counting on the Hungarian Mol, or rather, on local Prime Minister Viktor Orban, and the plan is for that company to buy 11.3% of NIS shares, writes the NIN weekly. The plan should be finalized in mid-November, when a delegation from Moscow will arrive in Budapest. According to the weekly, not all cards are placed on potential Hungarian partners, but negotiations are also underway with the Emirates. The Russians believe that the signal of a gradual exit from the ownership structure of NIS is enough for the US Office of Foreign Assets Control of the US Treasury Department (OFAC) to “suspend the sanctions next week,” the text states. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said on Tuesday that Russia was talking to a “third party” about the management structure of NIS, but that he couldn’t discuss the details. Minister of Mining and Energy Dubravka Djedovic Handanovic said that the Russian owners of NIS had sent a request to the OFAC for an extension of the operating license based on negotiations with a third party. Sanctions on NIS were imposed earlier this year due to Russia’s ownership stake, but their implementation was delayed until October 9, when they came into effect. NIS a.d. content_it: Sono in corso intensi negoziati per la vendita di una parte delle azioni di Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS). Secondo il settimanale NIN, la Russia punta sulla compagnia ungherese MOL, contando sul sostegno del primo ministro ungherese Viktor Orbán, con l’obiettivo che quest’ultima acquisti l’11,3% del capitale di NIS. L’accordo dovrebbe concretizzarsi a metà novembre, in occasione della visita di una delegazione russa a Budapest. Tuttavia, come riportato da ekapija.com, Mosca non starebbe puntando esclusivamente su MOL, poiché sono attivi colloqui anche con investitori degli Emirati Arabi Uniti. La Russia ritiene che il segnale di un graduale disimpegno dalla proprietà di NIS possa indurre l’Ufficio per il controllo dei beni esteri del Dipartimento del Tesoro statunitense (OFAC) a sospendere le sanzioni già la prossima settimana. Il presidente serbo Aleksandar Vučić ha confermato martedì che Mosca sta discutendo con una “terza parte” riguardo alla struttura gestionale di NIS, pur dichiarandosi impossibilitato a fornire dettagli. La ministra serba dell’Energia e delle Miniere, Dubravka Đedović Handanović, ha riferito che i proprietari russi di NIS hanno chiesto all’OFAC una proroga della licenza operativa, sulla base dei negoziati in corso con questa terza parte. Le sanzioni contro NIS, imposte all’inizio dell’anno a causa della partecipazione russa, erano state differite fino al 9 ottobre, data in cui sono entrate in vigore. L’operazione, se conclusa, potrebbe aprire nuove prospettive per la stabilità del settore energetico serbo, con possibili opportunità per imprese internazionali, incluse quelle italiane, nei segmenti di fornitura, tecnologia e servizi specializzati.

title_en: Tender for development of Detailed Regulation Plan for reconstruction of Pancevo Bridge – New access ramps
title_it: Gara per il piano regolatore del ponte di Pančevo
content_en: (Photo: lunja/shutterstock) The PE Roads of Serbia has announced a tender for the development of a Detailed Regulation Plan for the reconstruction of the road-rail bridge over the Danube River - Pancevo Bridge in Belgrade, on the IB-class state road no. 47, section Belgrade (Bogoslovija) - Krnjaca interchange, and the construction of access ramps. As stated in the program assignment, the importance of the implementation of this project is reflected in the improvement of traffic conditions in terms of safe traffic flow and reduction of travel time, as well as improving the living conditions of the population. The reconstruction also includes the construction of access ramps, which are located in the zone of the grade-separated intersection with Dunavska and Vuka Vrcevica streets, Palilula Municipality. The access ramps are being built so that traffic over the Pancevo Bridge can proceed unhindered throughout the construction period. The tender is worth 14 million dinars and expires on December 9. For other details, click HERE . Fotografije: Opis: Pančevački most ili Pančevac je poznati beogradski most preko Dunava. Sa izgradnjom mosta se počelo 1933. godine, otvoren je 1935. godine, a obnovljen nakon Drugog svetskog rata 1946. godine. U vreme izgradnje, bio je jedan od najdužih mostova u Evropi. Nazvan je Most Petra II Karađorđevića, a Nemci su ga u oktobru 1944. godine gotovo skroz srušili. Renoviranje mosta urađeno je 1966. godine kada je dobio sadašnji izgled i novo ime. content_it: La società pubblica "Strade della Serbia" ha indetto una gara per l'elaborazione del Piano Regolatore Dettagliato relativo alla ricostruzione del ponte stradale e ferroviario sul Danubio – il ponte di Pančevo a Belgrado – lungo la strada statale di classe IB n. 47, tratto Belgrado (Bogoslovija) – svincolo di Krnjača, nonché per la costruzione di rampe di accesso. Come riportato nel capitolato, il progetto mira a migliorare la sicurezza e la fluidità del traffico, ridurre i tempi di percorrenza e innalzare la qualità della vita della popolazione locale. Le rampe, ubicate nell’area dello svincolo con le vie Dunavska e Vuka Vrčevića nel comune di Palilula, consentiranno il transito continuo sul ponte durante i lavori di ricostruzione. L'appalto, del valore di 14 milioni di dinari, scade il 9 dicembre, come riportato da ekapija.com. Il ponte di Pančevo, lungo 1.526,4 metri e largo 18, è stato inaugurato nel 1935, gravemente danneggiato durante la Seconda guerra mondiale e ricostruito nel 1946. Ulteriori interventi risalgono al 1966, quando assunse l’aspetto attuale. Ogni giorno lo attraversano circa 100.000 veicoli. L’incarico potrebbe rappresentare un’opportunità per imprese italiane specializzate in ingegneria, pianificazione infrastrutturale e servizi tecnici nel settore dei trasporti.

title_en: State to borrow EUR 260 million to finance works on Morava Corridor
title_it: Prestito di 260 milioni per il Corridoio Morava
content_en: (Photo: Dejan Aleksić) The Government of Serbia has adopted the Draft Law on the Confirmation of the Credit Arrangement Agreement, which concerns an unsecured loan of up to EUR 260 million with a guarantee from the British agency UKEF. The funds will be used to finance construction services performed in Serbia by Bechtel Enka UK Limited , through its branch in Belgrade, for the needs of the company Koridori Srbije (Corridors of Serbia), in connection with the construction of the infrastructure corridor of the E-761 highway, the Pojate-Preljina section, known as the Morava Corridor . The law is being passed in order to confirm the Credit Arrangement Agreement signed on October 27 between the Republic of Serbia, represented by the Government of the Republic of Serbia, acting through the Ministry of Finance, as the borrower, and J.P. Morgan SE, as Agent, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., London Branch, as the Original Authorized Lead Arranger, Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank and ING Bank N.V., as Authorized Lead Arrangers, and certain other financial institutions, as Original Lenders. The Morava Corridor, Pojate-Preljina section, is approximately 110 km long and connects central Serbia with key international transport routes, Corridors 10 and 11. The construction of the highway increases accessibility to municipal centers, economic zones and tourist destinations, connecting the settlements of Cicevac, Stalac, Krusevac, Trstenik, Vrnjacka Banja, Kraljevo and Cacak. The credit arrangement provides for a loan of up to EUR 260 million, with a maturity of up to 12 years , including a two-year grace period. The interest rate is variable and is based on 6M EURIBOR with a fixed margin of 0.6% per annum, while the commission on undrawn funds is 40% of the margin amount, charged semi-annually. I. Z.
