content_it:
Il Governo della Serbia ha adottato il progetto di legge per la conferma dell’accordo di finanziamento relativo a un prestito non garantito fino a 260 milioni di euro, con garanzia dell’agenzia britannica UKEF. I fondi serviranno a finanziare i servizi di costruzione svolti in Serbia da Bechtel Enka UK Limited, attraverso la sua filiale a Belgrado, per conto di Koridori Srbije, nell’ambito della realizzazione del tratto Pojate-Preljina dell’autostrada E-761, noto come Corridoio Morava.

L’accordo è stato firmato il 27 ottobre tra la Repubblica di Serbia, rappresentata dal Ministero delle Finanze, e un consorzio di istituti finanziari guidato da J.P. Morgan SE, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank e ING Bank N.V.

Il tratto autostradale, lungo circa 110 km, collega la Serbia centrale ai Corridoi europei 10 e 11, migliorando l’accessibilità a centri municipali, zone economiche e destinazioni turistiche come Ćićevac, Stalać, Kruševac, Trstenik, Vrnjačka Banja, Kraljevo e Čačak.

Il prestito ha una durata massima di 12 anni, con un periodo di grazia di due anni. Il tasso d’interesse è variabile, basato sull’EURIBOR a 6 mesi con un margine fisso dello 0,6% annuo; la commissione sui fondi non utilizzati è pari al 40% del margine, applicata semestralmente, come riportato da ekapija.com.

L’attuazione di questo progetto infrastrutturale offre opportunità alle imprese italiane specializzate in macchinari per l’edilizia, materiali da costruzione e servizi tecnici connessi alle grandi opere stradali.

title_en: Srbijavoz to borrow EUR 42 million for purchase of new sleeping cars – Trains to Thessaloniki, Villach, Vienna, Munich, Prague again?
title_it: Srbijavoz: prestito da 42 milioni per nuovi vagoni letto
content_en: Illustration (Photo: potowizard/shutterstock.com) The Government of Serbia has adopted the Draft Law on the Confirmation of the Guarantee Agreement between the Republic of Serbia and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, by which Serbia guarantees the obligations of Srbijavoz under a loan intended for the purchase of 12 new sleeping cars. Namely, as stated in the explanatory memorandum to the law, the state signed a Guarantee Agreement with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on October 31, which guarantees the obligations of Srbijavoz under a loan of EUR 42 million. The agreement stipulates that the Republic of Serbia, as the guarantor, unconditionally covers all financial obligations for Srbijavoz, including the repayment of principal and interest under the Loan Agreement, as well as the fulfillment of all other obligations arising from that agreement. The project includes three parts: the procurement of new sleeping cars, Public Transport Obligation (PTO) fees and donor-funded technical assistance , including the engagement of consultants to review the PTO contract in accordance with international standards. The planned completion date of the project is December 31, 2028. Currently, only four sleeping cars in the fleet Currently, the Srbijavoz fleet has four sleeping cars, between 40 and 60 years old , which do not meet European Union standards and are limited in speed and technological capacity, making them unsuitable for international lines. The procurement of 12 new high-standard sleeping cars, capable of speeds of up to 200 km/h, is, as stated, a strategic step in the modernization of the company. A significant increase in the quality of services, an increase in capacity and strengthening of competitiveness in the European market is expected. The new sleeping cars will enable more comfortable and safer travel, and Serbia will reportedly re-establish direct rail connections with key European destinations, including Thessaloniki, Villach, Vienna, Munich and Prague. content_it: Il Governo della Serbia ha adottato il disegno di legge per la conferma dell’accordo di garanzia tra la Repubblica di Serbia e la Banca europea per la ricostruzione e lo sviluppo (BERD), con il quale lo Stato garantisce gli obblighi di Srbijavoz relativi a un prestito di 42 milioni di euro destinato all’acquisto di 12 nuovi vagoni letto. L’accordo, firmato il 31 ottobre, prevede che la Serbia copra incondizionatamente tutti gli obblighi finanziari di Srbijavoz, inclusi capitale, interessi e altre obbligazioni derivanti dal contratto di prestito. Il progetto comprende anche il finanziamento degli oneri per gli obblighi di servizio pubblico (PTO) e assistenza tecnica cofinanziata da donatori, tra cui consulenti per il riesame del contratto PTO secondo standard internazionali. Il completamento è previsto entro il 31 dicembre 2028. Attualmente, la flotta di Srbijavoz dispone di soli quattro vagoni letto, vecchi tra i 40 e i 60 anni, non conformi agli standard UE e inadatti alle linee internazionali. I nuovi vagoni, capaci di raggiungere i 200 km/h, rappresentano un passo strategico per la modernizzazione del servizio ferroviario serbo, con un previsto miglioramento della qualità, aumento della capacità e rafforzamento della competitività sul mercato europeo. Si prevede inoltre il ripristino di collegamenti ferroviari diretti con destinazioni chiave come Salonicco, Villach, Vienna, Monaco e Praga, come riportato da ekapija.com. Ciò potrebbe aprire nuove opportunità per le imprese italiane attive nel settore ferroviario, in particolare nella fornitura di componenti, servizi tecnici e consulenza specializzata.

title_en: Tamara Milovanović, general director of PMI for Southeast Europe - Who gives wings to domestic innovators
title_it: StarTech accelera l'innovazione in Serbia
content_en: Tamara Milovanović (Photo: Stefan Jovanović) The Global Week of Entrepreneurship raises again the topic of the necessity of a close encounter between two seemingly different worlds - small entrepreneurs and large corporations. Startups bring speed and creativity, while corporations provide resources, technology and access to global networks. When they work together, ideas move more quickly from the lab to practice, and digital transformation becomes a reality. Philip Morris International , which has been investing in the improvement of the local community since its arrival in Serbia in 2003, has recognized that supporting innovation is key to the long-term development and competitiveness of the domestic economy. It is precisely for this reason that StarTech was launched - a platform that shows how partnership can speed up the path from idea to market and open the door to the world for innovators across Serbia. T amara Milovanović, PMI`s general director for Southeast Europe , talks about the scope of the program and the key challenges of digitalization for eKapija. How can large companies contribute to digital transformation in practice? - The transfer of knowledge, technology and funds from large companies to startups and entrepreneurs with big ideas - it`s a pattern... that`s easy to set up, but much harder to implement in the right way. Because only ad hoc subsidization of innovations is not enough - it is necessary to establish a sustainable cooperation mechanism and avoid the effect of "innovation theater" - programs that actually serve branding and PR, not innovation for the sake of general benefit. I believe that the way Philip Morris applies this form in Serbia is "for textbooks". It`s not exactly a textbook, but the recently published Research on cooperation between corporations and startups in the Western Balkans, prepared by the ICT Hub with the support of the EBRD, confirms my claim and highlights us as an example to follow. And it all started with internal transformation - for two decades we have been changing from a traditional company to a company where science and innovation are the basis of every business move. In this way, we gained expertise, and then secured funds, had a strong will and a great commitment to transfer that approach to the domestic ecosystem as well. That`s how StarTech was born, a program that supports the development of innovation and startup ecosystem in Serbia through financial support (grants) and improvement of the business environment. From there, PMInnovia was later born, as an "open innovation" program, which enables domestic startups and scientific teams to develop innovative solutions for the needs of the Philip Morris company. Thanks to this project, "homegrown intelligence" is already participating in the continuous improvement of our products based on technologically advanced, less harmful forms of nicotine delivery, thereby contributing to a faster transition to a world without tobacco smoke. You started StarTech five years ago with NALED and the Serbian Government. What was the vision that launched the whole project? - Startech may be formally called a project, but I see it more as a strategic initiative that connects knowledge, innovation and business into one sustainable system. It is not just a grant scheme, but a long-term platform that changes the way the entire innovation ecosystem works. Today, after five years, StarTech remains the largest program of its kind in the country, entirely funded by a private company. We have positioned ourselves as a partner to innovators, but also to institutions - a program that supports product development and improves the conditions in which innovators work. Our goal in the years to come remains the same: to create an environment where a good idea can become a globally marketable product much faster than before. We are proud to hold the title of "first" or "biggest" in this type of cooperation at this moment, but our goal is not to be the only one. The more companies that follow the same path, the deeper the transformation will be and the more tangible the progress. What results of StarTech would you single out as the greatest - what has changed the domestic innovation ecosystem the most? - The news was announced these days that the autonomous AgAR tractor produced in Serbia achieved significant success at the fair in Hanover, where it entered the finals for the Robot Tractor of the Year Award. It is one of 100 projects supported by StarTech so far. In December, we will also announce a new generation of grantees. Through the program, all of them receive financial mentoring support, access to a network of partners and promotion. All of this has led to some small teams becoming serious companies that export worldwide. Today, solutions such as agricultural robots, advanced medical devices or digital platforms are changing their industries for the better and creating new jobs throughout Serbia. As much as 45% of the grantees are already present in foreign markets - in as many as 27 countries, not counting our country. Of course, the region and the EU predominate, but there are also Australia, Japan, the USA, China, Korea, Egypt, Malta... Grants are the most visible, but not the only, part of the Startech program. Together with the Government of Serbia and NALED, we have improved the innovative business environment - from regulating the status of freelancers and technology transfer, to developing the Register of subjects of the innovation system. We actively participate in Government working groups, prepare a startup ecosystem development strategy 2026 - 2030, and even connect academia and business through the Science Caravan, promoting industrial doctorates and a portal for connecting science and business. StarTech has become a pillar of innovation development, as confirmed by the European Commission`s award for promoting entrepreneurship. What is the key obstacle to digital transformation in Serbia today - and where lies our greatest development potential? - There are plenty of ideas, technologies developed by domestic innovators exist, but the path to wider application in the economy is not yet fast enough. That`s to be expected – we`re still struggling with a legacy where innovation and science are seen as theory rather than tools for growth. It is precisely through this struggle that we reach our greatest potential - effective application. Serbia has an exceptionally strong engineering staff and an increasingly mature innovation scene, which is confirmed by international indices. On the Global Innovation Index, we are 54th among 139 countries, and among middle-income countries we are in the top 10. The European Innovation Scoreboard records progress in cloud technologies, the development of IT experts and the cooperation of innovative small and medium-sized enterprises. These are the areas in which we can make the fastest progress. With better digital skills, stronger intellectual property protection and a greater focus on applied research, we can significantly accelerate the digital transformation of the entire economy. How do you see the current startup scene in Serbia - and what do domestic teams need the most in order to take their product to the global market? - The startup scene in Serbia today is more diverse, ambitious and regionally distributed than ever. Ideas arise everywhere - from Belgrade to Niš. Through the Pop-Up Export Hub initiative, which is also part of StarTech, we are already helping teams from the south of the country to enter international markets, because the talent exists, but the path to global visibility requires additional support. Domestic startups need more stable industrial partners in order to develop solutions in a real environment, a predictable regulatory framework that facilitates growth, investment and technology transfer, mentors and a support network - connecting them to the global market and investors. content_it: Tamara Milovanović, direttrice generale di Philip Morris International (PMI) per il Sud-Est Europa, illustra a ekapija.com il ruolo delle grandi aziende nella trasformazione digitale e nello sviluppo dell’ecosistema innovativo serbo. Dal 2003, PMI sostiene la comunità locale in Serbia, lanciando nel 2019 la piattaforma StarTech insieme al Governo serbo e a NALED. L’iniziativa non si limita a erogare finanziamenti, ma crea un sistema sostenibile di collaborazione tra startup, istituzioni e grandi imprese. Attraverso grant, mentoring, accesso a reti internazionali e supporto alla commercializzazione, StarTech ha già sostenuto 100 progetti, tra cui il trattore autonomo AgAR, finalista al premio Robot Tractor of the Year a Hannover. Oggi il 45% dei beneficiari esporta in 27 Paesi, tra cui USA, Giappone, Cina e Australia. Parallelamente, PMI ha avviato PMInnovia, un programma di “open innovation” che coinvolge startup e team scientifici nello sviluppo di soluzioni per prodotti a base di nicotina meno dannosi. Oltre al sostegno diretto, StarTech ha contribuito a migliorare l’ambiente normativo, promuovendo la registrazione dei freelance, il trasferimento tecnologico e la creazione del Registro dei soggetti del sistema innovativo. La Serbia figura al 54° posto su 139 Paesi nell’Indice Globale dell’Innovazione ed è tra le prime 10 economie a reddito medio. Nonostante ingegneri qualificati e una scena startup sempre più dinamica e distribuita territorialmente, servono partner industriali stabili, un quadro regolatorio prevedibile e maggiore tutela della proprietà intellettuale per accelerare la trasformazione digitale. Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa sinergia tra grandi aziende e innovatori locali rappresenta un modello replicabile per rafforzare la competitività dell’economia serba. Le imprese italiane attive nei settori della meccatronica, delle tecnologie agricole, dei dispositivi medici e della consulenza per l’innovazione potrebbero trovare opportunità di collaborazione con l’ecosistema serbo in espansione.

title_en: Boris Samohvalov, Sales Director Yettel Bank: The Future of Banking? It’s already here.
title_it: Yettel Bank: banca trasparente e digitale
content_en: In the world of banking, where conversations often turn into a maze of technical terms and hidden fees, it sounds almost unexpected when the sales director speaks simply, openly and without calculation. This is precisely the approach that comes from Yettel Bank , where transparency is the core product and customer experience is the main strategy. On what they sell when they "hide nothing" and what the future of banking looks like, we are talking to Boris Samohvalov, sales director of Yettel Bank . When we say “sales director of a bank,” most people imagine a conversation filled with financial jargon, product explanations and reasons why one bank is supposedly better than another. But not all banks on our market are the same - Yettel Bank is a pioneer not only in digital banking, but also in simple communication and transparent products. Does that make sales easier or harder? - I’ve been in sales for over a decade, and I know exactly how hard it is when things just  don’t move - like trying to push a car uphill in the rain with the handbrake on. I don’t want to sound immodest, but our situation is completely different: we have products that practically sell themselves. Because we removed everything people dislike about banking. The entire philosophy behind Yettel Bank is that there are no fine print tricks, no hidden fees, and no profit at the customer’s expense. With this mindset, I believe our 320,000 active customers are only the beginning. We’re not selling a bank - we’re offering real solutions to real needs, saving people their two most valuable resources: time and money. And beyond all that, I believe the key role is played by our dedicated sales specialists and agents who are in daily contact with customers and carry our mission forward - we don’t want to sell at any cost: we want genuine customer satisfaction. The best proof that this is true is that I have yet to meet a customer who tried our bank and said, “It’s good, but it’s not for me”. What’s the secret behind that success? Has our market finally matured enough to fully embrace digital banking? You’ve previously said that the term “digitalization” is outdated - that digital is the new normal. Where is that “normal” today, and is it what makes the difference for customers? - Talking about digitalization today is like talking about introducing electricity in the 21st century - late and pointless. Development is fast, AI is reshaping everyday life, and the only real secret to success is innovation that truly solves real customers needs. Our mobile app has a 4.8 rating - and that number matters. It proves that the app isn’t an add-on to the bank, it is the bank. It provides all the features customer need for everyday banking, shortening the distance between intention and execution. I don’t want to sound too salesy, so I won’t list everything it offers - I’ll highlight just a few innovations: second-generation Liveness video identification and our instant cards. That is the future of banking - secure, instant, without waiting, without delays, without wasting time or patience. This vision is what brought me to the bank in the first place, as a customer. At the start, I was impressed by the pioneering approach to digital banking and today, that approach is raising my personal expectations not only for banking, but for all industries in the future. So the future of banking is really the future of customer experience. How do you strike the balance between innovation and customer focus? There is no balance and no compromise. Every innovation must be rooted in customer satisfaction. If it doesn’t start there, it's just an expensive gadget. Bank MAX account is the best example of this. Our 174,000 customers rely on it because it was designed around their needs, not industry norms. We asked them what bothers them, and the answer was clear: fees. So we created an account with no maintenance fees, no ATM withdrawal fees anywhere, no transfer fees - and all they need to do is transfer part of their income or spend at least 30,000 dinars on their card. And this isn’t just my narrative - our latest achievement proves it: the silver award at the ICXA competition in London for “Best Innovation in CX”. It confirms that the market sees what we see: customer is the center, everything else is decoration. Congratulations on that recognition - it truly shows things are moving in the right direction. Speaking of direction and development, we have to mention Yettel Sve. We’ve seen these two words all summer - on social media, TV ads, billboards and bus stops. What exactly is Yettel Sve and what can we expect next? - Yettel Sve is a truly unique program, not only in our region but beyond. It’s designed as a special loyalty program for customers who use both Yettel and Yettel Bank. What’s important is that the program costs nothing - if customers meet the conditions, all benefits are available immediately and free of charge. One part of the program is the Sve za put travel package, which is why we saw it everywhere during the summer. Customers should know that all benefits - cashback, travel insurance, flight discounts and additional roaming are valid throughout the year. Yettel Sve is there for both summer and winter holidays, making sure our 30,000 active customers travel worry-free. Naturally, further development of the program is planned, and it will certainly bring new benefits. When I explain the program to friends, I always use this analogy - imagine you want a nice cappuccino. In one café they only have coffee, in another only milk, and in a third only sugar. You don’t want to go from café to café collecting parts, you just want your drink. It’s the same with telecom and banking services you want everything in one place. With an offer like this, I’m sure you’ve experienced the reaction: “This is too good to be true”. Has that happened? - Yes, we often get the question: “Is it really like that” and the answer is yes. There are no hidden fees, no obligations we didn’t mention. I know it feels unusual because people aren’t used to it. And speaking of habits I often tell my team that our biggest competition isn’t other banks, but the habits of customers. People sometimes accept something worse simply because they fear change. That’s why we keep reminding them: it’s not too good to be true, and we encourage them daily to try our bank. Our message is simple - don’t settle for anything less than the best. A beautiful message to end on - that we should all aim for the best. What will Yettel Bank aim for in 2026? - We started with digital, so I’ll end there too. In 2026, I wish for the whole sector to push the market even further and adopt advanced solutions that make life easier. I’m not talking about reducing waiting times - that’s long outdated. I’m talking about banking at a click: not tomorrow, not soon, but now. This year has proven that we’re ready for big things through organic growth. Our goal is simple - to become the first choice of customers. The number of salary receivers, savings accounts and active loans shows we’re on the right path. Since our rebranding, we’ve reached over half a million loan accounts. That’s a sign of trust, a sign that we can. In 2026, we plan to show we can even more, and we’re entering the year ready to make something extraordinary. I’m genuinely excited by every new comment from our customers, because together with our amazing team of dedicated experts, we’re building a bank people will truly love. Boris Samohvalov, direttore commerciale, sottolinea che la filosofia del gruppo elimina ciò che i clienti tradizionalmente detestano delle banche: clausole oscure, commissioni impreviste e profitti a loro spese. "Non vendiamo una banca, offriamo soluzioni reali che risparmiano tempo e denaro", afferma Samohvalov, ricordando che i 320.000 clienti attivi sono solo l’inizio.  

L’innovazione è guidata dall’esperienza del cliente: l’app mobile, con un punteggio di 4,8, non è un accessorio ma il cuore dell’operatività bancaria. Tra le soluzioni più apprezzate, l’identificazione video di seconda generazione e le carte istantanee. Il conto Bank MAX, utilizzato da 174.000 clienti, elimina le commissioni di gestione, prelievo e bonifico a fronte di semplici condizioni d’uso. Questo approccio ha valso al gruppo il premio d’argento all’ICXA di Londra per la “Miglior Innovazione nell’Esperienza del Cliente”.

Il programma Yettel Sve, gratuito per chi utilizza sia i servizi telecom che quelli bancari del gruppo, offre cashback, assicurazione di viaggio, sconti voli e roaming aggiuntivo tutto l’anno. “La nostra vera concorrenza non sono altre banche, ma le abitudini dei clienti”, osserva Samohvalov, incoraggiando a superare la paura del cambiamento.

Per il 2026, Yettel Bank punta a diventare la prima scelta dei consumatori, forte di una crescita organica che ha già portato oltre mezzo milione di conti prestito da quando è avvenuto il rebranding. Come riportato da ekapija.com, l’obiettivo è rendere la banca “a un click” una realtà immediata, non futura.  

Per le imprese italiane attive nei settori fintech, telecomunicazioni e servizi digitali, il modello di Yettel Bank rappresenta un’opportunità di osservare come integrazione di servizi e customer experience possano ridefinire interi mercati.

title_en: Click to Success - Sounds Good, but Does it Work?
title_it: Cliccare verso il successo?
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Shutterstock.com/3Dsss) While we were preparing the special edition before you, the former "Digitalization" special edition newsletter, we asked ourselves: Does it make sense to talk about digitalization in 2025? While artificial intelligence is already "solving" our emotional, health, and business problems, when machines assist us in decision making, diagnostics and strategy, and the algorithms shape our experience, digitization sounds almost old-fashioned. A term that has done its job and retreated before the onslaught of a new, more complex technological era. But digitization, in fact, has not disappeared. It just became invisible. It is so taken for granted that we no longer recognize it as a process but as background noise. It is a basic layer, an operating system. Without it, there would be neither artificial intelligence, nor automation, nor smart decisions. And it was precisely the years of digital transformation that brought us to the moment in which we are today. And then we asked ourselves something else: Is success really possible "with a click", or is it just a myth that the industry persistently sells us? If digitization has become an invisible infrastructure, the "click" has become its most visible symbol. But not because success comes with a single tap on the screen. Because the click has become a metaphor : for the decision, for the courage to change processes, for the willingness to understand what is beneath the surface of every technological solution. That`s why this edition has a new name: Click to Success - Fast. Digital. Smart. In this edition, we are not dealing with digitization as a final stage, nor with success as a product that can be "ordered online". We deal with the in-between, what triggers the click, but also what makes it effective. In front of you is an issue that invites us to think: maybe success was never in the click, but in what we do after it. digital transformation digitization special edition newsletter special edition newsletter Click to success Fast Digital Smart Your comment Send
content_it:
Mentre preparavamo l’edizione speciale “Digitalizzazione”, ci siamo chiesti: ha ancora senso parlare di digitalizzazione nel 2025? In un’epoca in cui l’intelligenza artificiale “risolve” problemi emotivi, sanitari e aziendali, in cui algoritmi e macchine supportano decisioni, diagnosi e strategie, il termine “digitalizzazione” sembra quasi superato. Eppure non è scomparso: è diventato invisibile, talmente scontato da non essere più percepito come un processo, ma come un dato di fatto. È il livello base, il sistema operativo senza il quale non esisterebbero né l’intelligenza artificiale, né l’automazione, né le decisioni intelligenti.

Ci siamo allora domandati: il successo è davvero a portata di “clic”, o si tratta solo di un mito che il settore ci propina? Se la digitalizzazione è ormai un’infrastruttura invisibile, il “clic” ne è diventato il simbolo più visibile — non perché il successo derivi da un singolo tocco sullo schermo, ma perché il clic rappresenta metaforicamente la decisione, il coraggio di cambiare i processi e la volontà di comprendere cosa si nasconde dietro ogni soluzione tecnologica.

Questa edizione, intitolata “Click to Success – Fast. Digital. Smart”, non tratta la digitalizzazione come traguardo né il successo come un prodotto acquistabile online. Si concentra piuttosto su ciò che precede e rende efficace il clic: forse il vero successo non sta nel clic stesso, ma in ciò che facciamo subito dopo, come riportato da ekapija.com.

title_en: Serbia recording fastest growth of ICT services in region – Surplus of EUR 2.6 billion

content_en: (Photo: asharkyu/shutterstock.com) In the period January-September 2025, Serbia’s export of ICT services amounted to EUR 3.333 billion, which is a growth of 12% compared to the same period last year, said Prime Minister Djuro Macut, adding that Serbia was a leader in the region when it came to the growth and development of ICT services. – The surplus is EUR 2.624 billion. Macut pointed out that the ICT sector had long been the most successful sector in terms of growth rates. – This is a great motivation and obligation to continue developing it and move forward towards achieving even better results – Macut said. Nei primi nove mesi del 2025, le esportazioni serbe di servizi ICT hanno raggiunto i 3,333 miliardi di euro, segnando un aumento del 12% rispetto allo stesso periodo dell’anno precedente. L’espansione del settore ICT serbo rappresenta un’opportunità per le imprese italiane specializzate in tecnologie, software e servizi digitali, in un mercato in rapida crescita e con crescente domanda di competenze e soluzioni innovative.

title_en: Darko Marjanović, director of Things Solver, a member of ASEE Group - Digital workers and agentic AI are already transforming business in Serbia
title_it: AI agente trasforma le imprese serbe
content_en: Darko Marjanović (Photo: Danilo Danilović) By 2035, agent-based artificial intelligence could generate about $450 billion in enterprise software application revenue, Gartner estimates. Its practical application has already reached Serbia through the so-called digital assistants - AI agents that take over routine operations in companies, speed up processes, relieve employees and improve customer support, Darko Marjanović, director of Things Solver and a pioneer in the application of agentic AI in the region, points out in an interview for the eKapija portal. He adds that these assistants help companies overcome labor shortages, optimize costs and free up employees` time for creative and strategic tasks. We discussed how agentic AI works, where it is already being used in Serbia and what changes it will bring in the coming years. What is agentic AI and how is it different from generative or traditional AI? - Agent AI, or agentic AI, uses large language models not only to generate text, but also to perform tasks independently. For example, an AI sales agent for banking products can read a catalog with all relevant information on its own, launch an application for a customer and manage the entire process that a human would normally do. This enables companies to perform entrusted activities faster and more accurately, without the need for complex coding. Agent AI brings digital assistants closer to human capabilities, improves collaboration between people and systems, and opens up space for employees to dedicate their time to more complex and strategic tasks. In contrast to traditional AI models, which respond to individual queries, agent AI functions as a standalone operating system. It breaks down complex tasks into a series of smaller steps, executes them automatically, but leaves people with the ability to monitor and correct when necessary, making digital assistants an integrated part of teams. How does this model apply to banking, payments, and technology? - In banking, AI agents are mostly used to optimize back office processes, such as document preparation, loan approval or various checks. In this way, the risk of errors is reduced and the process is accelerated, which directly affects efficiency and customer satisfaction. For younger generations, who are used to apps and chatbots, interacting with an AI agent becomes a natural part of the process, while for older users it is still a question of trust. When it comes to payments, the technology is ready to perform transactions and more complex activities, but the key factor is user trust. It is expected to grow as AI agents are increasingly used in everyday financial interactions and as people have the opportunity to verify the system`s accuracy and security. How does agentic AI work within the Workforce Hub platform and what are the benefits? - The Workforce Hub platform was developed to enable companies to create AI agents with clearly defined skills and actions. Each agent has tasks it can perform, knowledge it relies on, and protections that prevent errors or unwanted actions. In this way, the agent can perform activities independently, while the management still has complete control over the process. The platform enables companies to monitor the work of agents, evaluate results and ensure that all activities are in accordance with internal rules and legal regulations. The advantage of this approach is that small and medium-sized companies can implement digital assistants and improve business operations without large IT resources. The Workforce Hub makes it easy to integrate agentic AI into everyday processes, connecting practical application and security into a single solution. What are the biggest benefits for companies implementing AI agents? - The most important advantage is greater operational efficiency, as the AI ​​agent takes over routine and standardized tasks, allowing employees to focus on strategic, creative and valuable activities. Additionally, agent AI reduces the possibility of errors in processes such as customer support or document processing. Digital assistants work consistently and can operate 24/7, which further improves overall efficiency. The presence of digital assistants relieves staff and allows companies to optimize costs, because sometimes one agent is sufficient for certain activities instead of new full-time employees. This is particularly important for industries facing a shortage of skilled labor, such as banking, retail or telecommunications. In which industries are AI agents currently used the most in Serbia and where is the greatest potential? - They are mostly applied in banking, telecommunications, retail, and the oil and gas sector. In these industries, there is a great need for standardized processes where digital assistants can speed up operations and improve customer support. Interest is also slowly growing in other sectors, such as hotels, human resources, employment and logistics. Any company that owns a significant amount of data or faces repetitive tasks can benefit from AI agents, as they enable faster and more accurate processing, freeing up people`s time for more complex decisions and customer interactions. How do AI agents work in practice – as a substitute for humans or as a support? - The AI agent can operate in three modes: Assistant mode: the agent supports employees and facilitates their tasks, but does not take full responsibility. People still make key decisions. Semi-autonomous mode: the agent performs certain activities, while critical steps are under human supervision. This is useful in high-risk processes like financial transactions. Fully autonomous mode: the agent independently executes all tasks within the defined procedures, with the possibility of human control when necessary. In practice, this means that employees no longer spend hours checking documentation or answering basic customer questions, which reduces stress and improves overall efficiency. Can you provide an example of a specific customer experience with AI agents? - One client even gave his AI agent a name and treats him as part of the team, which shows how integrated digital assistants are already in the day-to-day work of companies. Response time to inquiries has been reduced from tens of minutes to a few seconds, and users can now quickly find information about products or services before contacting employees. The agent is available on the web platform, tablets, in-store screens and mobile devices, which enables a consistent and high-quality user experience. This approach shows how much digital assistants can improve operations and relieve people from routine tasks. What are the next steps in development and what advice would you give to companies looking to implement AI agents - The next step in the development of agentic AI is the additional improvement of security and data access control, as well as integration with business process modeling systems. The advice to companies is to approach the implementation of AI agents in a deliberate and systematic way. It is important to clearly define the agents` tasks, centralize their management and control, and monitor the results to avoid unintended consequences. Digital assistants are not there to replace employees, but to be a support and work partner. Their application enables companies to improve operational efficiency, reduce errors and improve service quality, while leaving employees more time for more complex and creative tasks. content_it:
Entro il 2035, l’intelligenza artificiale basata su agenti potrebbe generare circa 450 miliardi di dollari di ricavi nel settore del software enterprise, secondo le stime di Gartner. In Serbia questa tecnologia è già operativa grazie agli assistenti digitali – agenti AI che svolgono operazioni routinarie, accelerano i processi, alleggeriscono il carico del personale e migliorano l’assistenza clienti, spiega Darko Marjanović, direttore di Things Solver e pioniere dell’AI agente nella regione, in un’intervista per ekapija.com.

L’AI agente si distingue dall’AI generativa o tradizionale perché non si limita a rispondere a domande, ma esegue autonomamente compiti complessi: ad esempio, un agente per prodotti bancari può consultare autonomamente un catalogo, avviare una domanda per il cliente e gestire l’intero iter che normalmente richiederebbe un operatore umano. Questo modello funziona come un sistema operativo autonomo, scomponendo attività complesse in passaggi più semplici ed eseguendoli automaticamente, pur mantenendo la supervisione umana quando necessario.

Nel settore bancario, gli agenti AI ottimizzano processi back office come la preparazione di documenti o l’approvazione di prestiti, riducendo errori e tempi di attesa. Nella piattaforma Workforce Hub, sviluppata da Things Solver, le aziende possono creare agenti con competenze specifiche, controllarne le azioni e garantire conformità normativa, anche senza grandi risorse IT.

I principali vantaggi includono maggiore efficienza operativa, riduzione degli errori, disponibilità 24/7 e ottimizzazione dei costi, particolarmente utile in settori con carenza di manodopera qualificata come banche, retail e telecomunicazioni. Gli agenti operano in tre modalità – assistente, semi-autonoma e completamente autonoma – a seconda del livello di rischio e complessità del processo.

Un esempio concreto in Serbia mostra un’azienda che ha dato un nome al proprio agente AI, integrandolo come membro del team: i tempi di risposta alle richieste sono passati da decine di minuti a pochi secondi, con un’esperienza utente coerente su web, tablet e dispositivi mobili.

Secondo Marjanović, il prossimo passo è migliorare sicurezza e controllo sull’accesso ai dati, nonché integrare gli agenti con i sistemi di modellazione dei processi aziendali. L’AI agente non sostituisce i dipendenti, ma li affianca, liberando tempo per attività strategiche e creative.

title_en: “Click to Success – Fast. Digital. Smart.” – Introducing eKapija’s new special edition newsletter
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: (Photo: eKapija) The eKapija business portal has published the special edition newsletter “Click to Success – Fast. Digital. Smart.,” in which we once again confirmed that digitalization is no longer a matter of choice, but an inevitability. It is the driver of growth, innovation and success, and companies that recognized this in time are operating much faster and more efficiently today. The thematic newsletter was implemented in partnership with AIK Bank. In this issue, read about the situation in the IT sector in Serbia, what is most hindering the digital transformation process in Montenegro, and meet some exceptional women who are shaping the IT industry in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The data center market in Europe and the region is going through the most dynamic period of development so far, under the strong influence of artificial intelligence, cloud services and digital transformation. How AI is changing the architecture of data centers, what are the key technologies of the future and how Schneider Electric is responding to new market needs, is revealed by Jelena Pejkovic, Sales Director of the Secure Power Supply Sector at that company . In the world of banking, where conversations often turn into a maze of technical terms and hidden fees, it sounds almost unexpected when a Sales Director speaks simply, openly and without calculation. This is exactly the approach that comes from Yettel Bank , where transparency is the basic product and user experience is the main strategy. We talked to Boris Samohvalov, Sales Director of Yettel Bank , about what they sell when they “hide nothing” and what the banking of the future looks like. Battery energy storage is becoming a key part of modern energy infrastructure, and ENEL PS , a company with more than 30 years of experience in developing solutions for uninterruptible and backup power supply, is already designing and implementing innovative solutions in Serbia that combine battery storage, renewable energy sources and advanced software platforms. In an interview with Gordan Vujicic, Director of Strategic Development at the company , we learn how this technology helps data centers and industrial facilities to be reliable, flexible and market-active, and what Serbia can expect in the coming years in the field of smart grids and energy storage. What does a company in Serbia need when it comes to telecommunications and ICT services? And is it possible to find all these services in one place, or is it necessary to find several suppliers? Sasa Miljatovic, Director of ICT Services at Yettel , reveals to us that, during the integration of Yettel and SBB , they combined resources, knowledge and experience to create a whole range of new services - from infrastructure, through business applications to advanced security services. This was done with one goal - to provide companies with unified solutions and become their technological partner, not just a service provider. Philip Morris International, which has been investing in the improvement of the local community since its arrival in Serbia in 2003, has recognized that supporting innovation is key to the long-term development and competitiveness of the domestic economy. For this reason, in cooperation with NALED and the Government of Serbia, StarTech was launched - a platform that shows how partnership can accelerate the path from idea to market and open doors to the world for innovators across Serbia. Tamara Milovanovic, PMI ’s General Manager for Southeast Europe , spoke to eKapija about the program’s achievements and key challenges of digitalization. Artificial intelligence is the biggest topic of this era, and Milan Jevtic, Executive Director for Technology at AIGO , shared his insights on its impact on people, business, and technology with us. He believes that our urgent task is to master new tools and principles. The sooner we are comfortable with them the more time we will have to devote to what the client wants to pay. Then we will sell our products at higher prices, they will carry greater value. And so on until some new industrial revolution and new topics of concern. By 2035, agent-based artificial intelligence could generate about USD 450 billion in revenue from enterprise software applications, according to Gartner. Its practical application is already arriving in Serbia through the so-called digital assistants – AI agents that take over routine operations in companies, speed up processes, relieve employees, and improve customer support. Darko Marjanovic, Director of Things Solver and a pioneer in the application of agent AI in the region, spoke to eKapija about how agent AI works, where it is already used in our country, and what changes it will bring in the coming years. Digitalization today is not a luxury, but a condition for survival. Companies that introduce new technologies become faster, more efficient, more accurate, and more competitive; they reduce costs, increase customer satisfaction, and open up new business models. That is why the Center for Digital Transformation was established within the Serbian Chamber of Commerce , one of the main goals of which is to help the Serbian economy, especially micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises, keep pace with global technological changes. AikBank , the largest domestic private bank, provides its clients from all segments – citizens, entrepreneurs, small and medium-sized enterprises, and corporations – with solutions that prioritize practicality and accessibility in financial management. As a bank that understands that digitalization is a priority in business, AikBank has launched several innovations for clients on the market in 2025 alone. In this special edition newsletter, you will also have the opportunity to learn about WebChrono - a system developed by Solutis , which is completely changing the way working hours and access to facilities are recorded and monitored. Instead of manual entry and paper records, employees’ entry and exit are recorded by RFID cards and a mobile application, transmitting data directly to a central database. In an era of increasingly pronounced climate change, ABB offers solutions that bring measurable energy savings and stronger resilience of key systems. Their highly efficient motors of the latest IE classes, combined with frequency converters and digital monitoring, transform processes in agriculture and industry into smart, optimized systems that consume only as much energy as necessary. In this way, ABB enables reduced emissions, greater equipment reliability and more sustainable resource management. We also addressed the topic of phishing , and the example of an employee of a Belgrade company shows us that it is no longer a mass fraud sent to thousands of addresses, but an attack aimed at specific people in a specific organization. Instead of generic emails that once easily gave away fraud, today spear phishing attacks, compromised business emails, social media scams, and SMS and WhatsApp messages that look completely legitimate dominate. We also looked at the recent participation of regional startups at the prestigious WEB Summit technology conference in Lisbon . Seven companies from Montenegro and four from Serbia presented their solutions, and the great interest of investors is a clear signal that this region has enormous potential when it comes to developing modern tools in various fields. This is confirmed by the company Dren Bio , founded by Serbs in America, which was declared the best biotechnology startup for this year. Another confirmation comes from Bosnia and Herzegovina , which ranked 91st in the Global Startup Ecosystem Index 2025 and entered the top 100 startup ecosystems for the first time . At the beginning, we already mentioned that digitalization is no longer a matter of choice, and this has been recognized by the Montenegrin state administration. Thus, this country is one of the pioneers in the region, considering that it has introduced artificial intelligence into public services. Now Chatbot Masa helps citizens and investors in the processes of legalization and issuing building permits. Also, the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) portal has been launched, where entrepreneurs and service providers can now find all the information on procedures, regulations and competent institutions required to start or conduct business in one place. title_en: Danger on the screen and one click to fraud - How did Ljiljana prevent the company from losing EUR 35,000?
title_it: Phishing mirato: come evitare frodi aziendali
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Photosani/shutterstock.com) Ljiljani, who works in the finances of a Belgrade company, recently received an email marked "URGENT" in her inbox. The director requests to immediately transfer 35,000 EUR to the account indicated in the attachment. At first glance, nothing unusual. But something didn`t give her peace. Maybe just that imposed urgency. And maybe the fact that she`s received in-house cyber security training and knows full well that any email that creates a sense of pressure, panic or urgency needs to be double-checked. She checked. The director didn`t send the email. A serious financial loss was prevented. Such scenarios have become commonplace today and the best proof that phishing is no longer an amateur message with bad spelling, but a carefully designed scam. Dr. Miloš Jovanović, professor of information security at the University of Kragujevac and president of the OpenLink Group , warns against this, as he points out that today`s attacks are "far more sophisticated and personalized than ever before". According to him, phishing is no longer a mass fraud sent to thousands of addresses, but an attack aimed at specific people in a specific organization. Instead of generic emails that once easily betrayed a scam, spear phishing attacks, business email compromises, social media scams, as well as SMS and WhatsApp messages that look completely legitimate dominate nowadays . - Phishing is no longer a mass campaign "for everyone", but a precisely targeted attack against a specific person, function or organization. Today, such attacks often include elements of social engineering, where the user is psychologically manipulated into believing in the authenticity of the communication. In addition, attackers increasingly use generative artificial intelligence in order to create messages without grammatical errors and with a convincing tone, which makes it even more difficult to recognize fraud - our interlocutor explains. The attackers prepare in detail: they use data gathered from social networks, information from previously compromised databases, imitate the communication style of executives and increasingly apply generative artificial intelligence to create messages, which seem flawless in tone and language. Because of this, says Jovanović, "the line between real and fake messages becomes extremely thin ". In such an environment, recognizing phishing calls for both technical and psychological attention . - First of all, employees should check the address of the sender, the tone of the message and possible grammatical errors, as well as links leading to suspicious domains. Any message that creates a sense of urgency or pressure ("react immediately", "the account will be blocked") should arouse suspicion - the professor emphasizes. Every second employee falls for the scam However, research shows that less than half of employees react correctly in the first seconds of contact with a suspicious message, which, according to Jovanović, clearly shows that education must be continuous and focused on practical simulations, and not on one-time presentations. When it comes to protection, companies need to build a multi-layered strategy that combines technical tools and employee awareness. - Technical measures include multi-layered protection, from advanced e-mail filters and DMARC/SPF/DKIM policies , to the introduction of multi-factor authentication (MFA) and controlled access to sensitive resources . At the organizational level, a clear security culture that includes clearly defined procedures, constant education and proactive monitoring of suspicious activities through systems for detection and response to incidents (EDR/SIEM solutions) is key - says the eKapija interlocutor. The best protection, he emphasizes, is a combination of technology and user awareness , because even the most expensive security system cannot compensate for one wrong click. - The individual protection of users through passkey systems and biometric authentication, which reduce the risk of password theft and phishing attacks, plays an increasingly important role. Such solutions allow logging in without a classic password, with identity confirmation via fingerprint, facial recognition or security key, which significantly increases the level of personal and corporate security - explains Professor Jovanović. And what if someone does click? Dr. Jovanović emphasizes that the speed of the reaction makes the decisive difference. - In practice, it is not crucial whether someone clicked, but how quickly it is reported and how the organization reacts . If there is a clear channel to report a suspicious event and if the IT team immediately isolates the device, checks the network traffic and informs other users, the harm can be completely prevented, he says The problem, however, arises when employees remain silent for fear of being blamed . That`s why, he points out, the culture of security transparency must be part of the internal policy, which should mandate that mistakes be reported immediately and without fear of sanctions. In the long term, businesses need to change the way they think about security. - It is no longer enough for the IT team to be the only one thinking about protection , but every employee must understand that they are part of the first line of defense. This means that every message, link or request for confidential data is checked without haste and without automatic trust, even if it seems legitimate. Regular, practical training of employees is crucial, but not through dry presentations and "online trainings", but through real examples and trainings that help people learn to recognize suspicious situations in their daily work. And finally, it is important that there is a clear and simple procedure for reporting suspicious messages, without fear of making a mistake, because a quick reaction often makes the difference between minor disturbances and a serious security incident - Professor Jovanović concludes. content_it:
Ljiljana, impiegata amministrativa di un’azienda di Belgrado, ha recentemente ricevuto una mail contrassegnata come “URGENTE”, in cui il direttore chiedeva il trasferimento immediato di 35.000 EUR a un conto indicato in allegato. Pur apparentemente legittima, la richiesta le è sembrata sospetta, soprattutto per l’insolita urgenza. Grazie a una formazione interna sulla sicurezza informatica, ha verificato l’autenticità della mail e ha scoperto che il direttore non l’aveva inviata, evitando così una grave perdita finanziaria.  

Come riportato da ekapija.com, episodi del genere dimostrano che il phishing oggi non è più un messaggio generico pieno di errori, ma un attacco altamente sofisticato e personalizzato. Secondo il dott. Miloš Jovanović, docente di sicurezza informatica all’Università di Kragujevac e presidente del Gruppo OpenLink, gli attacchi moderni utilizzano ingegneria sociale, intelligenza artificiale generativa e dati provenienti da social network o database compromessi per imitare con precisione lo stile comunicativo dei dirigenti aziendali.  

Per contrastare questa minaccia, le aziende devono adottare una strategia multilivello che combini filtri email avanzati, autenticazione a più fattori (MFA), politiche DMARC/SPF/DKIM e una cultura organizzativa della sicurezza basata su procedure chiare, formazione pratica continua e sistemi di monitoraggio (EDR/SIEM).  

Il professor Jovanović sottolinea che la reazione tempestiva è cruciale: anche in caso di click su un link malevolo, è fondamentale che il personale possa segnalare l’evento senza timore di sanzioni, consentendo al team IT di isolare il dispositivo e bloccare eventuali danni.  

In un contesto così complesso, la sicurezza informatica non è più solo compito del reparto IT, ma responsabilità di ogni dipendente. Per le aziende italiane, questo scenario rappresenta un’opportunità per esportare soluzioni avanzate di cybersecurity, sistemi di autenticazione biometrica e programmi formativi pratici mirati alla prevenzione del phishing mirato.

title_en: Serbia’s ICT services exports reach EUR 3.333 billion in first nine months
title_it: Export ICT serbo a 3,33 miliardi
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Pixabay / RAEng_Publications) Serbian Prime Minister Djuro Macut stated yesterday that Serbia was a leader in the region when it came to the growth and development of ICT services and that the latest data showed that in the period January-September 2025, exports of those services had amounted to EUR 3.333 billion, which is a 12% increase compared to the same period of the previous year. Macut emphasized that we should be proud of those results, adding that the surplus in that area amounted to EUR 2.624 billion, and that Serbia also had excellent results when it came to the number of employees in this sector. In the third quarter of this year, 115,933 citizens worked in this sector, which is 3,678 or 3.3% more than in the same quarter last year, the Prime Minister wrote on Instagram. The ICT sector has long been the most successful sector in terms of growth rates, he reminded, adding that it was a great incentive, but also an obligation, to continue its development and move forward towards achieving even better results. Vlada Republike Srbije Đuro Macut export of ICT services Your comment Send
content_it: Il Primo Ministro serbo Đuro Macut ha dichiarato ieri che la Serbia è leader nella regione per crescita e sviluppo dei servizi ICT. Secondo i dati più recenti, nel periodo gennaio-settembre 2025 le esportazioni di tali servizi hanno raggiunto i 3,333 miliardi di euro, con un aumento del 12% rispetto allo stesso periodo dell’anno precedente. Macut ha sottolineato che si tratta di un risultato di cui essere orgogliosi, ricordando che il surplus commerciale nel settore ammonta a 2,624 miliardi di euro. Ha inoltre evidenziato l’ottima performance del Paese per quanto riguarda l’occupazione: nel terzo trimestre del 2025 hanno lavorato nel settore ICT 115.933 cittadini, ovvero 3.678 unità in più (+3,3%) rispetto allo stesso trimestre del 2024. Il Premier ha ricordato che il settore ICT è da tempo quello con i tassi di crescita più elevati, rappresentando un forte incentivo ma anche un impegno a proseguire nello sviluppo per raggiungere risultati ancora migliori, come riportato da ekapija.com. Questa dinamica offre opportunità interessanti per le imprese italiane specializzate in tecnologie dell’informazione e della comunicazione, potenziali partner in progetti di collaborazione o investimento.

title_en: From wellness to digital security - Serbian startups attracted investors' attention in Lisbon
title_it: Startup serbe brillano al Web Summit
content_en: (Photo: Gajus/shutterstock.com) Four startups from Serbia - MyFlow, Njuppa , Codekido and FinoApp - successfully presented themselves in the prestigious Showcase program of the Web Summit in Lisbon and made the best use of the opportunity that, out of over 4,000 applicants, only 400 startups received, PKS announced. MyFlow is a science-based wellness platform that combines physical activity, music and color to rapidly rebalance the body and mind. In just 14 minutes it reduces stress, improves focus and motivation, and increases vitality, without the need for additional equipment or interruption of the work process. Tanja Lazarevic says that the MyFlow platform establishes the psycho-physical balance of a person in a very short time: - We reset both the brain and the body when a person needs it the most, depending on the current psychophysical condition. We have different programs for low energy, stress, stiffness from long sitting... - says Lazarević. The platform is based on scientific research, and user condition measurements are based on the most cited scientific tests and research results. - We consider it a great success that we managed to get a space for a showcase presentation at the Web Summit — in less than a minute we raised the audience`s energy, everyone stood up, we got a big applause and comments that their energy and focus changed in just a few minutes - Lazarevic emphasized. Presenting the FinoApp application, Sofija Drecun stated that her focus is on children`s safety and additional information about influencers: - Influencers make money online through their platforms, often across multiple platforms — be it TikTok or Instagram. What we are doing is to show their earnings in one place, instead of entering and searching each one individually - explained Drecun. She added that while they didn`t have high expectations from the Web Summit, they got a lot out of it — from discussing partnerships to connecting with influencers from other regions. Nemanja Trbović from Njuppa stated that at the Web Summit they are presenting a platform, which helps businesses to offer food that they failed to sell or that is about to expire, through the Njuppa platform. On the other side are users who "save" that food and buy it at a price up to 70 percent lower. The goal is to reduce food waste globally. - I would like to thank the Serbian Chamber of Commerce for the opportunity to attend the Web Summit and connect with partners. We already have several interesting meetings with investors - we will see what happens, but this performance is certainly a great experience - said Trbović. Gorana Radovanović stated that Codekido has developed the Nerbit platform — a control center for security operations of the new generation that enables centralized security management and process automation: - When we started this story, we were a very young, inspirational team and we wanted to encourage innovation. Our first platform is Nerbit — a kind of defense center, a defense system against everything that happens in the digital space. Together with the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, we were also at Giteks - stated Radovanović. At the Serbian stand, apart from the four mentioned startups that had special presentations, under the motto "Think Tech, Choose Serbia", also performed: Canandi , GetTrusty, NSage.ai, GuideLites (Lites), Peasy , GetData (Apparo), DigitalLeather , Tridan AI, Kampster AI, SpiceAds , Qreadible (ible), Veritium , Cloud City, Includify , KleverCargo , Smart Part , NutriMedik, HealthControl Niš , CyberParent, Motiqum and Nais Robotics . MyFlow è una piattaforma per il benessere basata su evidenze scientifiche che, in soli 14 minuti e senza attrezzature aggiuntive, riduce lo stress, migliora concentrazione e vitalità combinando movimento, musica e colore. La fondatrice Tanja Lazarević ha sottolineato il successo della loro presentazione, che ha generato entusiasmo e applausi dal pubblico. FinoApp, presentata da Sofija Drecun, offre trasparenza sugli introiti degli influencer online, aggregando dati da diverse piattaforme. Infine, Codekido ha sviluppato Nerbit, un centro di controllo di nuova generazione per la sicurezza informatica, che permette gestione centralizzata e automazione dei processi di difesa digitale, come spiegato da Gorana Radovanović. Oltre a queste, altre 20 startup serbe erano presenti allo stand nazionale con lo slogan "Think Tech, Choose Serbia". La crescente vitalità dell'ecosistema tech serbo rappresenta un'opportunità interessante per le imprese italiane attive nei settori della sicurezza digitale, dell’innovazione agroalimentare e delle tecnologie per il benessere.

title_en: Bosnia and Herzegovina first time in the top 100 startup ecosystem - Fintech and health tech lead development
title_it: Startup in crescita in Bosnia-Erzegovina
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Pixabay.com/Gerd Altmann) Bosnia and Herzegovina ranked 91st on the Global Startup Ecosystem Index 2025, which represents a shift of five positions compared to the previous year, with an annual growth rate of 27.8%, according to data from StartupBlink. Currently, 56 startups are operating in the country, with the support of 15 coworking spaces, 3 accelerators and one startup organization. The startup scene is not yet concentrated in a single industry - companies are active in e-commerce, blockchain, HR and IT outsourcing. Experts assess that Sarajevo, with adequate support and simplified administrative procedures, can become the leading technological center in the region. The most developed industry among Bosnian startups is fintech, with nine startups, accounting for 16% of the overall scene. This area positions Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 78th place globally and 17th in Eastern Europe. Of particular note is Rolla, a fitness tech startup that secured a record 6.3 million euros in seed investment in 2023 - which is the biggest amount ever invested in a fitness and health tech startup in Central and Eastern Europe. Analysts believe that further development of the startup ecosystem in Bosnia and Herzegovina depends on improving administrative procedures, greater investor support and the creation of a network for connecting entrepreneurs. content_it: La Bosnia-Erzegovina si è classificata al 91º posto nell’Indice Globale degli Ecosistemi Startup 2025, guadagnando cinque posizioni rispetto all’anno precedente, con un tasso di crescita annuo del 27,8%, secondo i dati di StartupBlink. Attualmente operano nel Paese 56 startup, sostenute da 15 spazi di coworking, 3 acceleratori e un’organizzazione dedicata. Il panorama imprenditoriale non è ancora concentrato in un unico settore: le aziende sono attive nell’e-commerce, nella blockchain, nell’outsourcing HR e IT. Gli esperti ritengono che Sarajevo, con un adeguato sostegno e procedure amministrative semplificate, possa diventare il principale hub tecnologico della regione. Il settore più sviluppato è il fintech, con nove startup (16% del totale), che colloca il Paese al 78º posto a livello globale e al 17º nell’Europa orientale. Da segnalare Rolla, una startup nel campo della fitness tech, che nel 2023 ha raccolto 6,3 milioni di euro in finanziamenti seed, il più alto investimento mai registrato per una startup del settore salute e benessere nell’Europa centro-orientale. Secondo gli analisti, lo sviluppo futuro dell’ecosistema dipenderà dal miglioramento delle procedure amministrative, da un maggiore sostegno da parte degli investitori e dalla creazione di reti per la connessione tra imprenditori, come riportato da ekapija.com. Per le imprese italiane attive nei settori fintech, health tech e digitalizzazione, questa crescita rappresenta un’opportunità di collaborazione e investimento in un mercato in rapida evoluzione.

title_en: Saša Miljatović, Director of ICT Services at Yettel - Our Company as a Technology Partner in Business, not just a Service Provider
title_it: Yettel: partner tecnologico per le imprese
content_en: Saša Miljatović (Photo: Yettel) What does a company in Serbia need when it comes to telecommunication and ICT services? And is it possible to find all these services in one place, or is it necessary to find several suppliers? We talk about it with Saša Miljatović, director of ICT services at Yettel . After e&PPF Telekom Group, which owns Yettel , also bought SBB earlier this year, your two companies started the integration process. What does this mean for small and large companies that have been your customers so far? - When we started the integration of Yettel and SBB, one of the first things we did was to look at how we can act jointly towards business users. We have combined resources, knowledge and experience and have created a whole range of new services - from infrastructure to business applications to advanced security services. Our goal is to provide companies with unified solutions, from network infrastructure, through data storage and protection, to IT services with capacities available at any time. To become their technology partner, not just a service provider. What does it mean in practice for a smaller company, for example? - To put it in the simplest language – everything it needs. We offer unified telecommunication and ICT services, and we are here to be a full support during the entire process, not only during the service introduction. We can provide all workstations for employees, including computers, laptops, tablets and phones. We offer not only hardware, but also overall maintenance: help desk, system administration, device monitoring, software installation and updates, as well as security protection like antivirus and endpoint protection. To praktično znači da preuzimamo ulogu njihovog IT sektora. Brinemo o svakom uređaju, svakoj radnoj stanici i svakom zaposlenom, kako bi mala kompanija mogla da radi bez zastoja i bez potrebe da ima sopstveni IT tim. What are the benefits of your offer? And how reliable and stable is it compared to other solutions on the market? - Our infrastructure is one of the most complex ICT "stacks" in Serbia, which is to be expected for an operator of our size. For years, we have invested in a network, data centers and platforms that support millions of users and are available at all times. Now we are transferring that experience to business users. We use the technologies and systems of global vendors whose solutions are among the most reliable in the industry. Our data centers are built to extremely high security standards and have multiple levels of protection, access control, constant surveillance and are resistant to various risks. Thanks to this infrastructure, we provide business users with a stable service, quick elimination of potential incidents and continuous improvement of the system. In short, we offer them our know-how and experience in working on high-capacity and complex systems, which is the strongest guarantee of reliability. What is the most important thing for companies to know when choosing ICT solutions? - A reliable ICT environment is based on three principles: secure data storage, stable infrastructure and clear management procedures. This is a big difference compared to the situation when the server is kept in the company`s office, without adequate protection against physical and cyber risks. Our data centers have a specially designed security ecosystem, which includes fire and flood protection, advanced access control, and continuous monitoring. In addition, our network is designed to ensure high availability and business continuity. Smaller companies, as well as larger companies, get an environment where their data is protected and services are constantly available, regardless of unexpected situations. What are the concrete benefits for business users who opt for such solutions (from smaller companies to large enterprises)? - The advantages are numerous and, I would say, very concrete. First, the user gets a top quality service that is secure, stable and fully supported by our expert team. In addition to standard maintenance and monitoring, we provide all users with personalized, expert support from engineers with many years of industry experience, so they can focus on their business without worrying about IT problems. Second, he does not have to invest in its own infrastructure, which significantly optimizes costs. Third, he gets a unified service without the need to work with multiple different providers or deal with maintenance and planning. Backup, monitoring, security policies and system modernization come as part of the service. For small companies, this means a simpler and more accessible path to professional ICT solutions, while for large enterprises it brings space for improving existing capacities, security and reliability that they cannot achieve with internal infrastructure alone. How do you see the further development of ICT services in Serbia and what technologies, in your opinion, will shape the coming years? - In the coming period, two areas will be key, namely "cloud" and security. "Cloud" solutions are being adopted more and more quickly, because they allow companies flexibility, faster service introduction and cost optimization. However, with that growth comes greater security challenges, so "cloud" security will be one of the central topics. Another trend is artificial intelligence. In the next five years, we expect a wider application of AI services on our market, from process automation to analytics and optimization of business decisions. This raises the issue of data security and responsible use of AI technologies again. That`s why I believe that in the coming years, services that put cloud, advanced security services and AI solutions at the fore will be highlighted, because they will enable companies to work more efficiently, smarter and faster. content_it:
Saša Miljatović, direttore dei Servizi ICT di Yettel, illustra la trasformazione dell’azienda da semplice fornitore di servizi a partner tecnologico per le imprese in Serbia. A seguito dell’acquisizione di SBB da parte del gruppo e&PPF Telekom, proprietario di Yettel, è iniziato un processo di integrazione volto a offrire soluzioni unificate per le aziende di ogni dimensione. L’obiettivo è fornire servizi completi, dalla infrastruttura di rete all’archiviazione e protezione dei dati, fino alla gestione IT completa, inclusi dispositivi, manutenzione, aggiornamenti e protezione avanzata.

Per le piccole imprese, ciò significa poter delegare interamente la gestione IT, evitando di dover mantenere un team interno. L’infrastruttura di Yettel, tra le più avanzate in Serbia, si basa su data center con elevati standard di sicurezza, ridondanza e monitoraggio continuo, garantendo stabilità e continuità operativa. I clienti beneficiano di supporto personalizzato da ingegneri esperti, ottimizzazione dei costi grazie all’assenza di investimenti infrastrutturali iniziali e gestione centralizzata di backup, sicurezza e aggiornamenti.

Miljatović sottolinea che il futuro dei servizi ICT in Serbia sarà guidato dal cloud, dalla sicurezza informatica e dall’intelligenza artificiale, con un’enfasi crescente sulla protezione dei dati e sull’uso responsabile delle nuove tecnologie. Come riportato da ekapija.com, questa evoluzione apre opportunità per le imprese italiane specializzate in soluzioni cloud, cybersecurity e servizi IT avanzati, grazie alla crescente domanda di partner tecnologici affidabili nel mercato serbo.

title_en: Two billion euros of French investments in Serbia – From subway and nuclear energy to supercomputers
title_it: Investimenti francesi in Serbia: 2 miliardi di euro
content_en: Illustration (Photo: Pixabay /  jacqueline macou) France is increasingly strengthening its economic presence in Serbia, with more than 130 companies and investments that account for two-thirds of total French investments in the Western Balkans, said the director of the French-Serbian Chamber of Commerce, Sanja Ivanic. According to her, Serbia is a key country for the French presence in the Western Balkans, while French companies in our country are implementing large and long-term projects that further strengthen the economic cooperation between the two countries. – Last year, trade between our two countries was somewhere close to EUR 2 billion. It has more than doubled in the last 10 years, which is a sign that Serbia is a very interesting country for France and for French investors – says Ivanic. Ivanic reminded of one of the largest French investments, the entry of the company Vinci into the Belgrade Airport in 2018, worth EUR 800 million. The latest meeting between presidents Aleksandar Vucic and Emmanuel Macron, as Ivanic points out, showed that the economic cooperation between the two countries is entering an even more dynamic phase. A special focus was on accelerating already launched strategic projects, including the Belgrade subway (in cooperation with Alstom and RATP Dev), the wastewater treatment plant in Veliko Selo (implemented by Suez and Vinci Grand Projet), energy projects, from the development of smart grids to low-carbon technologies and cooperation in the field of nuclear energy. France, as one of the world leaders in the field of nuclear energy (EDF), has already signed a strategic agreement with Serbia on the development of the energy sector. – This year, a conference dedicated to nuclear energy will be held as part of the French Week, where the establishment of a legal and regulatory framework, the development of domestic personnel and labor, with the support of French experts, the inclusion of Serbian companies in supply chains, which could enable them to participate in regional and European projects – she says. Serbia and France are also deepening cooperation in the field of innovation. The Serbian government has signed a contract with the French company Bull/Atos to purchase the BullSequana XH3000 supercomputer, which will be installed in a data center in Kragujevac. This system will support the development of artificial intelligence, as well as the digitalization of healthcare, energy and infrastructure. – The goal is for this supercomputer and the so-called AI factors to be part of Serbia’s national strategy for the development of artificial intelligence and support the development of sectors in our country and digitalization, such as the digitalization of the healthcare sector, the energy sector, and infrastructure, so we will have the BullSequana XH3000 supercomputer installed in the data center in Kragujevac – says Ivanic.
