title_it: 86% dei serbi favorevole al sistema di deposito cauzionale
title_rs: Globalno istraživanje: 86 odsto građana Srbije podržava povraćaj ambalaže
content_it:
Secondo un’indagine globale condotta da Every Can Counts, l’86% dei cittadini serbi sostiene l’introduzione di un sistema di deposito cauzionale (DRS) per il recupero degli imballaggi, il livello di consenso più alto tra i 16 Paesi coinvolti nello studio. L’indagine, che ha coinvolto oltre 16.000 persone, evidenzia che a livello globale il 71% dei cittadini appoggia il DRS, noto in Serbia come sistema cauzionale, e l’88% ritiene che gli imballaggi restituiti tramite questo sistema vengano riciclati in modo efficace. Inoltre, l’87% degli intervistati ritiene che tutti gli imballaggi monouso – lattine, bottiglie in vetro e PET – debbano essere inclusi nel sistema per tutelare l’ambiente.

In Serbia, 9 cittadini su 10 considerano il DRS il metodo più efficace per riciclare gli imballaggi per bevande, e il 58% auspica un modello in cui il deposito sia proporzionale alla dimensione della confezione, a dimostrazione della richiesta di un sistema equo e incentivante. Altri Paesi con alti tassi di approvazione includono Brasile (85%), Grecia (83%), Belgio (82%) e Ungheria (80%). Tuttavia, solo il 17% degli intervistati sa che la lattina in alluminio è l’imballaggio più riciclabile, con un tasso globale di riciclo del 71%.

Come riportato da novaekonomija.rs, secondo Alessandra Williams, presidente di “Every Can Counts”, l’adozione crescente di DRS migliora la qualità dei materiali raccolti e riduce l’inquinamento nella filiera del riciclo, permettendo a un numero sempre maggiore di lattine di tornare a nuova vita. Il 71% degli intervistati dichiara inoltre di essere più propenso a riciclare se il processo è semplice, divertente o associato a incentivi. David Van Heuverswyn, direttore globale del progetto, sottolinea che i cittadini desiderano contribuire al cambiamento, ma vogliono vedere un impatto concreto del proprio impegno: il DRS rappresenta un primo passo per unire consumatori, industria e istituzioni verso un obiettivo comune.

L’elevato sostegno al sistema cauzionale in Serbia potrebbe rappresentare un’opportunità per aziende italiane attive nel settore del riciclo, delle tecnologie per la gestione dei rifiuti e della produzione di imballaggi sostenibili.
content_rs: Srbija 08.11.2025. 10:07 Čak 86 odsto građana Srbije podržava uvođenje sistema povraćaja ambalaže (DRS), što je najviši nivo podrške među svim zemljama obuhvaćenim globalnim istraživanjem Every Can Counts (Svaka limenka se računa). Prema istraživanju, koje je obuhvatilo više od 16.000 učesnika u 16 zemalja, 71 odsto ljudi širom sveta podržava DRS sistem, kod nas poznatiji kao kaucioni sistem (sistem povraćaja depozita). Takođe, 88 odsto ispitanika veruje da se ambalaža vraćena kroz DRS efikasno reciklira. Dalje, 87 odsto ispitanika smatra da sva ambalažu za jednokratnu upotrebu (limenke, staklene i PET boce) trebalo da bude uključena u DRS radi zaštite životne sredine. “Za polovinu ispitanika, cirkularna ambalaža podrazumeva da se reciklira u isti proizvod iznova i iznova, dok 57% ispitanika veruje da cirkularna ambalaža podrazumeva pametan dizajn koji omogućava njeno lako recikliranje i ponovnu upotrebu materijala”, dodaje se u saopštenju. Građani Srbije pružaju najveću podršku DRS-u Građani Srbije pokazuju najveću podršku DRS-u od svih zemalja koje su obuhvaćene istraživanjem – čak 86 odsto . Konkretno, 9 od deset ispitanika u Srbiji veruje da bi DRS sistem bio najefikasniji način reciklaže ambalaže za piće. Pored toga, 58 odsto ispitanika u Srbiji zalaže se za sistem u kojem bi iznos depozita bio veći za ambalažu većeg formata, odnosno da se vrednost povraćaja povećava u skladu sa veličinom ambalaže – što pokazuje da građani žele pravedan i podsticajan model koji dodatno motiviše na reciklažu. Pored Srbije, i ispitanici iz drugih zemalja iskazali su visoku podršku DRS-u. Tako je 85 odsto ispitanika iz Brazila iskazalo podršku DRS-u. Tu su i Grčka (83 odsto), Belgija (82) i Mađarska (80). Ipak, samo 17 odsto ispitanika zna da je aluminijumska limenka najreciklabilnija ambalaža. Preciznije, aluminijumska limenka ambalaža je sa najvećom stopom reciklaže u odnosu na sva druga pakovanja – 71 odsto je globalna stopa njenog recikliranja. „Kako sve više zemalja uvodi DRS, povećava se kvalitet sakupljenog materijala i smanjuje zagađenje u lancu reciklaže. To znači da sve više limenki može ponovo postati nova limenka – i da sve manje završava na deponijama“, istakla je Aleksandra Vilijams, predsednica projekta “Svaka limenka se računa”. Prema istraživanju, 71 odsto ispitanika kaže da bi više reciklirali kada bi proces bio jednostavniji, zabavniji ili povezan sa nagradama. „Ljudi žele da učestvuju u promeni, ali žele i da osete da njihov trud ima smisla. Sistemi povraćaja ambalaže su prvi korak ka tome – oni povezuju potrošače, industriju i državu u zajedničkom cilju“, rekao je izjavio je Dejvid Van Heuversvyn, globalni direktor projekta. title_it: Aumenteranno le accise sui carburanti nel 2026?
title_rs: Da li će i koliko porasti akcize na gorivo – država želi veće prihode nego ove godine
content_it: Secondo il progetto di bilancio adottato dal governo serbo, nel 2026 le entrate derivanti dalle accise ammonteranno a 453,3 miliardi di dinari (circa 3,8 miliardi di euro), pari al 19% delle entrate fiscali totali previste. La componente principale proviene dalle accise sui derivati del petrolio (244 miliardi di dinari), seguita da quelle sui prodotti del tabacco (154 miliardi) e da altre accise, tra cui quella sull’elettricità, fissata al 7,5% del consumo. Le entrate dalle accise sui carburanti sono stimate in aumento del 3,8% rispetto alle previsioni per il 2025, nonostante le sanzioni statunitensi imposte alla Naftna industrija Srbije (NIS) a causa della proprietà russa. Il bilancio prevede un adeguamento annuale delle accise all’inflazione dell’anno precedente, stimata intorno al 3%. Ljubodrag Savić, professore della Facoltà di Economia, sottolinea che, sebbene i prezzi dei carburanti siano attualmente bloccati da un decreto governativo, potrebbero aumentare in futuro qualora l’approvvigionamento risultasse compromesso dalle sanzioni. L’economista Milan Kovačević osserva che un aumento dell’IVA sui carburanti sarebbe stato più efficace per incrementare le entrate, poiché l’accisa è un importo fisso per litro. Attualmente, l’accisa è di 70,11 dinari per litro di benzina e 72,09 per il gasolio. Il testo di bilancio per il 2026 sarà discusso dal Parlamento entro la fine di novembre, secondo quanto annunciato dal ministro delle Finanze Siniša Mali. Come riportato da novaekonomija.rs, si prevede comunque il mantenimento del rimborso delle accise per gli agricoltori, subordinato alla regolare fornitura del mercato interno. Per le imprese italiane attive nel settore energetico e della distribuzione di carburanti, la situazione serba evidenzia potenziali opportunità legate all’eventuale ristrutturazione del mercato derivante dalle sanzioni su NIS.
content_rs: Srbija 12.11.2025. 08:55 U državnu kasu će, kako je isplanirano budžetom, naredne godine biti uplaćeno više od tri milijarde evra na ime akciza. Dobar deo ovih prihoda, zapravo najveći, iznose akcize na gorivo. Interesantno je da država planira uvećane prihode od akciza u odnosu na tekuću godinu, uprkos neizvesnoj situaciji sa NIS-om, koji je odnedavno pod sankcijama. Ipak, stručnjaci ukazuju na to da će se veći prihodi dostići uvećanjem ovog nameta. Akcize su značajan prihod države, i predstavljaju posebnu vrstu poreza, koji se plaća prilikom kupovine goriva, cigareta, alkohola, ali i za potrošnju struje. U narednoj godini, vidi se u predlogu budžeta koji je usvojila Vlada Srbije, planirani su prihodi od akciza u iznosu od 453,3 milijarde dinara, odnosno oko 3,8 milijardi evra. Od toga, 154 milijarde dinara su akcize na duvanske proizvode. Potom, 55,3 milijarde su ostale akcize, među koje spada i struja, koja je ove godine poskupela, pa je samim tim povećan i iznos koji svaki potrošač plaća za ovaj namet, a koji se naplaćuje u iznosu od 7,5 odsto od iznosa utrošene električne energije (i različitih taksi koje se plaćaju kroz račun). Ipak, najveći deo ovog prihoda dolazi od akcize na naftne derivate – 244 milijarde dinara. Ukupno, akcize će činiti oko 19 odsto svih poreskih prihoda planiranih u 2026. godini. Uvećani prihodi od akciza na gorivo Planirani prihodi od akcize na naftne derivate u 2026. godini veći su za 3,8 odsto u odnosu na procenu ovih prihoda u 2025. godini. “Promet naftnih derivata tokom 2025. godine je stabilizovan, pa je tekuća potrošnja dobra osnova za planiranje prihoda od akciza u narednom periodu. Za budžetsku 2026. godinu projekcija prihoda od akciza na derivate nafte pretpostavlja nepromenjen obim potrošnje i iznose akciza koji će, u skladu sa važećom regulativom, biti usklađeni sa inflacijom iz prethodne godine”, navodi se u obrazloženju budžeta. Takođe, nastaviće se primena povrata akcize na gorivo koje kupuju poljoprivrednici, ali “pod pretpostavkom nesmetanog snabdevanja domaćeg tržišta svim potrebnim vrstama i količinama naftnih derivata”. Sledi povećanje akciza Profesor Ekonomskog fakulteta Ljubodrag Savić kaže za Novu ekonomiju da će redovno godišnje usklađivanje akcize sa inflacijom iznositi upravo onoliko koliko povećanje očekuje vlast. “Usklađivanje se radi u skladu sa inflacijom, koja je tri odsto, plus-minus jedan procenat. Dakle, to je otprilike onoliko koliko se u budžetu navodi da će biti povećanje prihoda od akciza”, kaže Savić. Međutim, sagovornik Nove ekonomije ne isključuje mogućnost da cene goriva u narednoj godini budu više , imajući u vidu činjenicu da je Naftna industrija Srbije pod američkim sankcijama zbog ruskog vlasništva. “NIS radio ili ne radio, mi ćemo naftu uvoziti. Ipak, može da se desi teži uvoz zbog sankcija, pitanje je kakva će biti mogućnost nabavke, da li ćemo moći dovoljno iz Evrope da uvezemo, a konačno, skuplje je da se uvozi sirova nafta, pa da se onda ona prerađuje. U konačnici, derivati koje će potrošači kupovati biće skuplji ”, objašnjava Savić. On dodaje da sada postoji Vladina uredba kojom su cene benzina i dizela ograničene, ali da ona može da bude ukinuta, i tada će gorivo moći da poskupi. Međutim, čini se da vlast na takav scenario ne računa, imajući u vidu da je planirano povećanje prihoda od akciza u skladu sa inflacijom. Da će povećanje akcize biti način na koji će država ostvariti veće prihode, smatra i ekonomista Milan Kovačević . “Međutim, ako država hoće da uveća svoje prihode, bilo bi logičnije da je uvećala PDV na naftne derivate, jer se ovaj iznos naplaćuje u određenom procentu na cenu, dok je akciza fiksni iznos koji se plaća po litru goriva”, kaže Kovačević. Inače, akciza akciza na benzin trenutno iznosi 70,11 dinara po litru. Ovaj namet nešto je skuplji za dizel, pa je akciza 72,09 dinara po litru. Podsećamo, Vlada Srbije usvojila je prošle nedelje nacrt budžeta za 2026. godinu . Preostalo je da ga usvoje i poslanici u Skupštini, a prema najavama ministra finansija Siniše Malog, on će se naći na dnevnom redu krajem novembra. title_en: What makes Savina Residences an ideal investment opportunity?
title_it: Savina Residences: opportunità immobiliare a Obrenovac
content_en: (Photo: Savina Residences) A unique opportunity for investors is available in Obrenovac, only 30 kilometers from the center of Belgrade: a plot with the developed Savina Residences project, ready for the realization of a modern residential and business complex. This 2.4 ha plot in the heart of Obrenovac`s green belt, next to the Sava River, represents an ideal location for developers and construction companies, who want to develop a condominium or residential-business complex with modern infrastructure. The site combines the best of two worlds: peace and nature along the river and green areas, and at the same time the proximity of urban facilities, schools, kindergartens and main roads. The plot is only a 30-minute drive from the center of Belgrade and Nikola Tesla International Airport, in the vicinity of the Miloš Veliki highway and future development points such as the National Stadium and the space planned for EXPO 2027. Key project benefits High potential of the location: a quiet part of the city with excellent connectivity, in the immediate vicinity of urban amenities and natural attractions. Ready planning documentation: the developed urban-technical project enables a quick start of construction and shortens the implementation process. Flexibility in development: suitable for luxury residential units, combined residential-business premises or premium apartment concept; the possibility of increasing commercial contents or other dominant commercial purpose (shopping center). Safe investment: constant growth in demand for quality housing in Obrenovac ensures high return and profitability. (Photo: Savina Residences) What does Savina Residences offer? Savina Residences is a future condominium that combines contemporary architecture, thoughtful urban concept and a clear vision of a family community. The complex was designed with a landscaped park of about 2,000 m2, closed access system and 24/7 security, which provides residents with carelessness and a sense of community. In addition to peaceful surroundings and rich green areas, the Savina Residences project also offers a variety of facilities for all ages - from children`s playgrounds and sports fields to fitness trails and recreation areas. Schools, kindergartens, shopping centers and business complexes are located in the immediate vicinity, and the Sava River and the Zabrana Forest are only a few minutes away , which further contributes to the quality of life in this part of Obrenovac. (Photo: Savina Residences) Ideal investment opportunity The project`s special potential is reflected in its investment value. The location has more than 23,000 m2 of surface area and the possibility of developing up to 60,000 m2 of gross space , which makes it extremely attractive for strategic investors, construction companies and investment funds. Apart from the residential part, the project also offers significant potential for the development of commercial contents , which sets Savina Residences apart as a location with wider development possibilities. On the plot, it is possible to plan shopping centers, smaller retail formats, business units, as well as private health facilities and diagnostic centers, the demand for which is constantly increasing , especially in the parts of the city that are experiencing intensive residential growth. Such facilities not only improve the quality of life of future tenants, but they also contribute to the long-term value and sustainability of the investment , because they create a self-sustaining microsystem in which daily needs are available within the complex itself. Savina Residences is designed in a way that it can be adjusted to the needs of investors and markets - whether it is developed as a predominantly residential complex with accompanying amenities, or as a combined residential-business concept with a larger share of commercial capacity. Flexibility in planning allows investors to shape the final concept according to their own business strategy and target group, depending on market dynamics. For investors, this area offers a clear market logic: Obrenovac is a part of Belgrade with a stable local market, above-average wages and a constant influx of new residents. The sustainable growth of demand for new types of housing, especially condominiums with infrastructure and security, makes Savina Residences one of the most promising development locations in the vicinity of the capital. Along with geographic and infrastructural potential, the project also offers investment security in a segment that records constant growth in value. Investing in Savina Residences means investing in the future, in an area where family peace, business functionality and long-term value meet in one place. For more information, a detailed presentation of the project and all conditions of sale, visit: www.savina.rs or contact via e-mail: office@savina.rs . A Obrenovac, a soli 30 chilometri dal centro di Belgrado, è disponibile un'opportunità di investimento unica: un terreno di 2,4 ettari con il progetto già sviluppato “Savina Residences”, pronto per la realizzazione di un moderno complesso residenziale e direzionale. Situato nella cintura verde della città e adiacente al fiume Sava, il lotto unisce tranquillità e natura alla prossimità di infrastrutture urbane, scuole, asili e vie di comunicazione principali. È a soli 30 minuti dal centro di Belgrado e dall’aeroporto internazionale Nikola Tesla, vicino all’autostrada Miloš Veliki e ai futuri poli di sviluppo come lo Stadio Nazionale e l’area prevista per EXPO 2027.

Il progetto offre documentazione urbanistica già approvata, consentendo un avvio rapido dei lavori, e grande flessibilità: è adatto per residenze di lusso, complessi misti residenziali-commerciali o concept di appartamenti premium, con la possibilità di ampliare le componenti commerciali, inclusi centri commerciali, negozi, uffici o strutture sanitarie private, in linea con la crescente domanda legata all’espansione residenziale della zona.

La superficie totale supera i 23.000 m², con potenziale di sviluppo fino a 60.000 m² di superficie lorda, rendendolo particolarmente interessante per investitori strategici, imprese edili e fondi immobiliari. La domanda costante di alloggi di qualità a Obrenovac, città con salari sopra la media e afflusso stabile di nuova popolazione, garantisce redditività e sicurezza dell’investimento.

Savina Residences è concepito come una comunità familiare con circa 2.000 m² di parco attrezzato, accesso controllato e sicurezza h24, arricchita da aree ricreative per tutte le età. La vicinanza al fiume Sava e alla foresta di Zabrana ne accresce il valore abitativo.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, il progetto rappresenta una delle location più promettenti nei dintorni della capitale serba. Per le imprese italiane del settore edile e dello sviluppo immobiliare, questa opportunità offre un contesto stabile e in crescita, con potenziale per partnership o investimenti diretti in un mercato in espansione.

title_en: Dušan Milosavljević, director of Marera's concrete production division: Two decades of reliable partnership in building Belgrade
title_it: Marera rafforza il mercato del calcestruzzo a Belgrado
content_en: (Photo: Marera) High quality, reliability and effective delivery are the principles which form the core of Marera Division`s fresh concrete production business, which operated under the Beton plus brand until last year. With more than 20 years of tradition, the division is one of the leaders in the production and delivery of concrete on the Belgrade construction market. The division`s portfolio consists of successfully implemented projects - from residential and commercial to public infrastructure projects. About past success, business within Marera, available resources and capacities, strategic plans for the future, we talk with Dušan Milosavljević, director of the Marera division for concrete production . How is the first year of operation of the Marera division for concrete production going? - So far, we have achieved intense growth and very visible results, which are the result of the expansion of the client base and participation in large projects. The focus was on the improvement of each segment of business - from manufacturing processes and quality control to logistics and client relations. We paid special attention to modernization of equipment and optimization of processes, which contributed to higher efficiency and reliability of delivery. Thanks to a dedicated team and clearly set objectives, in the first nine months of this year, we achieved double-digit percentage growth. These results confirm that we are consistently building a stable and competitive position on the market, based on quality, reliability and the trust of our partners. What impact on the development and positioning of the Division for Concrete Production has functioning within a large and integrated system such as Marera? - Functioning within a strong system like Marera has an extremely positive influence on the development of the division. Thanks to the stable and well-organized group structure, we have strong support in all business segments - from finance and procurement to marketing and project management. In just eight years, Marera has built a recognizable portfolio of brownfield commercial buildings, with more than 100,000 m² of renovated space, including buildings of historical importance. Such experience and capacity make the system an extremely reliable environment for our division. An integrated platform for development, construction and facility management has enabled us to fully focus on our core business – concrete production, increasing the number of projects and strengthening operational capacities. (Photo: Marera) Today, Belgrade is rapidly developing through numerous infrastructural and commercial projects. Which projects would you single out as the most important references ? - The leading position is a great privilege for us, but also a responsibility to continue to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, reliability and quality in delivering standard, pumped and special concrete. So far, we have built strong references and gained the trust of a large number of clients and partners. The concrete produced in our factories is used in the realization of the most diverse projects - from public infrastructural, through commercial to the construction of modern residential complexes. Among them are Belgrade on the water, Soul 64, Ozon residence, National Stadium, Delta District, Lastavice, Nemanja grad, West Gate, Expo 2027 and others. We are proud that thanks to these and other projects, our concrete has become part of the urban transformation of Belgrade and synonymous with quality, reliability and longevity in the construction industry. Bearing in mind all the projects you mentioned, what kind of capacities do you have in order to be able to satisfy such a demanding and dynamic market as the Belgrade one? - We have three LIEBHERR concrete plants with a total capacity of 360 m³/h. We use 36 mixer trucks for fast and efficient transport of fresh concrete to the construction site, while we have 9 auto-pumps for pumping concrete to high or hard-to-reach locations. At the end of last year, we renewed our fleet by purchasing four new Volvo mixers, in which we invested half a million euros. In this way, we further improved the efficiency of delivery and enabled timely supply of fresh concrete to our clients. Our distribution and delivery fleet is the second largest in Belgrade. We invest in equipment and capacity to ensure top quality and reliability. The investment in capacities allowed us to reach the total production of last year in 9 months of this year. All of this would not be possible if we did not have a professional and dedicated team of people whose precision, coordination and care about deadlines ensure that every client is satisfied with our service. We are proud of the fact that even after the integration, we have kept the same team in which we have great confidence and with whom we continue to build success together. What are the division`s plans in the coming period? Are you considering expanding to other local markets? - We maintain high standards and constantly work on improving all key processes and capacities of our personnel, in order to do responsible and sustainable business. The company`s focus is on further strengthening its position on the Belgrade market, and we plan to transfer decades of expertise, what we are best at, to new markets, creating value for everyone we do business with. L’elevata qualità, l’affidabilità e la puntualità nelle consegne sono i pilastri su cui si fonda l’attività della divisione calcestruzzo di Marera, operativa fino allo scorso anno con il marchio Beton Plus. Con oltre 20 anni di esperienza, la divisione è tra i leader nella produzione e consegna di calcestruzzo fresco nel mercato edilizio di Belgrado, avendo realizzato con successo progetti residenziali, commerciali e infrastrutturali.

Dušan Milosavljević, direttore della divisione, ha dichiarato che nei primi nove mesi dell’anno in corso si è registrata una crescita a doppia cifra, grazie all’ampliamento della clientela, alla partecipazione a grandi progetti e alla modernizzazione degli impianti. L’integrazione nel gruppo Marera, attivo con oltre 100.000 m² di immobili ristrutturati in otto anni, ha fornito solide basi in termini di supporto finanziario, logistico e gestionale.

Tra i progetti di rilievo figurano Belgrade on the Water, Soul 64, Ozon Residence, lo Stadio Nazionale, Delta District, Lastavice, Nemanja Grad, West Gate ed Expo 2027. Per soddisfare le esigenze di un mercato dinamico come quello di Belgrado, la divisione dispone di tre impianti LIEBHERR con capacità complessiva di 360 m³/h, 36 betoniere (di cui quattro nuove Volvo acquistate con un investimento di 500.000 euro) e 9 autopompe, costituendo la seconda flotta più grande della città.

Pur focalizzandosi sul consolidamento della posizione a Belgrado, Marera prevede di trasferire la propria esperienza decennale ad altri mercati locali. Come riportato da ekapija.com, le imprese italiane attive nel settore delle macchine per l’edilizia, del calcestruzzo preconfezionato e della logistica per le costruzioni potrebbero trovare opportunità di collaborazione con gruppi strutturati come Marera, che privilegiano standard qualitativi elevati e partnership affidabili.

title_en: Two companies to carry out reconstruction of Pupin’s House – Investment worth 61 million dinars
title_it: Ricostruzione Casa Pupin: appalto da 61 milioni di dinari
content_en: (Photo: Print screen / Google maps) The public procurement of works announced by the Zrenjanin City Administration has been completed. The companies Asing from Belgrade and Crna Trava gradnja from Crna Trava, as the only bidders, were awarded the job of reconstructing, renovating and repurposing the building at 9 Kej 2. oktobra Street in Zrenjanin, known as Pupin’s House. Repurposing into Youth Center Pupin's House should be converted into a public facility - the Central Banat Youth Center “Mihajlo Pupin,” i.e. into a modern space intended for young people - for the implementation of free youth content, coordination of youth associations and support for the work of youth organizations. The total value of the works is 61,317,012 dinars including VAT. The public call for bids, which the Zrenjanin City Administration announced three months ago, has since undergone five changes, but in the end a contractor has been selected. The members of the commission for this public procurement were Srdjan Negovanovic, Eudjenija Besu and Zorica Novakov. Ministry of Tourism also helping As a reminder, in October last year, Mayor Simo Salapura signed an agreement on cooperation between the City of Zrenjanin and the Youth Union of the OPENS association. This agreement regulates the guidelines and frameworks for joint action in the process of establishing, developing and further operating the Youth Center in Zrenjanin. Following this agreement, in December last year, a contract on the implementation of the project, i.e. on the allocation of financial resources, was signed at the Ministry of Tourism and Youth. By the terms of the contract, the ministry committed to financing the project up to the amount of the total approved funds in the amount of 54 million dinars, with a deadline for the implementation of the project of 12 months. Opis: Pupinova kuća je podignuta krajem 19. veka, a svedoči o porodičnim vezama slavnog naučnika Mihajla Idvorskog Pupina sa Zrenjaninom, piše na spomen-tabli koja se nalazi na objektu na adresi Kej 2. oktobra broj 9 u Zrenjaninu. Nedugo nakon proglašenja za počasnog građanina tadašnje Velikog Bečkereka, Mihajlo Pupin je 1922. godine kupio kuću i ustupio na korišćenje svojoj sestri Persidi Olćan i njenoj porodici, održavajući do kraja života stalnu vezu sa svojom rodbinom, pisao je Dnevnik. Vidi sve Grad Zrenjanin Crna trava gradnja d.o.o. Crna trava Asing doo Beograd Pupin House Central Banat Youth Center Mihajlo Pupin reconstruction rennovation Your comment Send
content_it:
L’appalto pubblico per i lavori, bandito dall’Amministrazione comunale di Zrenjanin, è stato aggiudicato alle imprese Asing di Belgrado e Crna Trava gradnja di Crna Trava, uniche offerenti. L’intervento riguarda la ristrutturazione, il restauro e la riconversione dell’edificio sito al numero 9 di Kej 2. oktobra a Zrenjanin, noto come Casa Pupin, in un centro giovanile pubblico: il “Centro Giovanile del Banato Centrale Mihajlo Pupin”. La struttura diventerà uno spazio moderno dedicato ai giovani, destinato ad attività libere, al coordinamento delle associazioni giovanili e al sostegno delle organizzazioni della gioventù. Il valore complessivo dei lavori ammonta a 61.317.012 dinari, IVA inclusa.

Il bando, pubblicato tre mesi fa, ha subito cinque modifiche prima della selezione dell’impresa aggiudicataria. La commissione giudicatrice era composta da Srdjan Negovanovic, Eudjenija Besu e Zorica Novakov.

Come riportato da ekapija.com, nell’ottobre dello scorso anno il sindaco Simo Salapura ha firmato un accordo di cooperazione tra il Comune di Zrenjanin e l’Unione Giovanile dell’associazione OPENS, finalizzato a definire le linee guida per la creazione e la gestione del Centro Giovanile. A seguito di tale accordo, nel dicembre scorso è stato stipulato presso il Ministero del Turismo e della Gioventù un contratto per l’attuazione del progetto, con un finanziamento pubblico di 54 milioni di dinari e un termine di esecuzione di 12 mesi.

La Casa Pupin, costruita alla fine del XIX secolo, testimonia i legami familiari del celebre scienziato Mihajlo Idvorski Pupin con Zrenjanin. Divenuto cittadino onorario dell’allora Veliki Bečkerek, Pupin acquistò la casa nel 1922 e la concesse in uso alla sorella Persida Olćan e alla sua famiglia, mantenendo un costante rapporto con i propri parenti fino alla morte.

L’investimento nella ristrutturazione di edifici storici e nella creazione di spazi dedicati ai giovani rappresenta un’opportunità per le imprese italiane specializzate nel restauro architettonico e nella fornitura di servizi per centri giovanili e culturali.

title_en: Shore of Lake Palic getting new facilities – Guesthouses, villas and Adrenaline Park in “Weekend Settlement”
title_it: Nuove strutture turistiche a Palic
content_en: (Photo: Park Palić) The “Weekend Settlement” in Palic will soon get a new look, and the development plan for this area includes additional facilities, guesthouses, villas, catering facilities, and even an “Adrenaline Park .” The draft Detailed Regulation Plan for the “Weekend Settlement” in Palic and part of the “Banja Palić” area along the eastern shore of Lake Palic is being implemented by Park Palic d.o.o. and the Public Company for Road Management, Urban Planning and Housing, in cooperation with other public companies, institutions and plot owners. The client and investor of the project is “Park Palic d.o.o.”, and the developer is the City Administration - Secretariat for Civil Engineering of Subotica, and the responsible urban planner is Petar Andric. The Plan’s boundary covers an area of 43.63 ha, between the Novosadski put Street and the lake, of which the construction area, or rather construction land, covers 39.18 ha, and water areas (reeds and marshes) cover 4.45 ha. The area covered by the Plan can be divided into two urban units: the northern part - which represents the “Weekend Settlement” and the southern part, intended for spa tourism. (Photo: Unsplash/Thomas Le) In the northern part, holiday homes - weekend houses have been built, and in the southern part there are about ten illegally built facilities intended for family housing. These illegal buildings have been recorded as a problem that, as stated in the documentation, “needs to be solved.” In front of the existing “Weekend Settlement” there is a sandy beach, and the basic idea is to return the beach to its “old glory,” by enriching the existing and creating new sports, recreational and catering facilities. A mandatory condition is to improve the water quality in the lake. As stated in the technical documentation, the area for public purposes is 15.79 ha, and the area for other purposes is 27.84 ha. Of the areas for other purposes, holiday homes - cottages occupy 6.5 ha, space for family housing 3 ha, and facilities from the spa tourism category 1.7 ha. The solutions proposed by the Master Plan for the majority of the “Weekend Settlement” complex state that it is unorganized and that a new urban matrix is needed. (Photo: Print Screen/ Google Maps) The projections of this document suggest that this area should develop into a tourist settlement. For the northern part of the “Weekend Settlement,” the reconstruction and conversion of existing facilities into accommodation capacities (guest houses, villas...) with possible catering and entertainment facilities are planned, in order to increase the value of this attractive space above the sandy beach. In block B4, the construction of infrastructure facilities is planned in this part - a “hydroglobe” with a well and a hydrophore house. For the southern part of the area, the construction of more active facilities by the lake is planned: an “Adrenaline Park” and possibly a water ski resort. On the surface of the primary predominant land use, the plan allows the construction of commercial and tourist facilities for business, catering, trade, crafts, health and education and culture. Landscaping, fountains, furniture and urban equipment are compatible with all purposes and can be implemented on all surfaces. Deputy Mayor of Subotica Csilla Goli stated that the development of the “Weekend Settlement” was of great importance for the tourist development of Palic, as well as the development of other parts of that area. The draft development plan for the weekend settlement of Palic is on display for public inspection until November 18 and is available on the website of the Subotica City Administration. Palić JP za upravljanje putevima, urbanističko planiranje i stanovanje Subotica Weekend Settlement Palić Lake Palić Banja Palić City Administration Secretariat for Civil Engineering of Subotica Detailed Regulation Plan Petar Andrić development tourist features Your comment Send
content_it: Il “Weekend Settlement” sul lago di Palic (Serbia) sarà oggetto di una riqualificazione che prevede la realizzazione di nuove strutture turistiche, tra cui guesthouse, ville, servizi di ristorazione e un “Adrenaline Park”. Il piano dettagliato di regolamentazione, redatto dalla società Park Palic d.o.o. in collaborazione con l’azienda pubblica per la gestione stradale, la pianificazione urbanistica e l’edilizia abitativa, interessa un’area di 43,63 ettari lungo la sponda orientale del lago. L’amministrazione comunale di Subotica, attraverso il Segretariato per l’edilizia civile, è l’ente attuatore del progetto, la cui progettazione urbanistica è affidata a Petar Andrić. Il piano distingue due zone: la parte settentrionale, destinata al “Weekend Settlement” con case vacanza, e quella meridionale, riservata al turismo termale, dove sono presenti alcune costruzioni abusive da risolvere. Tra gli obiettivi principali vi sono il ripristino della spiaggia sabbiosa e il miglioramento della qualità delle acque lacustri. Sono previsti interventi di riorganizzazione urbanistica per trasformare l’area in un insediamento turistico strutturato, con la riconversione delle strutture esistenti in capacità ricettive e la costruzione di nuove infrastrutture, tra cui un “idroglobo” nel blocco B4. Nella zona meridionale è pianificata la realizzazione di un parco avventura e, eventualmente, di un impianto per lo sci nautico. Il piano permette anche la costruzione di strutture commerciali e turistiche per ristorazione, commercio, artigianato, servizi sanitari, educativi e culturali. Secondo la vicesindaca di Subotica, Csilla Goli, lo sviluppo del “Weekend Settlement” è fondamentale per la crescita turistica di Palic. Il progetto è consultabile fino al 18 novembre sul sito dell’Amministrazione comunale di Subotica, come riportato da ekapija.com. L’iniziativa presenta opportunità per aziende italiane operanti nei settori delle costruzioni, dell’arredamento per strutture ricettive, delle attrezzature per parchi avventura e dei servizi di ristorazione specializzati nel turismo.

title_en: Legalization of illegal buildings in the region - How will the new regulations affect the real estate market and investors?
title_it: NON PERTINENT
content_en: Illustration (Photo: urfin/shutterstock.com) The process of legalization of illegally constructed buildings is still one of the key issues in the construction sector of the countries of the region. Serbia, Montenegro and Bosnia and Herzegovina are implementing different models and legal solutions with the aim of registering existing construction , providing legal security to owners and encouraging further investments in legal flows. In Serbia, the issue of legalization has been current for more than a decade and represents one of the most extensive administrative processes in the urban planning sector. According to the data of the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure, more than one million requests for legalization have been recorded in the registers of local self-governments, while in recent years intensive work has been done on establishing clearer procedures and digitalizing data. Law on special conditions for recording and registering rights to immovable property actualized the issue of legalization of illegally built buildings in Serbia. The new law was conceived as a continuation of earlier solutions, with the aim of enabling the registration of existing buildings and the registration of owners` rights, but experts warn that the way it was prepared could have numerous negative consequences for citizens and the real estate market. Đorđe Vukotić, a lawyer and consultant in the field of planning, construction and legislation, indicates that the Draft Law did not pass the mandatory public discussion , which in practice means that experts and the general public did not have the opportunity to influence the final text. - The proposal for a new law regulating legalization not only did not pass the mandatory public debate, but during the work on the law, the relevant ministry did not conduct an appropriate consultative process, nor an analysis of the effects in relation to key legal solutions - Vukotić points out. According to him, circumventing the consultative process and control mechanisms leads to the adoption of unenforceable and potentially harmful laws, whereby citizens are left without adequate protection of their rights. The expert further warns that the proposed law changes the rights of users of legalization compared to the current Law from 2015. - The most harmful effect is the degradation of the quality of the rights that are acquired by registration in the cadastre, because an irremovable note is foreseen that publicly presents reservations regarding the object and the rights to it. The paradox is that citizens who have already submitted complete documentation under the previous laws must submit applications again - Vukotić explains. In addition, the new law prescribes too short a preclusion period of 60 days for submitting applications and objections, which puts citizens at risk of permanently losing their right to legalization. Also, the announced "zero tolerance" for new illegal construction, in Vukotić`s opinion, will not stop illegal construction. - The newly proposed law abandoned mass legalization and returns to the system of legalization upon application, which means that in practice we will have neither mass nor rapid legalization. Vukotić recalls that he previously proposed a two-stage model of legalization - first recording of buildings and owners with notes on possible deficiencies, and then removing those notes when citizens obtain the necessary documentation. In his opinion, the proposed law does not recognize this double phase, but introduces a complex procedure in which two state bodies act - the Spatial Planning Agency and the Republic Geodetic Institute - which additionally slows down the process and increases the risk of legal uncertainty. According to Vukotić, the paradox of the current proposal is that the citizens who were the most orderly, the buyers of apartments in buildings with a construction permit, are punished the most by the law. Increased fees, permanent notes and the obligation to re-obtain technical documentation create additional financial and administrative barriers. - In practice, the legalization procedure will cost the citizens several times more than the promised 100 to 1,000 euros, because they will only be able to protect their right to registration in the cadastre through a lawyer, whose tariff for submitting just one urgent application to the RGZ for processing the application is a minimum of 50,000 dinars, considering the high value of the real estate - notes Vukotić How to protect citizens and prevent future illegal construction? When asked about the most effective way to protect the interests of citizens who bought in good faith, and at the same time prevent future illegal construction, Vukotić emphasizes the importance of mass and automated legalization. - I believe that the most effective way to solve the problem of illegal construction would be to implement, in an automated procedure and in the shortest possible time, the most massive legalization of all buildings built by 2015, primarily in urban centers. It is precisely in these centers that professional investors have the greatest interest in continuing illegal construction - explains Vukotić. He adds that the state had to set a higher tariff for the legalization of buildings built after 2015, in order to ensure the payment of the necessary contributions for the development of construction land, because the policy of zero tolerance proclaimed in this way seems frivolous - With the Law on Legalization from 2015, the state determined the public interest in legalizing buildings illegally built from 1945 until then, aware that it was only with the amendments to the Law on Planning and Construction from 2014 that it relaxed the conditions and construction costs to an acceptable level. Vukotić points out that the process of legalization of individual buildings in rural and suburban areas can take longer, because such illegal construction also happens in EU countries, where legalization is usually carried out when the owner wants to sell the building. Number of illegal buildings - statistics or methodology? When asked about the difference between NALED`s data, which records about 2.1 million illegal buildings in Serbia, and the publicly mentioned figure of 4.8 million, Vukotić points out that the key lies in the census methodology. - As a rule, our politicians and the public are fascinated by statistics, and statistics can add and subtract anything. I assume that in these figures, in addition to multi-storey residential buildings and large production plants, there are also adapted attics, garages, sheds and other auxiliary rooms that our citizens built with their own hands - he explains. Vukotić adds that he is not sure that the total number of illegal buildings has doubled in the last few years, and that it is more likely that the difference refers to different criteria for determining the status of buildings. - What I am quite sure of is that the most valuable illegally built residential and commercial spaces in urban centers have doubled. It would be particularly interesting to see how many such buildings have been erected in the protection zones of natural and cultural assets. Only then would we be able to assess how much the new legal solution affects our cities, as well as natural and cultural resources - says Vukotić. Impact on prices and the real estate market Commenting on the possible impact of the new law on the market, lawyer Đorđe Vukotić estimates that the very act of legalization could increase the value of illegally built buildings, but with certain reservations. - I believe that objects that go through the legalization process will certainly gain in price, because the sale of such real estate will become legally indisputable and enforceable in the cadastre. However, their value will still be slightly below the market value, due to the entry in the cadastre indicating that the object is from legalization - Vukotić explains. According to him, the price difference will depend primarily on the available technical documentation on the basis of which the building was built, as well as on the visible quality of the construction. An additional factor that could affect the market value is the announced practice of entering in the cadastre a record of unpaid fees in the amount of the contribution for the development of construction land. - If such a note is applied, it can further reduce the value of the apartments in those buildings, because the legal consequences of such a note are not precisely prescribed - he points out. Speaking about the potential impact of the new registration regime on the market of new construction, Vukotić estimates that the effects could be different depending on the location and type of construction. - When we talk about new construction, we are primarily talking about apartments in urban centers, where prices are already extremely high - even in the suburbs of Belgrade, Novi Sad or Niš. It would not be a surprise if some buyers decide to wait, expecting that the legalization in those locations will temporarily lower the prices of apartments - says Vukotić. However, he adds that no significant changes should be expected in the central city zones, where large investors who build legally dominate. - In the center of Belgrade, illegal buildings are not a competition for serious investors. Therefore, in that segment of the market, we should not expect legalization to affect prices, even in the short term - Vukotić concludes. MONTENEGRO - THE GOAL TO ENABLE THE LEGALIZATION OF THE GREATEST NUMBER OF FACILITIES In August, Montenegro received a new Law on the Legalization of Illegal Buildings, and as previously ordered by the Ministry of Spatial Planning, Urbanism and State Property, the goal is to bring as many illegal buildings into the legal channels as possible, as well as to provide citizens with a fairer and more efficient legal solution than before. The new law, as explained, introduces clear procedures and stricter rules, and for the first time, aerial photogrammetry images are introduced as the basis for the procedure. It is estimated that there are around 120,000 illegal buildings in Montenegro, and when explaining this legal solution, the Ministry pointed out the inefficiency of the previous law, where only 5.5% of the buildings for which requests were submitted were legalized as of 2017. More precisely, out of 61,647 requests, 3,397 decisions on legalization were made. The new law is expected to establish order in the field of spatial planning, because the state, with the help of satellite images and digital procedures, will receive an effective tool for monitoring new construction and preventing illegal construction. Local self-governments are obliged to register all illegal objects on their territory within five months, thus establishing a comprehensive database on the situation on the ground for the first time. According to the new law, owners have until February 14 to register their buildings in the cadastre and submit a request for legalization. If they don`t, they risk demolition (where the cost is borne by themselves) and loss of ownership. An important item of this law is that it will enable the legalization of all buildings, except those located on land planned for infrastructure (roads, schools, hospitals), then if they cross the plot boundaries, or if they are temporary and unstable structures . In some cases, legalization will also be allowed in zones without a planning document, but not in protected parks and areas of special importance. The facility must be visible on a satellite or aerial photogrammetric image of the territory of Montenegro - those that are not visible cannot be legalized, nor can they be included in traffic. The cadastre will ex officio cancel the registration of such objects. Also, the owner must prove the ownership right to the building and the land or initiate court proceedings. For facilities on state or municipal land, local governments publish a call for redemption within 30 days; if the contract is not concluded, the facility becomes state property. All owners of illegal buildings must pay a fee for urban rehabilitation, with 80% going to the municipality and 20% to the state. Although the Ministry stated that one of the goals of this law is to ensure an orderly, safe and transparent real estate market, experts warn that precisely one of its provisions can block this market, which is among the fastest growing in Montenegro. Namely, the Law on Legalization prohibits the sale and lease of illegal buildings, as well as the performance of economic activities in them. The ban applies to buildings without a building permit or those that have been built with the building permit exceeded. The law gives the possibility that in an unlegalized facility intended for economic activity, it can be carried out for a maximum of three years, and that the owners are obliged to legalize such facilities during that period. If they do not do so, economic activity will be prohibited in them. Due to this item, the real estate market could slow down, because notaries are not allowed to deal with illegal objects. Many transactions have already been suspended, which affects buyers and sellers, as well as real estate agencies, which warn of the constitutionality of the traffic ban. The Association of Real Estate Agencies welcomes any initiative aimed at regulating the market and solving the long-standing problem of illegal buildings. According to them, the Law on Legalization is a necessary step towards a more transparent and stable market. - It is important to emphasize that Montenegro started the process of legalization in 2018 through the Law on Spatial Planning and Construction of Facilities. The legal solution at the time did not allow the legalization of buildings that did not meet urban planning parameters, so a very small number of buildings were legalized. Over the years, we have witnessed various attempts to solve this problem, and as an association that actively participated in the creation of the legal framework for our activity, we understand the complexity of this issue - Nataša Grdinić, executive director of CMM Investment Consulting Group , president of the Real Estate Trade Group at the Chamber of Commerce (PKCG) and member of the Association of Real Estate Agencies, said in an interview for eKapija. - However, we must be honest - the success of this law will not depend only on its provisions, but also on the way it is interpreted and implemented - Grdinić added. As she clarified, recent interpretations of certain provisions caused concern and showed that there is a need for additional clarifications and alignment with the real needs of the market. Positive aspects of the law Grdinić points to the positive aspects of this law and welcomes the legislator`s clear intention to regulate the market and ensure confidence in investing in Montenegro. - The aim of the law is to finally solve the problem that has burdened the market for years and creates legal uncertainty. Legalized facilities allow the owners to dispose of their assets without hindrance. Increasing the value of real estate is an inevitable effect that this law will bring. Facilities with proper documentation have a higher market value - she explains. Also, access to financing has been facilitated . Banks more easily approve loans for legalized buildings with complete documentation. In the end, the organized market attracts serious domestic and foreign investors , so this is a great incentive for investing in our country, the eKapija interlocutor notes. A possible blockage of the real estate market - What worries us is the way in which the law is interpreted and applied in practice, as well as the set deadlines in which legalization should be implemented. The provision of Article 33, paragraph 1 of the Traffic Prohibition Law was not sufficiently precise, which led to different interpretations. According to the opinion of the Ministry of Spatial Planning, the ban on traffic includes all illegally built buildings - both before and after the entry into force of the Act. This kind of restrictive measure practically blocks the real estate market - Grdinić points out. According to her, the seriousness of the situation is illustrated by the data of the Chamber of Notaries - in Montenegro, there are between 100 and 150 thousand objects for which a request for legalization has been submitted, but nothing has been done with them. Also, for a large number of objects, the request was not even submitted. - There is a justified concern that the state apparatus is not ready to process such a large number of requests, the cadastre as well as other state bodies in charge of legalizing buildings do not have the capacity to resolve such a large number of cases within the deadlines defined by the law. All illegal facilities as well as facilities without a use permit are currently out of circulation. This means that owners of illegal buildings cannot dispose of their property until they receive a legalization decision, which can take years. Disposition means that these properties cannot be sold, given away, gifted, inherited, pledged, etc. When we talk about publishing, a large space opens up for the creation of a new segment of the gray market - our interlocutor explains. She adds that there are serious doubts that this interpretation of the law is unconstitutional because it restricts the owners` right to dispose of their property. - The legalization process must be more efficient and transparent so that owners can adjust the status of their facilities as soon as possible. The drastic decrease in real estate turnover has a negative impact on the entire economy - from notaries and real estate agencies to the construction sector and local budgets. This is not only a problem of the real estate sector, but an economic problem that affects the entire society - Grdinić points out. She also reminds that the ban on the sale of illegal real estate was in force in the Republic of Serbia for about 7 years and it is more than evident that it did not bring the desired results, so the simplification of the procedures was started. - A few days ago, the Law on special conditions for recording and registering rights to immovable property was adopted, which will enable the majority of owners of illegal buildings to legalize their property. I hope that our decision makers will learn from this example - she states. Impact of the law on investors When asked what the Law on Legalization means for the investors themselves, Grdinić answers that it has a double meaning for them. On the one hand, it brings long-term benefits, but the current interpretation creates short-term challenges. - When we talk about long-term benefits, investors first of all value an organized market, transparency and clear legal frameworks. Legalization contributes to the creation of a stable investment environment and investment security. The purchase of legalized buildings eliminates the risk of future legal problems and enables unhindered use and disposal of real estate. Legalized real estate is easier to sell and has a higher market value, which is crucial for investors planning to resell. Also, banks are more willing to finance the purchase or renovation of legalized buildings, which opens up additional opportunities for investors - our interviewee explains. However, she adds, the current challenges are considerable. - According to the current interpretation of the law, a huge number of buildings are out of business until they are legalized. This drastically reduces the supply on the market and can instantly increase the prices of legal facilities. Investors who are interested in objects in the process of legalization must wait for solutions, which slows down transactions and investment plans until all ambiguities in the interpretation of the law are clarified and until an efficient legalization process is ensured - she says. She points out that the Association for Real Estate Trade strongly supports the implementation of the law and regulation of the market. - We are the ones who actively participated in the creation of the legal framework for our activity and we understand the importance of regulation. However, the method of interpretation and application of the law must be in accordance with the Constitution and the protection of the rights of owners, aimed at solving problems, not at deepening them, followed by an efficient process of legalization so that owners do not have to wait for years for solutions, and balanced between the need for order and the real possibilities of the market - says Grdinić. She adds that a constructive dialogue between state institutions, professional associations and market players is needed. - The law must be enforceable and efficient. The Ministry and the Legalization Directorate must ensure clear and unambiguous guidelines for the application of the law, an efficient and transparent process of legalization, realistic deadlines and adequate support for owners, as well as interpretations that will not block the market and the economy - she said. Message to investors Grdinić states that it is very important to send a message to investors that Montenegro remains an attractive destination for real estate investments . It indicates that the combination of a favorable tax system, a stable currency (euro), membership in NATO and expected accession to the EU makes our country attractive for long-term investments. - Current challenges in the application of the Law on Legalization are temporary. As an association that represents the leading companies in the sector, we will try to work on improving the application of the legal framework and its proper application. Our goal is a market that is regulated, transparent and functional - a market that protects both owners and investors. We invite all interested parties to work together on solutions that will enable the Law on Legalization to fulfill its purpose - to regulate the market - Nataša Grdinić concludes in an interview for eKapija. Legalization of illegal buildings in Republika Srpska: state and challenges The Ministry of Spatial Planning, Construction and Ecology of the RS points out that it does not have precise data on the number of illegally built buildings, because construction control is carried out by inspection authorities. - One year after the passing of the Law on the Legalization of Illegally Built Buildings, we asked local communities for information on the number of illegal buildings. Out of 64 units, only 45 submitted data, of which 26 had no data, while the remaining 19 reported 23,801 illegal facilities. We believe that the actual number is significantly higher, bearing in mind previous estimates that indicated more than 80,000 facilities in the field - the Ministry states. Since the entry into force of the Law on Legalization from 2022, 20,927 requests for legalization have been submitted in 38 local communities, and 10,430 requests have been resolved. According to data from 2023, 7,340 decisions on the legality of buildings were made. The Ministry notes that, due to the lack of legally binding records, it is not possible to accurately assess how many buildings have not yet entered the legalization process. - Free legalization, introduced by the Law from 2022, and a simplified procedure for certain types of facilities contributed to a greater number of submitted requests. The most common reasons for the non-legalization of buildings are incomplete documentation, unresolved property-legal relations, the need to divide plots or the absence of buildings on digital orthophoto plans - the Ministry points out. The legalization procedure, as they explain to us, is based on two principles: the standard procedure for buildings built before July 18, 2018, which includes obtaining documentation and paying prescribed fees, and a simplified "ex lege" procedure for buildings built by the end of 1992 or individual residential buildings up to 400 m² built by the end of 2013, where legality is determined based on evidence of the existence of the building. Remediation of the consequences of illegal construction is not an easy or simple job at all, but rather a challenging and complex process that has been going on for many years. When defining the legal solutions, the legislator, in order to protect the public interest, tried to offer legal solutions that would be sufficiently acceptable and stimulating for investors and owners to massively submit requests for the legalization of their illegally built buildings, and that such objects are introduced into legal flows as soon as possible and that investors dispose of their assets, but at the same time to prevent further illegal construction and that such situations do not become a mass phenomenon in the future - the Ministry of Spatial Planning, Construction and Ecology of the RS states. title_en: Bojan Jevtić, founder and managing director of Avalon Real Estate - Team strength key to success in a challenging year
title_it: Il mercato immobiliare serbo nel 2026
content_en: Bojan Jevtic, founder and managing director of Avalon Real Estate (Photo: Zoran Petrović) The company Avalon Real Estate, recognized as a leader in mediation in commercial real estate in Belgrade, records impressive results thanks to an innovative approach, a dedicated team and strategic planning. Under the leadership of founder and CEO Bojan Jevtić, Avalon excels in the realization of projects in the segments of office spaces, logistics, industrial facilities and hotel investments, combining expertise, quality and sustainability at every stage of business. In an interview for eKapija, Jevtic spoke about current trends in the commercial real estate market in Belgrade and the region, the impact of global economic flows, investment opportunities in 2026, as well as experiences from Expo Real in Munich. He particularly emphasized the importance of the recent sale of the IN hotel, which confirms the return of investors` confidence in the hotel sector of Belgrade and the city`s potential as an attractive investment destination. How would you describe the current trends in the commercial real estate market in Belgrade? - The commercial real estate market in Belgrade is currently in a phase of stable and sustainable growth. The logistics and industrial space sector recorded the greatest dynamics, where the demand still significantly exceeds the supply. In 2025, the rate of available space in this segment remained below 2%, while rents recorded a slight increase, due to higher construction and transportation costs, as well as the growing interest of tenants from the e-commerce and production sectors. The office market is characterized by stable activity and demand, especially for modern, energy efficient spaces in central parts of the city, while the retail sector is in the consolidation phase - with investors` focus on retail parks and local formats in suburban areas. What is the situation on the global market and to what extent do international capital flows, inflation and interest rates influence the events in Serbia? - The global commercial real estate market is undergoing a period of slowdown, primarily due to the prolonged effect of high inflation and higher interest rates, which had a significant impact on financing costs and project valuation. Nevertheless, we see that the market is gradually stabilizing - investors are more cautious, but still active, especially when it comes to high-quality, sustainable projects in good locations. In this context, Serbia is still perceived as an attractive investment market. Despite global challenges, the local economy is showing resilience, and investors recognize Belgrade`s potential as a growing regional center . Where do you see the greatest investment opportunities on the market in 2026? We expect that 2026 will bring market stabilization and gradual growth of investment activities, with the continuation of the trend of more careful, but strategically focused investment. I still see the biggest opportunities in the industrial and logistics sector, while office spaces will be driven by the need for flexible, technologically advanced and sustainable solutions. The hotel sector also stands out as an area with growing investment potential, boosted by the growth of tourist traffic and the arrival of international brands. Overall, 2026 could mark a new phase of market consolidation – investors are becoming increasingly selective and focused on long-term, sustainable projects and stable income streams, while Belgrade is more and more clearly profiled as an excellent destination for investments. Avalon Real Estate was present at Expo Real in Munich. What are the impressions and what are the key trends that, in your opinion, will shape the European real estate market in the coming period? - My impression is that the European real estate industry, after a period of uncertainty, shows signs of stabilization again. While higher interest rates and economic challenges continue to shape the market, there is a renewed willingness to seize new opportunities. The market is showing clear signs of recovery and a more mature approach - with a shift away from speculative transactions towards long-term value, quality and stability. Today, quality and long-term stability are the main priorities, and the market is entering a new phase of deliberate selection, analytical assessment and strategic thinking. At the fair in Munich, the importance of energy transformation of buildings and affordable housing was additionally highlighted, while the use of artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping market analysis, valuation and portfolio optimization. In Munich, a tone of cautious optimism prevailed, with the willingness of market players to respond to challenges, take advantage of opportunities and integrate modern technologies for business improvement. Recently, the sale of the IN hotel was realized, in which Avalon acted as an intermediary. What does this transaction say about current investor interest in the hotel sector in Serbia? - This transaction represents the largest and most significant hotel acquisition in the last few years, which confirms the investors` strong confidence in the further growth of the Belgrade hotel sector and at the same time highlights the city`s attractiveness as a dynamic investment destination with exceptional potential for growth. The total volume of investments in Serbia last year exceeded EUR 300 million, whereby the hotel sector accounted for slightly more than 30% of the total transaction volume. With the growth of investor confidence, the hotel sector is expected to maintain its upward trend in 2026, with attractive rates of return, quality offer and growing demand, which together contributes to a stable inflow of capital and more optimistic prospects for the overall return on investment. The upcoming exhibition EXPO 2027 represents a particularly attractive opportunity for investment, which will create the need for additional hotel facilities. However, it is important to think about sustainable development and plan in advance how these capacities will be used after the end of the event, in order to make the investments sustainable in the long term. Although your company has been on the market for a relatively short time, it has achieved exceptional results, especially in the office space sector, and now in the hotel sector as well. What are the key success factors that enabled you to achieve these results? - As a former basketball player, I like to quote from the American basketball player and coach Phil Jackson: "The strength of a team lies in each of its members, and the strength of each member lies in the team." In our case, people really are the key to success - even though we are a small team, thanks to expertise, commitment and mutual coordination, we achieve great results. I believe that it is precisely this combination of team spirit and individual contribution that is the basis of our success.
